title: Evaluation of the vertical microphysical properties of fog as simulated by Meso-NH during the SOFOG3D experiment
abstract: This study evaluates the representation of fog microphysics in high-resolution simulations from the Meso-NH model using the two-moment LIMA microphysical scheme, based on data from the SOFOG3D field campaign. This campaign combines remote sensing and vertical microphysical observations from a tethered balloon. Two fog events were simulated in order to assess the model's ability to reproduce their life cycle and identify any missing physical processes. title: Regional assessment of atmospheric CO₂, CH₄ and CO concentrations in Southern Brazil using WRF-Chem under present and energy transition scenarios
abstract: Abstract The objective of this study was to evaluate the spatial and temporal distribution of greenhouse gases (CO₂ and CH₄) and the atmospheric pollutant CO in Santa Catarina, Brazil, and to analyze the impacts of energy transition scenarios on their atmospheric concentrations. The methodology was based on the development of a regional emissions inventory, including stationary and mobile road sources, followed by the application of the WRF-Chem atmospheric model (Weather Research) and forecasting with Chemistry. title: Multi-decadal water budget dynamics of the Great Gibe river basin using google earth engine and SWAT
abstract: ABSTRACT Graphical abstract summarizes multi-decadal water budget components, remote sensing data, and annual hydrological trends in Ethiopia's Great Gibe River Basin. Climate change is intensifying pressure on water systems in data-scarce regions where a clear understanding of long-term water budget dynamics is challfenging. This study decodes the temporal and spatial variability of water budget components in Ethiopia's Great Gibe River Basin through multi-decadal analysis. title: A three-branch synergistic feature aggregation network for noise-robust compound fault diagnosis of rotating machinery
abstract: Abstract Reliable compound fault diagnosis of rotating machinery remains challenging because coupled fault components, measurement noise, and operating-condition variations can obscure weak discriminative patterns. To address these challenges, this paper proposes a Three-Branch Synergistic Feature Aggregation Network (TSFA). Three deterministic temporal representations, namely the original waveform, first-order difference, and second-order difference, are constructed to capture complementary waveform morphology, local transient variations, and higher-order temporal changes. title: Design and control of atmospheric water electrolysis systems for green hydrogen in arid environments
abstract: Freshwater scarcity limits green hydrogen production in arid regions like the Middle East and North Africa (MENA), despite high solar potential. This study compares two atmospheric-moisture-based systems: a Direct Air Electrolyzer (DAE) using a hygroscopic H₂SO₄ electrolyte in a porous sponge, and a hybrid dehumidifier-alkaline electrolyzer (DH-AE) that condenses ambient moisture via vapor-compression refrigeration. title: Historical evolution of snowpack capacity to buffer rain-on-snow runoff in a large Columbia River headwaters basin
abstract: Rainfall during the snow season plays an increasingly important role in flood risk as climate warms and extreme events become more frequent. However, a given sized rain-on-snow (ROS) event can yield outcomes ranging from flooding to no runoff, depending partly on the snowpack's antecedent cold content and capillary retention forces. Here, we analyze the seasonal evolution of the snowpack's physical state over a 72-year period to assess long-term changes in its capacity to buffer runoff from liquid water input. title: Climate-driven changes in wind–solar complementarity across California
abstract: Wind–solar complementarity plays an important role in enhancing energy production and reducing variability in renewable energy systems, yet how it responds to future climate change across multiple timescales remains insufficiently understood. This study presents a county-level assessment of wind–solar complementarity across California, explicitly distinguishing resource availability and stability from monthly to intra-day timescales. title: Wound healing in Atlantic spiny dogfish sharks
abstract: Field observations and limited experimental studies indicate that elasmobranchs can repair substantial skin injuries, but the temporal course and cellular composition of wound healing in Atlantic spiny dogfish remain poorly characterized. We conducted an exploratory laboratory study in 20 female Atlantic spiny dogfish (Squalus acanthias) using standardized full-thickness skin wounds monitored by serial photography for 35 days, histological analysis at defined post-injury time points, and pooled single-nucleus RNA sequencing of intact and wounded skin. title: On the Timescales of Atmospheric Adjustments to Contrail Cirrus Formation
abstract: Abstract Condensation trails (contrails) that evolve into contrail cirrus may constitute the largest contribution to aviation's climate impact. However the strength and timescales of the adjustments of the upper atmospheric water budget to contrail formation are poorly known. Thanks to multiple simulations with the ICOLMDZ climate model, the relatively small impact of a large pulse perturbation to ice cloudiness becomes statistically significant. title: Global inequalities in weather forecasts
abstract: Abstract Weather forecasts provide substantial economic value for society, but differences in forecast accuracy across regions can potentially exacerbate existing—and create new—economic inequalities. These differences are particularly important given the role of weather forecasts in helping prevent damage from climate change. In this paper, we provide a global analysis of the accuracy of predictions of temperature and relate our findings to existing economic inequalities. title: Extratropical teleconnections in a multi-model ensemble nudged towards the observed QBO
abstract: The Quasi-Biennial Oscillation (QBO), the dominant mode of interannual variability of monthly-mean zonal winds and temperatures in the equatorial stratosphere, has a significant influence on the circulation in other regions of the stratosphere and troposphere in boreal winter. To better understand these teleconnections, results from twelve models are analysed for three complementary experiments in which the QBO is either internally generated by the models (free-running), nudged towards the observed QBO, or nudged towards the observed climatology. title: Developing Cognitive Imagination through Narrative Visualization in Pre‑Service Primary School Teacher Education
abstract: This study explores how cognitive imagination is developed through narrative visualization in pre‑service primary teacher education. Situated in the course Drawing Materials and Expression, the study examined ϐive pre‑ service primary teachers who constructed self‑narratives and transformed them into multimodal visual stories. A multimodal qualitative case study design was employed, drawing on students’ narrative visualization works, em‑ bedded written texts, visual sequences, material expression, observation notes, and interview data. title: Taste preferences of tiger puffer ( Takifugu rubripes ) to common amino acids and feed attractants
abstract: The taste preferences of fish which directly influence the feeding action are diversified among species. The present study evaluated the taste preference of tiger puffer (Takifugu rubripes) to a number of compounds including an achiral amino acid (glycine), 16 L-amino acids, 15 D-amino acids and seven commonly used feed attractants. A total of 18 intact and healthy tiger puffers (initial body weight 43.33 ± 3.91 g) were randomly separated in nine 100-L tanks (two fish in each tank as one statistical unit). title: Stratospheric Quasi‐Biennial Oscillation Modulates Tropical Cyclone Extreme Rainfall Over East Asia via Intraseasonal Oscillation
abstract: Abstract Tropical cyclone (TC)‐induced extreme precipitation (TCEP) poses heavy risks, yet its seasonal predictability remains limited by insufficient understanding of cross‐scale climatic drivers. Here, we elucidate a stratosphere‐to‐stratosphere coupling pathway where the quasi‐biennial oscillation (QBO) modulates TC activity and subsequent TCEP over the southeastern coast of China, with the second boreal summer intraseasonal oscillation mode (BSISO2) acting as a critical mediator. title: Design and analysis of a two-wheeler chassis using glass fiber reinforced polymer composite materials
abstract: Abstract The increasing demand for lightweight, durable, and energy-efficient vehicles has accelerated the development of advanced composite materials for automotive structural applications. This study investigates the design and structural analysis of a two-wheeler chassis fabricated from Glass Fiber Reinforced Polymer (GFRP) as a lightweight alternative to conventional metallic chassis. title: Evidence for the impact of fire activity on daily variations of IASI mid-tropospheric CO 2 anomalies at 8–11 km over South America: a pyroconvective fingerprint
abstract: Biomass burning is a major, highly variable source of atmospheric CO 2 , but its impact on the free troposphere remains difficult to quantify because of uncertainties in injection heights and transport. In the tropics, intense fires can trigger pyroconvective plumes that loft combustion products to the mid- and upper troposphere. However, most fire emission inventories and global CO 2 inversions still assume simplified vertical distributions of CO 2 emitted by fires. title: Enabling climate change action in cities: A systematic assessment of conditions
abstract: Abstract Progress toward low-carbon, resilient cities remains a complex and evolving challenge. Enabling conditions, which are the institutional, economic, and social factors that shape the pace and depth of climate action, are central to understanding why some cities can advance more rapidly than others towards sustainable development pathways. While abundant technical and social response options exist, increasing the pace and scale at which these solutions are deployed in cities requires a nuanced and place-based understanding of these enabling conditions. title: Wave-to-wire robust control for a point-absorber wave energy converter
abstract: Wave energy converters with linear generator power take-off systems suffer from degraded conversion efficiency due to electrical losses, yet most control strategies treat the power take-off as an ideal force actuator, neglecting generator dynamics and copper losses. This paper presents a wave-to-wire co-design framework that integrates hydrodynamic buoy dynamics with detailed tubular permanent-magnet linear generator dynamics into a unified nonlinear state-space model. title: Wind turbine noise generation and propagation through large-eddy simulation and acoustic analogy: the case of the complete wind turbine
abstract: We perform the acoustic characterization of a model-scale wind turbine, including the tower and a fully reflective ground surface. The study constitutes the natural extension of the research presented in Rismondo et al. ( J. Fluid Mech. , 2025, vol. 1024, p. A33), where the isolated rotor (IR) was analysed. We use large-eddy simulation and acoustic analogy. title: The Asynchronous Evolution of Cold Waves Over China Revealed by 3D Spatiotemporal Tracking
abstract: Abstract Cold waves pose substantial risks to ecosystems, infrastructure, and society. While most studies have examined their station‐level frequency or regional intensity, the joint behaviors in both time and space remain largely unexplored. Here, we apply a three‐dimensional connected‐component labeling algorithm to daily temperature observations across China from 1960 to 2020, reconstructing spatiotemporally contiguous cold events (SCCEs) as independent Event IDs. title: Sustainability in bridge maintenance: a state-of-the-art review, classification framework, and future research roadmap
abstract: Abstract Operating bridges involves significant economic, social, and environmental impacts. Therefore, ensuring the sustainable maintenance of these vital structures throughout their life cycle must be carefully examined. This paper provides an analytical review of 51 manuscripts on sustainable bridge maintenance published in Scopus and Web of Science from 2000 to 2025. The search inquiry covers at least 4 of the 7 key sustainability themes. The novelty of this paper lies in developing an original classification system to evaluate targeted manuscripts: Case Studies and/or Comparative Assessme

title: Impact on the Health of Older Adults Exposed to PM10 and PM2.5 Emitted in a Metropolis with High Sugarcane and Ethanol Production: Scenario Evaluation
abstract: Abstract We conducted a Health Impact Assessment (HIA) of the older adult population (≥ 60 years) exposed to PM 10 and PM 2.5 , whose main emission sources are associated with sugarcane production. First, we characterized the local atmosphere using the PM 2.5 /O 3 ratio, which was 0.15 in 2018 and 0.16 in 2019, with PM 2.5 and O 3 data measured at ground stations and available on the Qualidade do Ar (Qualar) platform. title: Atmospheric dispersion modeling and radiological environmental impact assessment for the potential recommissioning of the Bataan Nuclear Power Plant, Philippines
abstract: To meet rising energy demands and reduce fossil fuel dependence, the Philippines aims to integrate nuclear energy in the energy mix by 2032, including the possible revival of the inactive Bataan Nuclear Power Plant (BNPP), a 621-MWe Westinghouse Pressurized Water Reactor. This work presents an updated radiological and environmental impact assessment (REIA) of estimated atmospheric radionuclide releases during normal operation using recent local meteorological data. The Hybrid Single Particle Lagrangian Integrated Trajectory (HYSPLIT) model was used to simulate long-range transport and depositi

title: Task aggregation as a strategy to optimize Earth System Model workflows in HPC: assessing real scenarios with EC-Earth
abstract: Earth System Models (ESMs) are commonly executed as complex workflows consisting of numerous interdependent tasks that comprise steps such as model and data deployment, simulation, data transfer, and post-processing. Workflows facilitate the execution of long high-resolution configurations by splitting the runtime of the simulation into different tasks, in order to ensure frequent checkpointing and to comply with the restrictions of the large High-Performance Computing (HPC) machines where they are executed. These machines are frequently congested due to their high demand and, therefore, imple

title: Conditional Kriging prediction of ship–ship hydrodynamic responses during non-parallel berthing
abstract: Non-parallel side-by-side ship interaction can generate strongly asymmetric and nonlinear hydrodynamic responses. This study investigates the effects of berthing angle, water depth, and lateral spacing on the surge force, sway force, and yaw moment of a KVLCC2 and an Aframax, and evaluates response-specific Kriging models within three conditional parameter groups: an angle group (CaseA), an angle–depth group (CaseH), and an angle–spacing group (CaseY). An available unsteady RANS–VOF response database with overset meshes was organized into 40 training samples and 10 held-out evaluation samples.
institutions: Jiangsu University of Science and Technology

title: Multi-scale validation of gridded precipitation datasets in Central-West Brazil
abstract: Abstract Accurate precipitation estimates are essential for hydrological modeling, water resource management, agricultural planning, and climate impact assessments, particularly in tropical regions with sparse and uneven observational networks. This study evaluates the performance of twelve gridded precipitation datasets at daily, monthly, and annual scales across Central-West Brazil, using observations from 120 INMET automatic weather stations distributed across the Amazon, Cerrado, Pantanal, and Atlantic Forest biomes. Continuous statistical metrics, including RMSE, MAE, PBIAS, Willmott’s d,
institutions: Instituto Federal de Educação, Ciência e Tecnologia de Mato Grosso

title: COMMUNITY-BASED RIVER CONSERVATION INITIATIVES AND THE USE OF DRONE TECHNOLOGY FOR MONITORING THE MAHAKAM SUB-WATERSHED ECOSYSTEM, EAST KALIMANTAN
abstract: Tropical rivers play an essential role in maintaining biodiversity, providing ecosystem services, and supporting local livelihoods. However, river pollution caused by household waste, market waste, plastic packaging, disposable diapers, organic debris, detergent foam, and riparian degradation accompanied by localized sedimentation has become a major environmental challenge, particularly in Samarinda City, East Kalimantan. title: Climate drivers of airborne pollen variability: 31 years of monitoring in Barcelona (NE Iberian Peninsula)
abstract: Climate change is increasingly modifying airborne pollen dynamics, with key implications for aeroallergen exposure in Mediterranean urban environments. This study analyses 31 years (1994–2024) of aerobiological and meteorological data from Barcelona (NE Iberian Peninsula) to assess long-term trends in pollen concentration, phenology, and their relationships with local climate variables and large-scale atmospheric circulation patterns. Meteorological records show significant warming, including higher autumn and summer maximum temperatures and summer minimum temperatures, together with reduced D

title: Quantifying CO and NO₂ transport fluxes over southeastern Australia: implications from the 2019-2020 Black Summer and multi-year variability
abstract: Abstract The 2019–2020 Black Summer (BS) wildfires provide a representative case for quantifying how extreme biomass burning affects regional pollutant transport. In this study, we combine satellite-derived column concentrations, ground-based observations, flux diagnostics, and forward trajectory analysis to evaluate the cross-boundary transport responses of NO₂ and CO over southeastern Australia. Anhui Institute of Optics and Fine Mechanics

title: Climate change intensifies the temporal persistence of droughts through a shift from seasonal to prolonged drought regimes
abstract: Climate change is altering not only the frequency and magnitude of droughts, but also their temporal structure. In addition to becoming more severe, droughts may persist longer and increasingly extend across consecutive seasons and years. This study investigates changes in the temporal symmetry of global meteorological droughts, defined here as the tendency for droughts to remain confined within a single season or to persist across consecutive seasons, using monthly precipitation and potential evapotranspiration from bias-corrected simulations from the Coupled Model Intercomparison Project Pha

title: Potential Selenium Benefits in Braised European Porcino (Boletus edulis)
abstract: The foraging of macrofungi from forests for local consumption has not changed throughout human history and across cultures. Carpophores of B. edulis were investigated on the occurrence and association of Se, THg and o-Hg, the effects of culinary braising and compounds intake assessment in the light of exposure and risk assessment procedures used in food and environmental toxicology. The porcine carpophores were collected from a forest surrounded with a rural and agricultural landscape, mainly nearby meadows. title: A semisubmersible offshore wind-to-hydrogen system: Effects of hydrogen storage tank size on dynamic stability
abstract: This study explores the integration of high-pressure hydrogen storage tanks into a floating offshore wind-hydrogen production system and assesses the impact of varying storage mass on the platform’s dynamic performance and structural integrity. Fully coupled dynamic simulations reveal that adding hydrogen production and storage capacity can elevate the platform’s center of gravity by up to 3.5 m and extend the natural periods of pitch and roll motions by approximately 13%. title: Irrigation drives dryland productivity gains in Asian endorheic basins
abstract: The ecologically fragile Asian Endorheic Basins (AEB) recently exhibited a pronounced productivity increase despite regional drying—a paradox known as the ‘greening despite drying’ dilemma. To quantify its drivers, we integrated satellite observations with Dynamic Global Vegetation Models (DGVMs) from 2001 to 2023. We show that 25.2% of the AEB experienced significant productivity gains, heavily driven by rapid irrigation expansion (43.2%), while climate change and CO2 fertilization played minor roles. title: Design and Implementation of a Servo Motor-Based Canopy Drive System for a Passenger Boarding Bridge
abstract: A Passenger Boarding Bridge (PBB) provides a safe and convenient connection between the airport terminal and an aircraft, while its canopy serves as a protective component that minimizes the gap between the bridge and the aircraft fuselage during boarding and deboarding operations. Accurate canopy positioning is essential to accommodate different aircraft types and ensure safe passenger access. However, the canopy mechanism in the existing boarding bridge mock-up is manually operated, resulting in limited positioning accuracy, inconsistent operation, and reduced simulation realism. journal: Micronic Journal of Multidisciplinary Electrical and Electronics Engineering

title: A review of numerical and experimental fluid sloshing mitigation techniques in elliptical tanks under dynamic braking conditions
abstract: The problem of liquid sloshing in partially filled tanks is a key safety and structural integrity issue in road transport, aerospace, maritime, and storage applications in industry. The sloshing literature is significantly underdeveloped in comparison to the well-studied canonical rectangular and cylindrical tank geometries, particularly in the case of elliptical cross-section tanks, which are commonly used in road tanker design, and are known for their low centre of gravity and favourable aerodynamic profile. title: Weather extremes in migration dynamics: evidence from the Philippines
abstract: This study examines the relationship between extreme weather events and internal migration in the Philippines using a migration gravity framework that combines census data with high-resolution climatic indicators. The results show that extreme precipitation events exert a modest but consistent positive effect on outmigration, while temperature extremes produce mixed and largely insignificant effects. title: Aviation-induced contrail forcing in the near term: Ensemble projections and seasonal hotspots for climate policy
abstract: Abstract Abstract Aviation-induced contrail cirrus is the dominant non-CO₂ climate forcer from aviation, yet ensemble-constrained projections for the policy-relevant 2024-2035 window remain absent from the peer-reviewed literature. Using CESM2/CAM6 with a 10-member ensemble, contrail effective radiative forcing (ERF) is projected under two aviation growth scenarios: a primary 3% annual growth trajectory consistent with ICAO near-term forecasts, and an upper-bound 9% sensitivity scenario. title: Process-based seasonal crop yield forecasting for early warning in Sub-Saharan Africa
abstract: Abstract Seasonal crop yield forecasts can support early warning and short-term adaptation in Sub-Saharan Africa (SSA), where rainfed agriculture dominates, but systematic multi-crop, multi-region evaluations remain scarce. Here, we develop and evaluate a forecasting system in which bias-corrected, downscaled SEAS5 forecasts drive the LPJmL crop model. title: Institutional Memory and Long-Run Economic Resilience through Learning from Recurrent Shocks
abstract: Economic resilience is often assessed through an economy’s immediate response to a discrete crisis, such as the speed of recovery or the extent of output loss. This event-based perspective provides limited insight into why some economies develop durable adaptive capacity across repeated disruptions while others remain vulnerable. This conceptual paper reconceptualizes economic resilience as a long-run institutional process shaped by institutional memory and learning from recurrent shocks. Drawing on institutional economics, historical institutionalism, and economic history, the framework expla

title: Tephra fall probabilistic hazard maps for VEI 3 and VEI 4 eruptions at Mt. Garibaldi (Nch’kay’) volcano, British Columbia, Canada
abstract: Abstract Following explosive volcanic eruptions, hazard from tephra fall can be widespread. Based on the geological record of past eruptions and risk to population and infrastructure, Mt. Garibaldi volcano ( Nch’ k ay’ ) in British Columbia has been assigned the highest threat ranking of any Canadian volcano. However, until this contribution no hazard map exists for the volcano. In our study, we formed a government-university partnership and modelled tephra dispersion for Volcanic Explosivity Index (VEI) 3 and VEI 4 scenarios for Mt. Garibaldi to produce probabilistic tephra fall hazard maps.

title: Linkage in the Diversity of Atmospheric Rivers: A Global Perspective on Multi‐Framework Classification
abstract: Abstract Atmospheric rivers (ARs) are essential yet hazardous components of the global water cycle. Despite the development of multiple classification frameworks, their interconnections remain unexplored. Here, we present the first global quantification of the statistical linkages among AR classifications based on oscillation frequency, moisture‐wind contributions, and association with extratropical cyclones. institutions: Qingdao National Laboratory for Marine Science and Technology

title: Review of Simulation Modeling Approaches in Water Resources Management
abstract: Over the past few decades, numerous computer simulation models have been developed to simulate various problems in water resources engineering, offering an alternative to costly and time-consuming physical models. This paper reviews research efforts related to simulation models and their applications, focusing on scientific research where these models have been implemented. The review analyzes the most important hydrological and hydraulic simulation software used in scientific research over recent decades. title: Digital Port Exposure in China's Maritime Connectivity
abstract: ABSTRACT China's maritime infrastructure expansion is usually analyzed through finance, ownership, location, and dual‐use potential. This article shifts attention to the digital systems through which ports now operate. It develops the concept of digital port exposure to describe how foreign‐linked digital systems become embedded in port operations, data environments, vendor relationships, and oversight structures. title: Skin friction mobilisation in rock-socketed piles: A coupled experimental and 3D finite element study across a wide UCS range
abstract: Rock-socketed piles are widely used in heavy bridge and high-rise construction whenever competent rock is encountered at shallow depths. The reliable estimation of skin friction along the socket is, however, still an open problem in geotechnical engineering, particularly when the rock is weak, fractured, or chemically altered. This study presents a coupled experimental and numerical investigation of the load-transfer behaviour of socketed model piles. title: Grand challenge in microbiome data science: recovering the microbiome as a system
abstract: The microbiome has never been only a census of organisms. In its original ecological formula4on, the term described a microbial community embedded in a defined habitat, with its own physicochemical condi4ons and "theatre of ac4vity" [1; 2]. That original framing is useful now because it reminds us that microbes do not act as isolated names on a taxonomic list. title: Attribution and projection of runoff variability in a subtropical monsoon basin under changing environments
abstract: Study region The Pearl River Basin is a humid subtropical monsoon basin in southern China and an important water source for South China, including the Pearl River Delta and Hong Kong. Its abundant precipitation, high vegetation coverage, and strong seasonal variability make it a representative basin for examining runoff responses to climate and land-surface changes in humid monsoon regions. Study focus This study applies the Budyko–Porporato–Guswa coupling framework to investigate historical runoff variability during 1990–2020 and to project future runoff responses during 2021–2060. title: No genuinely green wind power without effective engineering policies
abstract: Wind energy is widely regarded as a sustainable and low-carbon source of electricity. However, the assumption that wind power projects produce negligible or zero greenhouse gas emissions oversimplifies the complexities inherent in their life cycle. To investigate the carbon intensity reliably, we propose a probabilistic life cycle analysis framework that systematically accounts for variability in material inputs, energy consumption, and operational performance. title: Attribution estimates for similar extremes are robust across event definitions
abstract: Abstract Event attribution studies assess whether and to what extent human-induced climate change has altered the likelihood or severity of extreme weather events. In recent years, studies have become routine, particularly for heatwaves in many regions, and for heavy rainfall in parts of Asia and Europe. As this body of research grows, a key question emerges: when does a new attribution study add scientific or societal value? title: Drivers of topography in fold-thrust belts: a perspective from central Nepal
abstract: The roles of climate and tectonics in the evolution of mountainous landscapes over geological time are often assessed via continuum models that balance the forces in mechanical wedges with the assumption of pervasive small-scale faulting accommodating deformation. In contrast, observations from mountain ranges indicate an evolution of large-offset faults and paleoclimate. Here we ask the question, can observed faulting and paleoclimate histories replicate the characteristics of Himalayan topography? title: Experimental and numerical study on the compressive behavior of 3D-printed bionic sandwich plates
abstract: Biological structures in nature often achieve an exceptional combination of low weight, high strength, and efficient energy absorption through synergistic geometric design, demonstrating significant potential for protective and energy-absorbing applications. In this study, eight types of bionic sandwich plates are fabricated and compared, and in-plane quasi-static compression tests combined with finite element analysis are performed under identical geometric and material conditions. title: Projections of hydrological changes and riverflow extremes using TerM land surface model in the Limpopo River Basin, South Africa
abstract: Abstract Increasingly frequent hydroclimatic extremes in South Africa necessitate a robust understanding of how changing climate drivers will influence regional water balance. This study evaluates the impacts of climate change on hydrological extremes within the Limpopo River Basin, a region historically vulnerable to catastrophic flooding and prolonged droughts. The INM RAS-MSU (Terrestrial Model; TerM) Land Surface Model was used to project river flow from 2020 to 2100. title: A critical examination of the tourism climate index landscape
abstract: Abstract Tourism climate indices have become valuable tools for using raw meteorological data in quantifying and classifying the climatic suitability of a destination for tourism, and to determine the seasonality of optimal conditions to maximise the tourist experience. The initial Tourism Climate Index (TCI) was developed and applied globally in the mid-1980s, gaining renewed interest from the 2000s, when researchers began applying this index to individual countries, and later developed a range of adapted and specialised indices. title: Virtual sensing for strain estimation in wind turbine support structures based on a biaxial accelerometer
abstract: This paper introduces a novel model-based approach for virtual sensing of wind turbine support structures for full-field strain estimation using a single biaxial, DC-capable accelerometer and a sufficiently accurate structural model. It enables displacement and strain estimation in the quasi-static frequency band, which accounts for a large proportion of accumulated fatigue damage in offshore wind turbine support structures while saving costs by relying solely on accelerations from a single accelerometer as input. title: Technical note: HydroModPy (v1.0) – a Python toolbox for deploying catchment-scale shallow groundwater models
abstract: Despite the widespread use of physically based groundwater models, their deployment at the catchment scale remains challenging and time-consuming. HydroModPy was developed to address this gap by enabling automated and streamlined multi-site development of hydrogeological models at the catchment scale. This open-source Python toolbox facilitates the construction, execution, calibration, and analysis of unconfined shallow groundwater models. title: Sounding of the deforming solid earth surface: new opportunities for spaceborne Differential SAR Interferometry techniques to detect and monitor displacements affecting the ground and the built-up environment
abstract: We discuss in this work, through the analysis of four selected case studies, some new opportunities for the detection and monitoring of displacements affecting the ground surface and the built-up environment, through Differential SAR Interferometry (DInSAR) techniques. This is done by exploiting the data acquired by currently operating SAR constellations, such as SAOCOM-1 (providing L-band data), Sentinel-1 (providing C-band data), and COSMO-SkyMed (providing X-band data), and by also envisaging those that will be soon available through the forthcoming missions, as for the case of the NIMBUS S

title: Integrated geophysical and hydrogeochemical characterization of a fractured limestone aquifer in new Tuna El Gabel village, West El-Minia, Egypt
abstract: Abstract Groundwater is a vital component of water supply in arid regions, such as West El-Minia Governorate, Egypt, where water scarcity is projected to worsen, with per capita water supply expected to drop below 500 m 3 by 2025. In response, Egypt’s One and a Half Million Feddan (≈630,000 hectares) project aims to reclaim the Western Desert and develop new communities, aligning with the country’s Vision 2030 for sustainable development. title: Toward freight mobility-as-a-service through digital freight platforms and multimodal operations
abstract: Freight Mobility-as-a-Service (FMaaS) has been proposed as an open platform integrating scheduled and on-demand freight services. However, its conceptual boundaries, governance requirements, operational capabilities, and performance implications remain unclear because most relevant knowledge is dispersed across adjacent research streams. This study systematically reviews 69 publications from Scopus and Web of Science published between January 2015 and June 2026. title: Wavelet-based image preprocessing for enhancing trajectory estimation in monocular ORB-SLAM3
abstract: This paper examines whether classical wavelet-based image preprocessing can improve the accuracy of camera-based simultaneous localisation and mapping (SLAM). In such systems, a moving camera estimates its own trajectory by repeatedly recognising visual structures in consecutive images. The quality of these images therefore, has a direct influence on the stability of localisation, especially when the scene contains noise, weak texture, uneven illumination, or rapidly changing visual details. title: Revolutionising workplace safety in construction: the impact of IoT-integrated smart wearable systems
abstract: Purpose This study aims to evaluate the effectiveness of a smart wearable system in enhancing workplace safety, compliance and operational efficiency in construction projects, particularly focusing on reducing injuries, improving personal protective equipment (PPE) compliance and optimising emergency response times. Design/methodology/approach A smart wearable system comprising head and hand protection units was implemented at United Builders, Panvel. title: Experimental and numerical analysis of liquid sloshing within tank subjected to pitching motion
abstract: Liquid sloshing in partially filled tanks can generate large free surface oscillations, especially under pitch excitation. While extensive research has addressed sloshing in rigid containers, few studies focus on sloshing within flexible tanks or pure pitch-induced sloshing. This work presents a combined experimental and numerical investigation of sloshing dynamics in rigid and flexible tanks subjected to controlled pitch excitation. title: GPR-derived ice thickness of the temperate Hintereisferner glacier (Austrian Alps): evaluation of thickness models
abstract: Abstract. Alpine glaciers are retreating rapidly and have a potential for near complete ice loss at the end of the 21st century thus accurate glacier evolution models are crucial for predicting the magnitude and rate of future glacier changes. Without reliable ice thickness assessments, such models lack credibility and cannot be validated, thus here we evaluate several ice thickness models and present new ground-penetrating radar (GPR) ice-thickness measurements of the Hintereisferner – a temperate glacier located in the Ötztal Alps, Austria, which despite of being one of the WGMS reference g

title: Impacts of Mediterranean snow droughts on mountain socio-ecohydrology
abstract: Snow droughts, defined as periods with below-normal Snow Water Equivalent, have recently received substantial attention as an emerging hazard in a warming world, but their impacts are still poorly understood. Here, we shed light on these impacts across the socio-ecohydrologic spectrum, by leveraging heterogeneous data sources from 38 catchments in Italy: 13 years of snow and runoff data, remote-sensing and in-situ measurements of Gross Primary Production, an inventory of emergency water restrictions obtained via a web-scraping tool and direct consultation of national to local regulations, and

title: Impact of circumsolar irradiance and aerosol optical depth on CAMS surface solar irradiance estimates
abstract: The global horizontal irradiance is a main variable in the integration of solar energy systems in electricity grids, and in climate and weather studies. The physical model McClear is the clear-sky module for the all-sky irradiance retrievals from the CAMS Radiation Service. title: Divergence between physical and emotional heat resilience in Chinese cities
abstract: Under increasingly frequent urban heatwaves, public emotional responses do not always align with levels of physical heat exposure, but the relationship between the two remains unclear. Here, using social media and meteorological data, we quantify the mismatch between physical heat exposure and public emotional responses from 2010 to 2024 in China, identify its drivers and project this relationship under different shared socioeconomic pathways. title: Numerical and Experimental Characterization of an Aerodynamically Redesigned Disc in a DN350 Double-Eccentric Butterfly Valve in Terms of Flow Coefficient, Pressure Loss and Hydrodynamic Disc Load
abstract: Flow control in pressurized water-transmission and irrigation lines relies on large-diameter butterfly valves, whose disc governs both the line pressure loss and the actuation load. This study compares the conventional disc of a DN350 double-flanged double-eccentric butterfly valve with an aerodynamically redesigned disc using a dual-track approach. title: Anti-floating stability study of working shafts in pipeline tunnels within water-rich soft soil strata
abstract: Abstract Ensuring the anti-floating stability of pipe-tunnel working shafts adjacent to rivers in water-rich soft soil strata is a critical challenge throughout both the construction and long-term operation periods. Current research primarily focuses on conventional anti-floating measures for general underground structures, overlooking the potential of utilizing the soil-cement mass from base pressure grouting as a structural counterweight, particularly for deep circular shafts subjected to fluctuating groundwater levels. title: Multi-USVs Collaborative Water Pollution Traceability and Source Localization Using an Improved Wolf Pack Algorithm
abstract: With the increasing frequency of water pollution incidents due to urbanization and industrialization, this paper proposes an Improved Wolf Pack Algorithm (IWPA) for coordinating multiple Unmanned Surface Vessels (USVs) to achieve rapid river pollution traceability. The IWPA incorporates a dynamic step adjustment mechanism and a dynamic population adjustment strategy to overcome the limitations of the fixed step factor and random repositioning in the standard Wolf Pack Algorithm (WPA). title: Blue Rings reveal thermal thresholds of wood formation in Low Arctic tundra shrubs
abstract: Abstract Low Arctic tundra shrubs experience short growing seasons, prolonged cool conditions, and episodic cold extremes, but the effects of these events on wood tissue formation remain poorly understood. Here we identify thermal thresholds associated with lignification processes in two dominant shrub taxa ( Alnus alnobetula and Salix spp.) along a 68–69°N transect in northwestern Canada. title: From discovery to extinction? Phylogeography and niche modelling of a newly described dragonfly
abstract: The preservation of genetic diversity is a central goal in conservation. General theoretical frameworks such as the central–marginal hypothesis (CMH) often inform conservation strategies, but species with specialized habitat requirements or restricted distributions may not fit this model, hampering the delimitation of conservation units. We studied Onychogomphus cazuma, a recently described dragonfly endemic to Spain and restricted to thermal springs, to define a conservation framework. title: Divergent metal bioaccumulation and toxicity responses under metal-antibiotic co-exposure are associated with gut microbiota shifts in Eisenia fetida
abstract: Combined metal and antibiotic pollution (CMAP) is increasingly prevalent in agricultural soils, yet its joint toxicity to soil invertebrates remains mechanistically unclear. Using Eisenia fetida as a model organism, we examined associations among gut microbial-community shifts, metal body burden, and toxicological responses under Cd-ciprofloxacin (Cd-CIP) and Pb-norfloxacin (Pb-NOR) co-exposure. title: Combining branching processes and Allee effects into an integral projection model to assess invasion risk
abstract: Invasive species threaten both ecological systems and economies. Successful establishment is governed partly by demographic stochasticity, where random individual-level variation can significantly influence invasion dynamics. A critical factor is the Allee effect, which describes reduced population growth at low densities, potentially serving as a barrier to persistence. Size-dependent growth and survival further shape outcomes based on the size distribution of individuals within the population. title: Three-dimensional groundwater flow modelling of the Lower Mahanadi River Basin, Nayagarh, Odisha, India Using MODFLOW-GMS–NWT
abstract: Groundwater is the primary source of water for agricultural and domestic use in the lower part of the Mahanadi River Basin, particularly in Nayagarh district, Odisha. Increasing groundwater abstraction, coupled with spatial variability in recharge and changing rainfall patterns, has intensified pressure on aquifer systems, highlighting the need for scientifically robust groundwater assessment tools. title: Assessment and Rehabilitation of Corrosion Under Pipe Supports (Cups): Development And Validation Of A Structured Integrity Decision Model
abstract: Corrosion Under Pipe Support (CUPS) poses a significant threat to the integrity of offshore piping systems primarily due to harsh environmental conditions. This study investigates CUPS in offshore platforms, focusing on a comprehensive approach that includes inspection, degradation analysis, rehabilitation, and preventive strategies. An 8-inch diameter process piping was thoroughly inspected, revealing extensive wall thickness loss with the remaining thickness falling below critical thresholds. abstract: Reliable assessment of liquefaction hazard, particularly in the context of groundwater fluctuations associated with hydroclimatic changes and variability between liquefaction assessment methods, necessitates supplementary data and advanced site characterization methods. To understand liquefaction hazard and its relation to nonstationary groundwater levels in Napier, Hawke's Bay, New Zealand, a two‐part field testing campaign was conducted at three sites during two distinct seasons, dry (November 2023) and wet (June 2024). title: Seasonal shifts in regional and local controls on ambient isoprene in a semi-arid African savanna
abstract: Abstract A key challenge in semiarid savannas is determining whether ambient isoprene directly traces local biogenic emissions or represents an integrated signal shaped by chemistry and atmospheric dynamics. Here we use hourly measurements of isoprene, methyl vinyl ketone, and methacrolein from August to December 2024 at a savanna site near the Okavango Delta, Botswana, spanning dry to early wet seasons. title: Bioinspired topology-physical-field co-driven design of multi-morphology TPMS lattices for load-bearing and thermal insulation
abstract: The trade-off between load-bearing capacity and thermal insulation limits lightweight multifunctional structures requiring both mechanical support and thermal protection. Inspired by the three-layer architecture of pomelo peel, this study proposes a bioinspired topology-physical-field co-driven (BT-PF) strategy for designing Ti-6Al-4 V heterogeneous triply periodic minimal surface (TPMS) lattices. title: Tumor Exposomics: A New Paradigm for Individualized Continuous Exposure Monitoring
abstract: Exposomics provides a systems-level framework to characterize the environmental exposures experienced across the life course and their biological consequences, offering critical insights into tumor initiation and precision prevention. Advances in sensing technologies, intelligent materials, and data science now enable continuous acquisition of external exposures alongside endogenous molecular and phenotypic responses. title: Performance optimization of a hydrokinetic hybrid Gorlov-Savonius turbine using surrogate model
abstract: The main objective of this investigation is to optimize the performance of a hydrokinetic Hybrid Gorlov-Savonius (HGS) turbine using surrogate-based modeling. A nested configuration of the HGS hydrokinetic turbine is chosen as the base design considered for optimization. The general process of the investigation starts with an experimental evaluation of an HGS reference design performance in an open channel. title: A review of damage types, stress concentration and fatigue effects in evaluating the residual load-carrying capacity of defective steel girders in railway bridges
abstract: Steel girders of ageing railway bridges deteriorate through corrosion, perforation, loose fasteners and local deformation; in Vietnam, 465 of 1,862 railway bridges are classified as vulnerable and their residual capacity must be re-evaluated. Inspection practice rates such defects by visual condition and area loss, whereas most act through local stress concentration, which governs fatigue life and is invisible to global measurements; this gap has not been quantified. title: Spatiotemporal Evolution of Mesoscale Convective Systems (MCSs) and Rainfall Over Citarum River Basin, West Java
abstract: Mesoscale convective systems (MCSs) are major contributors to extreme rainfall in tropical regions, yet their lifecycle-dependent rainfall characteristics over the Indonesian Maritime Continent remain poorly documented. This study investigates the spatiotemporal evolution of MCSs and associated rainfall over the Citarum River Basin, West Java. We focused on the rainy seasons of 2013–2023, based on hourly infrared satellite data and IMERG precipitation. abstract: This study proposes a novel efficient framework for robust topology optimization of fully coupled exterior vibro-acoustic systems with hybrid random-interval uncertainties, utilizing the finite element method-boundary element method. For hybrid uncertainty quantification, the polynomial chaos-Chebyshev interval (PCCI) method has been widely adopted. title: A physics-informed spatiotemporal downscaling model for kilometer-scale hourly humid heat stress indices
abstract: High-resolution humid heat stress indices, characterizing the interactive physiological effects of temperature and humidity, are vital for precision heat-health assessment and climate adaptation. However, existing coarse-resolution datasets smooth fine-scale spatial heterogeneity and may therefore underestimated localized heat extremes. title: Projected Spatial Asymmetry of Daytime and Nighttime Temperature Extremes in the Middle East under CMIP6 Warming
abstract: The Middle East is one of the world’s most prominent climate-change hotspots, where future warming is expected to intensify both daytime and nighttime temperature extremes in spatially heterogeneous patterns. This study investigates projected asymmetry between daytime and nighttime thermal extremes across the Middle East using four temperature-extreme indices from the Expert Team on Climate Change Detection and Indices (ETCCDI): TX90p, TN90p, TXx, and TNx, derived from Stacking-EML-refined CMIP6 projections based on six global climate models for three future periods under SSP1-2.6, SSP2-4.5, a

abstract: Engineering ballistic materials development, optimization and improvement are primarily backed by scientific, experimental and mathematical theories and findings. This has led to the development of numerical strategies that are widely considered to effectively yield cost-effective and rapid materials development, and optimization for continuous improvement of existing materials. title: White light reduces flight height of birds in low‐density migration corridor
abstract: Abstract Artificial light at night (ALAN) has been shown to influence the behavior of migratory birds, yet how different light spectra modulate these effects remains unclear. We conducted a field experiment for 31 nights at a remote site in northern Colorado, USA, using 2 800‐W light‐emitting diode (LED) floodlights with white, red, amber, and blue lighting treatments during fall migration in 2023 and 2024. title: Hybrid TSA-TLBO optimization of an EF2 resonant DC-DC converter for energy-efficient fuel cell electric vehicles with reduced battery dependency
abstract: The fuel cell electric vehicles (FCEVs) with a lower battery dependency have a big problem in terms of the stability of voltage, high dynamic response and low torque ripple under different load conditions. title: Measuring cloud optical depth with a balloonborne microlidar operated from the stratosphere
abstract: The Balloonborne Cloud Observing micrOLidar (BeCOOL) has been developed to be operated onboard a stratospheric balloon in order to monitor the atmosphere below 20 km, more particularly thin ice clouds. This backscatter lidar operating at 802 nm was designed to maintain a high level of performance while keeping its mass below 6 kg and limiting its power consumption to 4 W on average. title: Scenario-based construction pathways for a “good urban area” under Nansha’s future urban framework, Guangdong, China
abstract: Introduction Rapid peri-urban expansion poses significant challenges, including spatial inequality, ecological degradation, and mismatches between land development and public-service provision. Addressing these issues requires integrated planning approaches that balance multiple sustainability dimensions. This study aims to evaluate alternative pathways for constructing a “good urban area” in Nansha District, Guangzhou, by systematically comparing scenarios that prioritize equity, growth, environmental protection, or maintain current trends. title: Experimental investigation of sandy soil stabilization via microbially induced calcite precipitation using spent coffee grounds
abstract: ABSTRACT Microbially induced calcite precipitation (MICP) is a sustainable bio-mediated technique for soil stabilization, yet improving its efficiency while incorporating waste-derived materials remains challenging. This study evaluates spent coffee grounds (SCG), a lignocellulosic waste, as a supplementary material for enhancing MICP-treated sandy soils. title: Architecture-informed O&M modelling of modular X-Rotor configurations for offshore wind: a two- and three-module comparison
abstract: Offshore wind farms located further from shore face increasing operations and maintenance (O&M) challenges because access becomes more weather-restricted and vessel logistics become more complex. This study evaluates how extending the established two-module X-Rotor configuration to a three-module architecture affects O&M performance while maintaining an approximately constant turbine rating of 5 MW. title: Atmospheric drying is a primary driver of past and future fire weather trends across the Western United States
abstract: Abstract There has been evidence of increasing fire activity in the United States since approximately the 1980s, now estimated to cause tens to hundreds of billions of dollars of damage per year. Weather is one of the key drivers of fire activity, with hot, dry, and windy weather commonly associated with high-risk conditions. title: A refined phylochronology of the second plague pandemic in Western Eurasia
abstract: The origin and spread of consecutive outbreaks of the second plague pandemic in Europe (14th to 18th c.) are still poorly understood, although over one hundred ancient Yersinia pestis genomes and a vast corpus of documentary data have been collected. For most ancient genomes, radiocarbon (RC) dates regularly spanning more than 100 y are the only temporal information. The necessity of modifying grouting mortars to increase the strength of the cement stone for intervals in permafrost formations is justified. abstract: Abstract We propose a new temporal merging method for seamless climate forecast information of climate extremes. In order to construct stable and seamless climate forecast information for user-oriented climate extremes, ensemble members are pooled across available start dates using relative weights, for a target season. title: Wildfire synchronicity across European regions is favored by specific weather regimes
abstract: Abstract Synchronous wildfires (wildfires occurring in multiple locations within a week) pose challenges to coordinated firefighting efforts between European countries. Despite their potentially severe impacts, their occurrence and relationship with predictable atmospheric circulation patterns are poorly understood. Studies have highlighted that climate change poses a significant threat to rangeland productivity and proposed stratospheric aerosol injection (SAI)–a geoengineering strategy–as a means to offset temperature-related impacts. In this study, the effect of ultrasonic nanocrystal surface modification (UNSM) treatment load on the microstructural evolution, mechanical properties, tribological behavior, corrosion resistance and fatigue performance of Al7075-T6 alloy was systematically investigated. title: Adaptive Spatial Systems: Evaluating the Performance of Flexible and Reconfigurable Design Strategies in Contemporary Urban Architecture
abstract: Contemporary urban architecture is increasingly challenged by rapid socio-economic change, climate uncertainty, and evolving patterns of space use, exposing the limitations of static, single function buildings. Adaptive spatial systems characterized by flexibility, reconfigurability, and responsiveness have emerged as a critical architectural strategy for addressing space underutilization and improving long-term building performance. abstract: Of the ~1,100 mitochondrial proteins, only a handful like PINK1 and ATFS-1 are known to stabilize and relocalize upon collapse of the proton motive force (PMF) to execute signaling roles. title: Modelling choices can outweigh climate variability in wind resource assessment
abstract: Abstract Wind power is an important source of renewable energy that is critical for achieving net-zero. To inform planning and policy, wind power modelling tools are frequently used to estimate wind power potential both in the present day and in the future, accounting for changing climate conditions and changes in turbine distribution and efficiency. abstract: : Optimizing irrigation in orchards is increasingly challenged by climatic variability, water scarcity, and structural heterogeneity, requiring indicators that robustly link canopy architecture with transpiration and energy exchange processes. title: From state estimation to active intelligence: safety-aware battery management for electric vehicles
abstract: Battery management systems (BMSs) are increasingly required to convert incomplete electrical and thermal measurements into safe control actions rather than merely report battery states. This Mini Review focuses on two deployment questions that connect electrochemistry with control: how electrochemical states can be made observable with affordable diagnostics, and how charging, thermal, balancing, and health objectives can be arbitrated when their constraints conflict. abstract: This study challenges the prevailing assumption in the International Relations (IR) literature that simulations constitute a single, uniform category, and argues instead that their function is determined by the institutional actor that designs and conducts them. title: RPA-LSTM: Reversible normalization and prediction-assisted LSTM for aero-engine intake-system ECU anomaly detection
abstract: Reliable anomaly detection in aero-engine monitoring systems is critical for flight safety, maintenance planning, and operational reliability under variable operating conditions. For turbocharged aviation piston engines, intake-system faults induced by turbocharger wastegate actuator degradation frequently occur during takeoff, climb and other high-load phases, creating an urgent demand for robust time-series diagnosis methods. title: Data-Quality and Single-Source-Of-Truth Frameworks for Inter Agency Reporting: A Review
abstract: Inter-agency reporting, the routine exchange of administrative data among public bodies to produce shared statistics, dashboards, and compliance returns, depends on the assumption that a figure reported by one agency will mean the same thing when consumed by another. In practice, that assumption is fragile. Divergent definitions, duplicated master records, and the absence of an authoritative reference source produce reconciliation disputes, delayed reporting cycles, and eroded institutional trust. title: Fault ride-through and grid disturbance mitigation for the stability of grid-connected floating offshore wind energy conversion systems
abstract: Ensuring the stability of grid-connected floating offshore wind turbines (FOWTs) under grid disturbances, such as voltage sags, frequency deviations, and fault ride-through (FRT) events, is challenging, particularly when electrical measurements are transmitted over long-distance submarine cables, which can significantly degrade measurement accuracy. title: Root-Cause and Thematic Analysis for Major Incident Management: A Review
abstract: Major incidents, large-scale disruptions to critical digital services, impose disproportionate costs on organisations and the publics they serve, and their aftermath is where much of the potential value of incident management is either realised or lost. This review synthesises two analytical traditions that shape how organisations make sense of such events: root-cause analysis (RCA), rooted in quality engineering and safety science, and thematic or qualitative analysis, rooted in interpretive social science. journal: INTERNATIONAL JOURNAL OF SOCIAL SCIENCES AND MANAGEMENT RESEARCH

title: Post-fire axial impact behavior of columns with hollow section
abstract: Abstract The objective of this work is the study of the dynamic response of fire-affected hollow steel stub columns subjected to axial impact loadings. Although this issue is of great importance for structural safety against multiple hazards, it has not been adequately considered previously. Dynamic FE models of fire-affected columns subjected to axial impact loading were generated using the ABAQUS/Explicit software package. Greece has many islands of various size, with more than two hundred of them being inhabited. To this end, a noteworthy number of remote Greek islands suffer from water stress. title: Scaling urban land governance in India: the NAKSHA Programme as a platform for governance innovation for sustainable cities
abstract: Introduction Urban land governance in India is historically constrained by the lack of comprehensive, legally recognised, and spatially accurate land and property records. This structural deficit significantly impedes municipal finance, precision urban planning, disaster management, infrastructure development, and macroeconomic stability. To address this systemic gap, the Department of Land Resources, Government of India, initiated the NAKSHA (NAtional geospatial Knowledge-based land Survey of urban HAbitations) pilot programme in February 2025. title: Building National Analytics Capacity: Advances and Future Pathways
abstract: The capacity of nations to collect, govern, analyse and act upon data has become a defining determinant of public value, competitiveness and resilience. This paper synthesises the state of the art in national analytics capacity, the interlocking set of infrastructures, human capital, institutional and governance arrangements that allow a country to convert data into decisions at scale, and charts a forward-looking research agenda. title: An optimization framework of spatially stratified heterogeneous sampling under sample size and cost constraints for soil pollution surveys
abstract: Soil pollution surveys are essential for pollution assessment, remediation and environmental management and soil contamination presents complex spatial patterns. Existing approaches, including conditioned Latin hypercube sampling (cLHS), stratified sampling, gridded sampling and the Bethel algorithm, either rely heavily on auxiliary variables or subjective designs, lacking explicit quantification of the trade-offs among sample size, cost and estimation uncertainty. abstract: Background: This research is a preliminary study in conflict archaeology focusing on motorized military vehicles from the World War II and Indonesian National Revolution periods (1942–1949) on the island of Java. abstract: Abstract This study develops an activity‐based inversion framework to quantify sectoral carbon dioxide (CO 2 ) emissions using observations of co‐emitted air pollutants. title: Evaluating Energy Consumption drivers in Saudi Arabia and Prioritizing Sustainable Solutions: An FAHP Approach
abstract: Saudi Arabia faces rising energy demand driven by rapid urbanization, industrialization, and population growth, presenting major sustainability challenges. This study employs the Fuzzy Analytic Hierarchy Process (FAHP) to evaluate the key determinants of energy consumption and to prioritize sustainable alternatives. energy-consumption drivers and strategies were identified through a systematic literature review and assessed using expert-based pairwise comparisons. title: Divergent range dynamics among non-native Coleoptera: climate drivers and poleward expansion in multiple species
abstract: Introduction The expansion and contraction of species ranges result from population dynamics, species interactions, and environmental responses. As temperatures rise at high latitudes, some temperate species may be shifting poleward. As non-native species expand in range they threaten native biodiversity and disrupt ecosystem functioning, making range dynamics critical to understand for effective control programs. title: A Typology of Digital Complaint-Resolution Systems for Public Accountability
abstract: Public organisations increasingly invite citizens to report grievances, service failures, and misconduct through digital channels ranging from municipal 311 hotlines and dedicated grievance-redressal portals to social-media pages and crowdsourced fault-reporting maps. Although these systems are widely promoted as instruments of public accountability, the literature treats them as an undifferentiated category, obscuring important variation in how each design distributes voice, obligates a response, and exposes performance to scrutiny. title: Design and Mechanical Characterization of Lightweight Lattice Structures Fabricated through Additive Manufacturing
abstract: The increasing demand for lightweight, mechanically efficient structures in aerospace, automotive, biomedical, energy, and transportation engineering has accelerated the development of architected cellular materials fabricated through additive manufacturing. Lattice structures provide a particularly attractive solution because material can be distributed according to structural requirements while maintaining low mass, controllable stiffness, and enhanced energy-absorption capability. This paper presents a comprehensive mechanics-based investigation of the design and mechanical characterization
journal: Stanzaleaf International Journal of Multidisciplinary Studies

abstract: Study region The Afram Plains South District, situated within Ghana’s Voltaian Basin. Study focus Groundwater is the mainstay of domestic supply in this district; however, many boreholes fail during extended dry spells. This study explored aquifer recharge sources and rates using hydrochemical signatures, stable water isotopes ( δ 18 Ο H2O , δ ²H H2O ) and the Chloride Mass Balance technique. Characterizing recharge processes of groundwater in this district is critical for guiding groundwater development and management in this hydrogeologically complex setting. title: Design lattice metamaterials with pre-strain-enabled soft mode switching via topology optimization
abstract: Soft deformation modes govern the compliant response and elastic-wave characteristics of lattice metamaterials, but these modes are usually determined by the as-fabricated geometry. This study presents a topology-optimization framework that jointly designs lattice connectivity and prescribed pre-strain to tailor the eigenvalues and eigenvectors of the tangent effective elasticity matrix. Prestress-dependent numerical homogenization accounts for changes in member geometry and the geometric stiffness generated by internal axial forces. title: Global dynamic changes in urban design: a critical review of theoretical evolution and emerging paradigms
abstract: Abstract Urban design theory has evolved through successive paradigm shifts since the early twentieth century, each driven by the failure of existing frameworks to address specific urban crises. This review examines three questions: what mechanism produces paradigm shifts; what different urbanisation conditions contribute to the theoretical archive; and what the discipline’s current theoretical diversity means for cities facing compound global challenges. journal: Frontiers of Urban and Rural Planning

title: Operational Resilience in Financial Services: An Integrated Risk, Control, and Analytics Framework
abstract: Operational resilience has moved from an operational-risk sub-discipline to a supervisory priority for financial services, driven by regulatory instruments that require firms to identify important business services, set impact tolerances, and demonstrate the capacity to remain within those tolerances through severe but plausible disruption. Yet the concept is often implemented as a compliance mapping exercise that is loosely coupled from the risk, control, and analytics machinery that firms already operate. This paper proposes the Integrated Resilience, Control and Analytics (IRCA) framework,
journal: JOURNAL OF ACCOUNTING AND FINANCIAL MANAGEMENT

title: Chiral separation of chloroalkanes with the chromatographic column onboard Martian rovers
abstract: The Rosalind Franklin rover of ESA's ExoMars mission, with scheduled launch in 2028, hosts the Mars Organic Molecule Analyzer (MOMA) instrument. MOMA is a GC-MS, equipped with an enantioselective capillary column for the separation of chiral molecules. Chirality analysis is an important part of the ExoMars mission as it allows for the determination of whether organic molecules are of biological or nonbiological origin. abstract: The traditional distinction between content and function words continues to underpin much psycholinguistic research, even though other areas of linguistics have long recognized it as problematic (e.g. Bennis et al., 1983, and Ishkhanyan et al., 2017 within aphasiology; Diessel, 1999: 150-153, and Bisang, 2010: 291 within linguistic typology; Emonds, 1985: 162-164, and Rauh, 1993 within grammatical theory). title: Limited but highly variable protected area use by Icelandic Whooper Swan Cygnus cygnus across the annual cycle
abstract: Protected areas form the cornerstone of biodiversity conservation, yet their utilisation by long distance migratory species, such as the Icelandic breeding population of Whooper Swans Cygnus cygnus , remains uncertain. We quantified the extent of protected area utilisation throughout the entire annual cycle using GPS tracking data from 47 individuals tagged in Iceland (>1,000,000 raw fixes, regularised to hourly positions with state-space models). title: Annual geospatial foundation model embeddings for landslide susceptibility assessment in Taiwan
abstract: Landslide susceptibility models (LSMs) must identify unstable terrain before failure is visible, yet it remains unclear whether compact geospatial foundation-model embeddings encode such pre-event information. We evaluate the efficacy of annual 64-dimensional AlphaEarth Foundations embeddings for LSM using Taiwan landslide inventories from 2017–2024. A lightweight classifier trained with hard negatives is used to predict newly mapped landslides from the previous year’s embeddings under temporal and spatial holdout validation. title: Soil and Water Assessment Tool reveals dominant baseflow in semi-arid catchment with sand dams in Kenya
abstract: Introduction Increasing water scarcity and climate variability threaten rural livelihoods in semi-arid regions. Sand dams are widely used as Nature-based Solutions (NbS) to retain water within the sandy matrix of ephemeral riverbeds, yet their catchment-scale hydrological effects remain insufficiently quantified. Methods We applied the Soil and Water Assessment Tool (SWAT+) in a 22.35 km 2 ungauged ephemeral catchment in Makueni County, Kenya, containing 22 sand dams. title: The associations between blue space exposure and lung function in young adults: a cross-sectional study
abstract: The benefits of natural environments for respiratory health are increasingly recognized; however, the effects of blue spaces on young adults’ respiratory health remain understudied. Young adulthood is critical for peak lung function, and exposures during this period may affect later respiratory health. We quantified blue space–lung function associations in Chinese undergraduates. This study aimed to explore the effects of blue space on undergraduates’ lung function using data from the Chinese University Cohort (CUC). title: A new event-scale evaluation framework suggests underestimated skill of WRF-HAILCAST model in climatological hail simulations
abstract: Abstract Hail simulation remains challenging in convection-permitting models, and diagnosing bias pathways is essential for targeted improvement. We developed a framework for evaluating the performance of WRF–HAILCAST in hail simulations from the perspective of mesoscale convection. Across 1,502 hail events in China, the model reproduced hail-swath morphology in 50.87% of cases. Among these cases, 53.4% also showed hail-size distributions consistent with observations. title: Branch-type dynamic vibration absorbers for enhanced and frequency-robust vibration suppression
abstract: Minimizing vibration transmission from mounted machinery remains an important challenge in vibration engineering. Although isolation mounts reduce vibration transmission, residual vibrations can remain significant when excitation forces are large. Moreover, practical machines such as pumps and compressors generate fundamental and harmonic components, requiring vibration suppression at multiple frequencies. title: Beyond Infrastructure Institutional Enablers as the Missing Link in Container Terminal Competitiveness- A Mixed Methods Study from Egypt
abstract: What makes a container terminal competitive in a fast-growing emerging economy? Conventional wisdom emphasises physical assets such as quay length, berth depth, crane capacity and yard area. This study challenges that view by examining the Alexandria Container and Cargo Handling Company (ACCHCO) in Egypt. abstract: This research is centered on BIM technology. By analyzing the technical gaps of typical cases such as the Anjiu Railway project, and drawing on the experience of prefabricated buildings and water conservancy projects, three integrated technology systems have been constructed: BIM + GIS + IoT / NB-IoT is used for long-distance environmental monitoring; BIM + intelligent bridge erection machine + RFID + InSAR is used for bridge settlement control; BIM + intelligent TBM + TSP is used for safe tunnel excavation. title: A comprehensive review of strategies to mitigate non-convexity in full waveform inversion
abstract: Sumamry The introduction of full waveform inversion has been the starting point of four decades of investigation in seismic imaging, which aim to reduce the ill-posedness of this nonlinear and quantitative imaging method. In this review, we propose a comprehensive overview of these investigations. Beyond simply cataloging proposed approaches, this work aims to classify them, identify similarities and differences between methods, establish connections with common concepts and practices in full waveform inversion, and emphasize the few core ideas underlying this long-term research effort. title: Satellite-to-ground quantum key distribution model under time-evolving turbulence
abstract: Atmospheric turbulence is the major challenge to satellite-to-ground quantum key distribution (QKD), yet most performance models treat turbulence only through average statistics, masking temporal loss fluctuations that dominate real links. Here we present an end-to-end, time-evolving satellite-to-ground QKD model that embeds a phase-screen description of turbulence into beam propagation, focusing, tracking, adaptive-optics compensation, and single-mode fiber (SMF) coupling. title: Nghiên cứu tác động của điều kiện khí tượng nhiệt đới đối với hoạt động của phương tiện bay không người lái ở Việt Nam
abstract: Phương tiện bay không người lái (UAV) ngày càng được ứng dụng rộng rãi trong cả lĩnh vực quân sự và dân sự. Tại Việt Nam, điều kiện khí hậu nhiệt đới gió mùa với đặc trưng mưa lớn, gió mạnh và nhiệt độ cao đặt ra nhiều thách thức đối với khả năng hoạt động bay. Nghiên cứu này đánh giá ảnh hưởng của điều kiện khí tượng nhiệt đới đến khả năng bay của UAV tại Việt Nam và khu vực Biển Đông. Ba yếu tố chính được xem xét gồm nhiệt độ không khí, tốc độ gió và lượng mưa, với hai nhóm UAV đại diện: UAV phổ thông (CD) và UAV chịu thời tiết (WRD). title: Investigation of the Influence of Segment Thickness on the Anti-Flotation Stability of Twin Shield Tunnels in Water-Rich Strata
abstract: Abstract Anti-flotation stability is a critical concern for shield tunnels constructed in water-rich strata, particularly for twin shield tunnels, where excavation-induced disturbance interacts with groundwater buoyancy. This study investigates the influence of segment thickness on the anti-flotation stability of twin shield tunnels through three-dimensional numerical simulations and physical model tests. title: Actores territoriales en los procesos de planificación estratégica de los gobiernos locales
abstract: El estudio abordó la limitada participación efectiva de los actores territoriales en los procesos de planificación estratégica de los gobiernos locales, problemática asociada con brechas entre la formulación de los instrumentos, la articulación institucional y la incorporación real de las necesidades ciudadanas en la toma de decisiones. El objetivo fue analizar la participación de los actores territoriales en estos procesos, identificando su intervención, mecanismos de articulación y contribución a la definición de prioridades y decisiones para el desarrollo territorial. title: Invited perspectives: Towards usable compound event research
abstract: Supporting stakeholders with science-based decision-making to mitigate and adapt to climate change impacts is a central mandate of the climate research community. In particular, mapping out scenario-dependent climate risk landscapes is one of the most pressing challenges. Increasingly, communities and regions are experiencing high-impact climate and weather extremes that arise from a complex interplay of processes and events acting across various spatial and temporal scales. title: Inferring groundwater overdraft in data-scarce arid agro-ecosystems: a semi-empirical remote sensing framework applied to the Elfeija watershed, Morocco
abstract: Introduction Small-scale irrigated agriculture in arid regions relies heavily on unmetered groundwater, creating an “invisible pumping” threat to aquifer sustainability. Monitoring these diffuse withdrawals remains a critical challenge for water governance. This study proposes a synergistic multi-sensor remote sensing workflow to infer groundwater abstraction and assess its impact on local water stress using a semi-empirical thermal-phenological model. abstract: Giriş ve Hedefler Orman alanlarındaki yer yüzey fenolojilerinin (YYF) değişiminin izlenmesi iklim değişikliğine uyum ve sürdürülebilir doğal kaynak yönetimi açısından oldukça önemlidir. title: The Regulation of Building Structures in Earthquake Disasters by the Internet of Things
abstract: The earthquake occurred suddenly and was extremely destructive, with buildings collapsing and structures being damaged being the core causes of casualties and economic losses in the disaster. Traditional building earthquake protection is difficult to meet the current urgent needs for disaster prevention in urban high-rise buildings.
