abstract: Retrieval-augmented generation increasingly serves as the knowledge backbone for sensor-informed infrastructure decisions, where a field engineer must retrieve the clause stating a design criterion, not a document about the topic. In twenty years (2005–2024) of Korea Expressway Corporation design-practice guidelines (HWP/HWPX), we identify a framing bias in dense retrieval as follows: embedding models over-weight the topical aboutness of a section title relative to the criterion in its body. title: Rapid increase of climate extremes reveals new areas of concern in Amazonia
abstract: Abstract Amazonia is highly sensitive to climate extremes, yet we lack an Amazon-wide assessment that examines the spatial-temporal changes in these extreme conditions. We address this within seasons and across the hydrological year, using a quantiles approach that integrates the frequency and magnitude of climate extremes and by linking changes in temperature with evapotranspiration. We show that high temperature extremes and temperature-linked measures of water deficit are both changing at a much faster rate than central trends. title: Spatiotemporal dynamics and driving mechanisms of net ecosystem productivity in the retrogressive thaw slump regions of the Qinghai-Tibetan Plateau
abstract: Global climate warming has led to the thawing of permafrost, triggering widespread and frequent retrogressive thaw slump (RTS) disasters on the Qinghai-Tibetan Plateau (QTP). Previous studies have mainly focused on RTS dynamics, while the spatiotemporal variations of net ecosystem productivity (NEP) in RTS regions on the QTP remain insufficiently understood, mainly due to the limited comparative assessments of NEP dynamics between RTS and non-RTS regions, and the underlying driving mechanisms remain unclear. title: Mechanical behavior and microstructural evolution of waste-derived geopolymer composites incorporating dredged sediment and waste shredded tire
abstract: The sustainable utilization of dredged sediment and waste materials in construction remains challenging because of the high compressibility of dredged sediment and the limited deformation tolerance of geopolymer-based materials. This study develops a waste-derived geopolymer composite incorporating dredged sediment, fly ash (FA), ground granulated blast-furnace slag (GGBS), and waste shredded tire (WST), and investigates its shear strength, compressibility, rebound behavior, and microstructural evolution. title: Parametric numerical analysis of anti-adhesion structural design for a bucket wheel reclaimer
abstract: To address the reduced discharge efficiency of Bucket Wheel Reclaimers caused by the strong material adhesion, this study investigates a typical Bucket Wheel Reclaimer used for lateritic nickel ore. Following the calibration of the discrete element method (DEM) parameters, simulations were conducted to investigate the effects of the bucket-lip cutting angle, bucket depth, and chute width on discharge performance. title: Dental Microwear Texture Analysis on Radular Teeth
abstract: ABSTRACT Dental wear is a well‐established proxy for inferring diet, habitat, and climatic conditions in vertebrate ecology, yet its proxy potential in invertebrates remains unexplored. Here, we introduce confocal disc‐scanning microscopy–based 3D surface texture analysis combined with dental microwear texture analysis as a quantitative approach for assessing wear in the radular teeth of the gastropod Vittina turrita . title: What Uniparental Lineages Tell Us About the Prehistoric Human Colonization of the Americas
abstract: OBJECTIVES: From the perspective of uniparental markers, the view of the human prehistoric settlement of America is that it resulted from a single main migration after the Last Glacial Maximum, following a long or short period of genetic isolation in Beringia. Ancient DNA and whole genome analyses have confirmed this view. My objective here is to demonstrate that humans entered America before the LGM and that the documented post-LGM expansions began in South instead of North America. title: In blockchain we trust? A critical review of blockchain in supply chains
abstract: The increasing importance of blockchain in supply chains has led to myriad papers with conflicting or imprecise results. This critical review of 118 articles first summarises the emerging literature on the role of trust in blockchain use in supply chains. Next, we identify and refine concepts that have been neglected or confused in the literature. We note the critical role of physical data verification (i.e., checking that on-chain records match the state of physical goods). title: Outsourcing logistics for smarter railways: quantitative evidence on cost, delivery and service performance
abstract: Purpose This study examines the relationship between logistics outsourcing and railway operational performance in the Moroccan railway sector, with particular emphasis on the mediating roles of cost efficiency, delivery reliability and service quality. Drawing upon transaction cost economics (TCE) and the resource-based view (RBV), the study investigates how logistics outsourcing contributes to operational performance through the enhancement of key operational capabilities. title: Shifts in Nitrate Formation Pathways and Precursor Sensitivity During Autumn PM 2.5 Pollution in Shijiazhuang, China
abstract: Abstract Fine particulate matter (PM 2.5 ) have significant impacts on regional air quality, climate, and human health. Among its chemical components, nitrate has shown a rapidly increasing contribution in recent years with the trend of dominating over sulfate. In this study, a field observation was conducted from October to November 2024 at an urban site in Shijiazhuang, Hebei Province in China. title: Rearrangement Towards Stability: Plastic Shakedown in Granular Materials Under Thermal Cycles
abstract: ABSTRACT Granular materials are routinely subjected to thermal cycling due to natural and anthropogenic phenomena. Despite the ubiquity of this occurrence and its relevance for science, engineering, and technology, the long‐term thermo‐mechanical response of granular materials to repeated heating and cooling remains poorly understood. title: Social Capital Recovery in Post-Nuclear Disaster: Perspectives through a Field Course in Fukushima
abstract: On 11 March 2011, the Great East Japan Earthquake and the Fukushima nuclear accident resulted in several detrimental consequences, including persistent stigmatization of disaster victims, disaster-related anxiety, and loss of trust for government authorities. Through a social capital lens, we aimed to share the perspectives of Fukushima residents who have lived through the post-disaster recovery process. title: Dust radiative effects and impact on energy production over the Mediterranean Basin
abstract: Abstract. Atmospheric aerosols are among the key factors affecting the Earth’s radiation budget, playing a fundamental role in understanding climate forcing, feedback mechanisms, and their impact on future climate projections and on solar energy systems. More specifically, dust aerosol particles, which are characterized by high complexity of their optical and microphysical properties, remain one of the most uncertain components. title: Experimental evaluation of adiabatic cooling due to CO2 injection into sandstone formations
abstract: This paper presents a systematic experimental investigation of Joule–Thomson (JT) and evaporative cooling during CO 2 injection into porous media under conditions relevant to depleted-reservoir Geological Carbon Sequestration (GCS). Core-flooding experiments were performed on two sandstones with contrasting permeabilities. title: Global drought shows no detectable recent acceleration under climate warming
abstract: Recent studies suggest that warming is accelerating continental drought, but these conclusions rely on drought indices using Penman-type potential evapotranspiration (PET). While Penman-type PET is widely used and may suit non-water-limited or irrigated surfaces, it can overstate evaporative demand at broader spatial scales by neglecting land-atmosphere coupling constraints; energy-based PET formulations can address this limitation. title: The Hydro-Meteorological Data Analysis on the Impacts of Climate Variability on Water Resources Governance in the Lake Naivasha Basin, Kenya
abstract: This study presents a comprehensive hydro-meteorological analysis of the Lake Naivasha Basin, a critical freshwater ecosystem in Kenya's Rift Valley, to evaluate the temporal and spatial variability of precipitation, temperature, evaporation, and lake water levels over multiple decades. The analysis integrates primary and secondary datasets obtained from the Kenya Meteorological Department, the Water Resources Authority, and satellite observations. title: Climate change both increases and decreases winter snowmelt across North America
abstract: Snowmelt, a vital source of freshwater for a large portion of North America’s population, is increasingly vulnerable to the impact of climate change. Air temperature and precipitation are significant climatic controllers regulating snowmelt dynamics. In this study, we quantified the response of winter snowmelt magnitude to changing temperature and precipitation across North America (Canada and the United States) using gridded, observation-driven data and future projections. title: Hydraulic Resistances of Membrane Filters and their Role in Industrial-Scale Make-Up Water Treatment
abstract: This study presents the design and evaluation of a multistage membrane filtration system to produce ultrapure quality make-up water for thermal power plants using the Danube River as the feedwater source. Laboratory-scale filtration experiments were performed using a flat-sheet test cell to determine the hydraulic resistances of ultrafiltration, nanofiltration, and reverse osmosis membranes under varying transmembrane pressures. abstract: This study investigated the compressive behaviour of concrete incorporating treated domestic sewage sludge (DSS), industrial sewage sludge (ISS), disposable face mask fibres (DFMF), and silica fume (SF), while evaluating the ability of the Concrete Damage Plasticity (CDP) model in ABAQUS to reproduce the observed mechanical response. title: Application of Computational Fluid Dynamics Techniques to Mitigate Wind Induced Noise in the Complex Built Environment
abstract: Wind induced noise occurs when airflow passes through narrow architectural openings such as window interface gaps, louvres, vents, façade joints, or around elements including fins, balustrades, or decorative cladding. These interactions can generate tonal or broadband noise often perceived as whistling, humming, or howling, particularly under elevated wind conditions. title: Fine particulate matter (PM2.5) and suicide in South Korea: an instrumental variable analysis using thermal inversion
abstract: Air pollution causes the deterioration of both physical and mental health and increases the risk of suicide. Existing studies on the association between air pollution and suicide rely on meta-analyses and simple correlation analyses, which cannot quantify how much the increase in air pollution levels increases suicide rates. This study thus examines the relationship between fine particulate matter (PM 2.5 ) pollution and suicide mortality in South Korea from 2015 to 2019 using thermal inversions as an instrumental variable to induce exogenous variations in PM 2.5 levels. abstract: The limitations of the research on the water-salt migration of sulfate-stained soil using solid waste as the sole binding material, such as the difficulty in characterizing the hydration reaction products over time, were addressed in this study. The research focused on different ratios of solid waste-based binding materials for solidifying sulfate-stained soil. abstract: Abstract Additive manufacturing (AM) combined with smart materials has enabled 4D printing of structures capable of programmable, stimulus-driven shape transformation. abstract: Abstract Most volcanoes on Earth display a range of eruptive styles, varying between effusive and explosive activity. Understanding the factors controlling these transitions is critical for volcanic hazard assessment but remains debated. While both pre-eruptive storage conditions and syn-eruptive conduit processes influence eruption style, their relative roles are often difficult to disentangle, particularly in alkaline volcanic systems. title: Integrating QUAL2KW nitrate modeling with ambient grey-water dilution pressure and wheat-pathway exposure screening in a semi-arid basin
abstract: Nitrate pollution in semi-arid rivers creates coupled ecological stress and downstream human exposure, particularly where surface water is reused for irrigation. This study integrated QUAL2KW hydrodynamic–water quality modeling with wheat-pathway exposure screening, ecological screening using Risk Quotients (RQ), and ambient grey-water dilution-pressure analysis in the Zayandeh-Roud River, Iran. abstract: Elevated dissolved organic carbon (DOC) concentrations are a major concern for ecosystems and drinking water supply. Data-driven studies revealed variable functioning of different landscape units (upland, riparian zone, and groundwater) in catchment DOC mobilization and export. However, lumped and landscape-explicit (separating upland and riparian zone) model structures are generally calibrated to stream DOC concentrations, while the internal DOC dynamics often do not receive sufficient attention. title: Mitigation strategies for addressing environmental, social, and governance challenges in third-party logistics: A sustainable transition perspective
abstract: Although environmental, social, and governance (ESG) practices are increasingly important in the logistics sector, small and medium-sized third-party logistics providers (SME 3PLs) continue to face significant barriers to sustainable transition. Existing studies have largely examined these barriers conceptually, with limited attention to systematically prioritizing them and linking them to targeted mitigation strategies. abstract: Wildfire serves a critical function in shaping the structure, composition and processes of Earth’s ecosystems. However, anthropogenic climate change over the past century has catalyzed a shift in wildfire regimes, particularly in California, as evidenced by increases in the extent, frequency and severity of fires. The broad social-economic consequences of extreme wildfire events necessitate systematic frameworks that incorporate multi-source observations to support risk assessments and pre-fire interventions. abstract: Volcanic mercury cannot be interpreted from bulk flux alone because the atmospheric transport, deposition, and preservation depend on speciation. This study presents a thermodynamic–kinetic approach for constructing equilibrium and quench speciation diagrams for mercury-bearing volcanic gases. abstract: This study presents a probabilistic seismic hazard analysis (PSHA) for Croatia and its 3 major tectonic zones: Adriatic Foreland, Dinarides, and Pannonian Basin, using the OpenQuake Engine in classical mode, with emphasis on the construction, justification and validation of a Croatia-specific seismic source model and its implications for seismic design practice. title: The Hidden Health and Climate Burden of Black Carbon under China’s Dual Carbon Strategy
abstract: Black carbon (BC) is a highly toxic air pollutant and potent short-lived climate pollutant. China’s Dual Carbon strategy—peaking carbon emissions before 2030 and achieving carbon neutrality before 2060—has driven rapid BC emission reductions. However, global inventories still misrepresent BC emissions in China, biasing estimates of its health and climate impacts. Using a localized BC inventory and revised health risk function, we estimate that over 540,000 premature deaths were attributable to BC in China in 2015, more than twice previous reports. title: Preventing a groundwater divide: Ensuring quality hydrogeology education for all in the age of online coursework following the COVID-19 pandemic
abstract: Abstract The COVID-19 pandemic forced an almost overnight rethink of traditional hydrogeology education, elevating online delivery as the primary means of teaching hydrogeology during 2020–2021. This change has had far-reaching effects, some of which persist in the form of greater reliance on online teaching formats in many universities. This paper describes the experience of delivering hydrogeology coursework in a city affected by the longest COVID lockdown in the world. Key lessons for hydrogeology education are examined.

title: Wildfire exposure and political participation in Africa
abstract: Abstract Civic engagement can shape collective responses to climate change. However, evidence on how climate-related disasters affect political participation in Africa remains limited. Combining Global Fire Atlas records with Afrobarometer surveys of more than 100,000 people in 34 African countries, we show that people living close to wildfires are more likely to vote, contact local councillors, attend community meetings, and raise collective issues, whereas protest participation shows weaker responses. title: Clean-air regulation reduces childhood wasting and overweight in China
abstract: Whether large-scale air-quality policies improve child nutrition remains uncertain. Here we show that China’s Air Pollution Prevention and Control Action Plan reduces wasting and overweight among children under five. We use annual data from 2759 counties between 2005 and 2017 and a matched difference-in-differences design to evaluate the policy as a natural experiment. The policy is associated with a 0.760% reduction in wasting and a 3.950% reduction in overweight relative to control areas. Reductions in fine particulate matter explain an estimated 57.7% and 68.9% of these respective effects.

abstract: ABSTRACT In developing countries, urban tourism systems increasingly rely on large-capacity buses, whose stopping, boarding, and manoeuvring operations often create localised congestion and traffic bottlenecks. However, contemporary routing algorithms can create a paradox whereby solutions that are optimal for individual tourist buses may collectively induce emergent network-wide congestion when deployed simultaneously across the entire fleet. abstract: Abstract In this study, the bond behaviour between steel bars and steel-fibre-reinforced recycled aggregate concrete (SFRAC) is investigated using 27 pull-out tests. The main test parameters include concrete strength grade, recycled coarse aggregate replacement ratio, steel fibre volume fraction, and bonded length. Based on the test results, the failure mode, bond strength, and bond stress-slip curves of the SFRAC bond specimens were analysed. title: Impact of urban waterlogging on fire service accessibility under extreme rainfall events
abstract: Extreme rainfall events associated with climate change exacerbate urban waterlogging, posing significant threats to fire services. This study constructs a hierarchical evaluation model to quantify the impact of such climate-driven compound events on fire service accessibility. Waterlogging avoidance areas were designated, and rescue times were then simulated using real-time traffic data. abstract: This study aims to examine the influence of product innovation, service quality, and customer satisfaction on passenger preferences, while incorporating the mediating role of loyalty and the moderating effect of land transportation policy implementation. abstract: Smart city megaprojects routinely fall short of the utopian visions promoted by their creators, yet the failure of these projects has not been systematically compared across cases or grounded in a shared analytical framework. This paper addresses that gap by examining ten smart city new-town projects from around the world, including Songdo, NEOM, Sidewalk Toronto, Masdar City, and others, at various stages of development, construction, suspension, and abandonment. title: TOWARDS A DIGITAL DATABASE FOR RELIGIOUS HERITAGE: THE IBN KHALDOUN MOSQUE IN BÉJAÏA
abstract: The conservation of architectural heritage poses significant challenges for countries aiming to preserve their cultural identity and pass on their heritage to future generations while addressing contemporary issues. Architectural heritage is often represented by richly decorated, historically significant monumental buildings. Yet less visible, more modest buildings can also be important bearers of cultural values. Béjaïa was once a major commercial and intellectual crossroads in the Mediterranean. Rich in centuries-old heritage, some of its more discreet components are still poorly documented.

title: A framework for evaluating the traceability of primary data elements for textile digital product passports
abstract: Digital Product Passports (DPPs) require high-quality traceable product data across complex supply chains. However, existing approaches to traceability assessment predominantly emphasise data availability and enabling technologies but offer no methodology for systematically evaluating whether individual primary data elements (PDEs) can be reliably linked to the physical product characteristics they are intended to represent. title: Dynamic analysis of a historical monumental structure due to acoustic and anthropic vibrations during large concert events
abstract: Abstract Historical monumental structures are a fundamental component of cultural identity, yet they are highly vulnerable to structural degradation driven by human activities. Among these, crowd-induced vibrations have emerged as a critical concern, particularly in historical venues that host large public events. This study investigates the structural impact of acoustic and anthropic loads on the historical Moletta Tower, located in the Circus Maximus archaeological site in Rome, Italy. title: A review of full-stack autonomous obstacle avoidance for assistive robots for the disabled
abstract: With the intensification of population aging and the increasing awareness of protecting the rights of the disabled, significant progress has been made in assistive robots for visually impaired people, the mobility impairments and other groups. abstract: Atmospheric hydrogen (H 2 ) plays a significant role in tropospheric chemistry, yet substantial uncertainty remains surrounding the magnitude and controls of the global soil sink. We report the first year-long, continuous measurements of H 2 exchange using the aerodynamic gradient (AG) method at a temperate grassland. While the FAO-56 crop coefficient approach is the most widely used method for estimating crop water requirements, the Allen & Pereira approach offers a more dynamic and less empirical alternative that may be particularly suitable for automated irrigation management. abstract: Sustainable urban planning frameworks presuppose institutional stability and regulated development, yet their applicability to conflict-affected cities remains theoretically underexamined. This qualitative case study examines how sustainability is interpreted and prioritised in Marib city, Yemen, an urban centre experiencing rapid growth amid armed conflict and mass internal displacement. title: Cross-Departmental Alignment Frameworks during Major Expansion Projects: A Strategic Review of Operations and Project Interface Management in Brownfield Liquefaction Expansions
abstract: A brownfield expansion places two organisations on one site with incompatible success criteria. The operating organisation is accountable for uptime, containment and the safety of a running facility, and is rewarded for stability. abstract: This study aims to reconstruct a Digital-Based Human Resource Management (DHRM) model that enhances employee motivation and sustainable performance in modern organizations. It examines how DHRM is implemented, contributes to employee motivation, and supports sustainable employee performance. abstract: Abstract The rapid expansion of textile and apparel manufacturing in emerging economies like Ethiopia has increased the need for Sustainable Supply Chain Management (SSCM) practices that balance economic growth with environmental and social responsibility. However, empirical evidence regarding SSCM implementation and its performance implications in emerging manufacturing contexts remains limited. abstract: The increasing global demand for resilient subsurface energy systems requires understanding how active tectonics influence hydrocarbon trap evolution and reservoir pressure behavior. abstract: Urban flooding has become an increasingly critical challenge worldwide, driven by urbanisation-induced changes to natural drainage systems and intensifying climate-driven precipitation extremes. Previous research on water-sensitive urban design has largely focused on stormwater runoff in simplified urban layouts, while giving less attention to the complexity of real urban form and its effect on flood behaviour. abstract: This study investigates four rockfall incidents that occurred in Ado Ekiti, Ekiti State, southwestern Nigeria, in August–September 2019, specifically at Olokemeji, Ayunbo, Moferere, and Odolofin. abstract: ABSTRACT Local environmental politics in China is often said to be dominated by state‐controlled modes of multi‐level governance. However, top‐down governance is embedded within and transformed by local politics, adding complexity to governance practices and environmental outcomes. abstract: This study developed future regional Intensity-Duration-Frequency curves for Sri Lanka using climate change scenarios to address the growing need for adaptive infrastructure planning. abstract: Wildfires are the primary disturbance in Mediterranean forest ecosystems, where climate change is projected to intensify fire hazard by reducing fuel moisture and altering fire regimes. abstract: Rapid, under-serviced urbanization across the tropical belt has left many cities dependent on open dumps. abstract: This paper reviews recent progress in high-precision carbon-14 measurements in tree rings and their importance for accurately reconstructing past solar activity cycles as well as extreme solar and galactic cosmic-ray events. abstract: A variabilidade dos elementos climáticos corresponde a um importante insumo analítico para a prevenção, redução e mitigação de impactos indesejáveis, especialmente no que diz respeito à produção de alimentos, ao abastecimento hídrico e à geração de energia elétrica. abstract: Straight outlet conduits (SOCs) are widely used in pump stations. abstract: Abstract Traditional rigid discrete element method (DEM) models cannot accurately describe the viscoelastoplastic deformation and fracture of wheat stubble under mechanical loading. abstract: Access to safe drinking water is a fundamental environmental health requirement, yet integrated assessments of treatment performance and health risks under different land-use pressures remain limited in South Africa. This study evaluated the performance of two drinking water treatment plants in Mahikeng and Klerksdorp, North-West province, representing agricultural and industrial catchments, respectively. abstract: Abiotic stresses are among the most important factors limiting plant growth and production worldwide. abstract: Societies increasingly face complex multi-risk environments, yet risk perception research typically examines hazards in isolation. title: Extending passivhaus to non-domestic buildings in the UK: performance under future climate variability and modelling simplification
abstract: Abstract Passivhaus is a world-leading standard for ultra-low energy, zero-carbon buildings. However, the long-term performance of such buildings under future variable climate change remains insufficiently understood. Building Performance Simulation (BPS) is a valuable tool to assess future impacts across scenarios, though workflows can be complex and time-consuming. This paper investigates whether passive building design can maintain thermal comfort and energy performance under future climate variability and evaluates the reliability of simplified BPS models in predicting these effects. title: Repurposing waste wind turbine blades as GFRP rebars in inorganic polymer concrete: A feasibility study
abstract: Although wind turbines are designed for long-term operation (20–35 years), many are approaching end-of-life, calling for efficient and cost-effective recycling strategies. In current industrial practice, blades are shredded as a whole, producing mixed waste streams with shortened fibres and resin-rich residues, thereby reducing material value and limiting reuse to low-value filler applications. This study presents, for the first time, a high-value repurposing route in which decommissioned wind turbine blades are selectively cut into GFRP rebars and incorporated into industrial slag-based concr
journal: Journal of Reinforced Plastics and Composites

title: The influence of weather on photovoltaic efficiency and solar mapping in Alagoas using the WRF-Solar model
abstract: Although the use of photovoltaic (PV) energy is a well-established strategy for the energy transition and climate change mitigation through the reduction of CO2 emissions, the literature lacks studies that integrate real-world field operation data with atmospheric models to map generation potential in the region. Power generation efficiency is directly influenced by the inherent characteristics of PV systems and by installation losses, variables quantified by the Performance Ratio (PR). title: CFD & experimentally validated quasi-static trailing-edge morphing-inspired configurations for aerodynamic enhancement of vertical axis wind turbines
abstract: Abstract This study presents a combined numerical–experimental investigation of a quasi-static trailing-edge morphing strategy to enhance the aerodynamic performance of vertical axis wind turbines (VAWTs), with emphasis on power coefficient ( C p ) improvement and wake evolution. A hybrid airfoil consisting of 60% rigid and 40% flexible trailing-edge section, based on NACA 2412, is analysed for quasi-static deflections of + 5°, + 10°, and + 15°. journal: Journal of Engineering and Applied Science

title: HydroSuite-AI: a web-based LLM environment for hydrological code generation and execution for the hydrosuite open-source ecosystem
abstract: Abstract Researchers in hydrology face technical barriers from complex models, evolving libraries, and fragmented documentation. We present HydroSuite-AI, an LLM-based assistant that integrates the open-source web hydrologic libraries HydroLang, HydroCompute, and HydroRTC for code generation, factual guidance, and in-browser execution of hydrological workflows. The system uses a Planner-Worker-Synthesizer architecture with retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) over library documentation and validates outputs in a client-side virtualized execution environment. title: Evaluation of simulated N cycling using observations from a 15 N tracer experiment in a mixed deciduous forest
abstract: Nitrogen availability constrains terrestrial carbon uptake and storage, yet large uncertainties remain in the magnitude of the effect, because the interactions of the carbon and nitrogen (N) dynamics are challenging to observe in undisturbed ecosystems at relevant timescales. Long-term experiments with 15 N tracer applications allow the study of the nitrogen cycle in a fairly undisturbed manner, and they are therefore a valuable data source to test the biogeochemical dynamics simulated by terrestrial biosphere models. In this study we applied the model QUINCY (QUantifying Interactions between

title: Operationalizing the Greening of Religion: Developing and Validating a Laudato si’ –Grounded Instrument
abstract: ABSTRACT The phenomenon of the greening of religion (GoR) has rarely been examined empirically. Existing instruments for measuring environmental attitudes are not designed with religious ecological discourse in mind, nor are they suited to testing its conceptual boundaries. The study aimed to develop and validate a measurement instrument grounded in the religious ecological discourse articulated in Laudato si’ ( LS ). Drawing on a content analysis of LS , the study developed a set of measurement scales comprising adapted preservation and utilization orientations and an additional Ecological Sp
journal: Journal for the Scientific Study of Religion
institutions: John Paul II Catholic University of Lublin

title: Image-guided cardiac focused ultrasound neuromodulation regulates heart rate
abstract: Symptomatic bradycardia can pose significant health risks, yet available therapies are either transient, invasive, or lack spatial precision. Here, we introduce an image-guided cardiac focused ultrasound (cFUS) neuromodulation approach that noninvasively and selectively engages cardiac sympathetic activity to increase heart rate (HR) while preserving sinus rhythm. title: The influence of stenosis severity and geometric orientation on atherosclerotic progression: A fluid-structure interaction study in the carotid artery
abstract: Atherosclerosis remains the leading global cause of mortality, and its progression is strongly influenced by the local hemodynamic environment. Low Wall Shear Stress (WSS) is widely recognized as a promoter of atherosclerosis, yet the combined influence of stenosis severity and its geometric orientation on disease progression in anatomically realistic geometries has not been systematically examined. This study assesses the risk of atherosclerotic progression in a carotid artery using one-way Fluid-Structure Interaction (FSI). Four stenosis levels were simulated (0, 30, 60, and 80%), along with
journal: Physical and Engineering Sciences in Medicine

title: Wire element: a kinematic compatibility-based curvilinear beam element for geometrically nonlinear analysis of highly flexible slender structures
abstract: Abstract This work presents a planar curvilinear beam finite element, referred to as the Wire Element, for the geometrically nonlinear analysis of slender one-dimensional structures undergoing large displacements and finite rotations. The proposed formulation differs from conventional displacement-interpolation approaches for it reconstructs the internal kinematics through direct integration of compatibility equations along the beam axis. title: AI-driven volcanic SO2 estimates using MSG-SEVIRI and Sentinel-5P TROPOMI
abstract: Abstract Sulfur dioxide (SO 2 ) is, after H 2 O and CO 2 , the most abundant volcanic gas released during shallow magma degassing and is readily detectable and quantifiable by remote sensing. Monitoring SO 2 provides key information on magma ascent rates, conduit dynamics, and eruption style and intensity, thereby supporting volcano monitoring and hazard assessment. The TROPOMI instrument onboard the low Earth Orbit Sentinel-5 Precursor delivers highly accurate and sensitive SO 2 retrievals but with limited temporal coverage (typically one overpass per day). title: Moisture-path-dependent thermal resistivity hysteresis of compacted soils for energy and geotechnical systems
abstract: Poor understanding of soil heat transfer and thermal resistivity accelerates the deterioration of buried energy and geotechnical infrastructure systems, with consequent effects on their short- and long-term safety and reliability. This study presents a unified, cross-textural framework that quantifies the effect of soil grain size on hysteresis (wetting and drying pathways)-driven alterations in soil thermal resistivity across complex soil textures and moisture contents. title: Study of the influence of the braided river configuration mode and injection–production relationship on remaining oil distribution: a case study of the Gudong Oil Field
abstract: This article addresses the problem that the matching relationship between the braided river configuration and the injection–production streamline of a reservoir in the late stage of ultra-high water cut leads to different distribution patterns of the remaining oil at the top and plane of the layer. This article studies the influence of static and dynamic factors on the distribution of remaining oil in the braided river sedimentary model by means of numerical simulation. title: Thermo-hydro-mechanical response of the operation style in a faulted Malm reservoir: Storage triplet vs. hydrothermal doublet
abstract: Abstract The existing heat in the earth can be considered as an abundant source of clean energy. Geothermal applications have extracted this resource via various approaches, such as petro- and hydrothermal systems or heat pumps. In recent years, thermal energy storage systems (ATES), which balance the temporal mismatch of the energy demand and supply were widely developed, primarily in the Netherlands. title: TECHNICAL VIABILITY OF UNDERGROUND HYDROGEN STORAGE IN DEPLETED HYDROCARBON RESERVOIRS: A GLOBAL COMPARATIVE ANALYSIS
abstract: Purpose of the work. This study evaluates the technical viability of underground hydrogen storage (UHS) in depleted hydrocarbon reservoirs, with a particular focus on Central European basin conditions. The work aims to assess whether depleted oil and gas fields can provide large-scale, long-duration hydrogen storage as an alternative to geographically constrained salt cavern systems. Methodology. The research is based on a structured literature review and comparative analysis of peer-reviewed publications, international energy agency reports, and documented field pilot projects. title: Utilization of iron powder as a partial replacement for silica sand in heavy-weight UHPC
abstract: This study investigates the feasibility of utilizing iron powder (IP) as a partial to full replacement for silica sand in Ultra-High Performance Concrete (UHPC), examining its effects on density, mechanical strength, durability, and microstructure. Six mixtures were prepared with IP replacement levels ranging from 0% to 100% by volume of fine aggregate. The results reveal a non-monotonic relationship between IP content and performance. title: Solar-based and battery-assisted energy harvesting systems for IoT: A systematic survey
abstract: Solar energy harvesting combined with battery storage is a key enabler for achieving long-term autonomy in Internet of Things (IoT) systems. However, existing research remains fragmented across heterogeneous hardware design strategies, energy-management techniques, and applications spanning a wide range of domains, often addressing isolated technical aspects without providing a comprehensive system-level perspective. Following the PRISMA guidelines, this systematic survey synthesizes 25 primary studies selected from an initial corpus of 357 publications on solar-based, battery-assisted Energy

title: Influence of hybrid lattice design on mechanical response, failure behaviour, and energy absorption characteristics
abstract: Abstract Hybrid lattice structures have gained a lot of interest for achieving desired physiologic properties such as mechanical performance, anisotropic and energy absorption behaviour. Triply periodic minimal surface (TPMS) lattices, whether with TPMS-TPMS or TPMS-strut configuration are not explored, particularly in terms of deformation mechanisms and failure prediction. title: Large‐Area Flat Optics Color Routing in Tilted Arrays of 2D Semiconductor Nanostripes
abstract: ABSTRACT Here, we introduce a scalable and self‐organised flat optics platform based on centimetre‐scale arrays of tilted Transition Metal Dichalcogenide (TMD) MoS 2 nanostripes, fabricated through an ion‐beam–driven faceting strategy that precisely defines the slope and periodicity of silica templates. This engineered morphology enables maskless, shadow‐assisted growth of crystalline MoS 2 nanostripes with controlled geometry and high uniformity. title: All-hazard management approach for wind
abstract: Despite the principle of managing all hazards, the disaster management field does not manage all wind hazards evenly across regions. This article aimed to identify ways to enhance all-hazard management of wind hazards. A structured narrative review was employed as the primary methodology, with the support of the Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses 2020 flow diagram. External hazard–oriented management (which involves managing air pollution, hurricanes, and wildfires) by international organizations as well as developed and developing countries was carefully analyz

title: Practical monitoring system for evaluating pounding risk of a skybridge under construction in a downtown area
abstract: This study proposes a practical structural health monitoring (SHM) framework for evaluating and managing pounding risk during the integral lifting of skybridges in dense urban areas. The proposed framework integrates pre-lifting numerical evaluation with construction stage real time monitoring. In the pre-lifting stage, time-series wind load data obtained from wind tunnel tests were applied to numerical time history analyses to evaluate displacement responses under representative wind-speed, wind direction, and lifting height scenarios. title: BERTRAG as a BERT-enhanced retrieval-augmented generation framework for preserving Awori and Ogu indigenous knowledge
abstract: Indigenous cultural knowledge is frequently distributed across heterogeneous and low-resource sources, including oral histories, archival records, ritual texts, community narratives, and locally produced documents. Such knowledge is often context-dependent and governed by community protocols, making it susceptible to distortion, hallucination, and loss of contextual meaning when processed using generic large language models (LLMs). title: Combined Impacts of Climate and Land-Use/Land-Cover Changes on the Flow Regime and Ecological Diversity in the Songkhram River Basin, A Tributary of the Mekong River
abstract: Abstract Climate change (CC) and land-use/land-cover (LU/LC) alterations are among the most pervasive drivers of hydrological and ecological change in river basins worldwide, yet their combined impacts on fluvial ecological diversity remain insufficiently quantified, particularly in data-scarce tropical regions. This study presents a novel integrated framework that jointly evaluates the individual and combined effects of projected CC and LU/LC change scenarios on flow regimes and aquatic ecological diversity in the Songkhram River Basin a critical tributary of the Mekong River in northeast Tha

title: Strengthening techniques for progressive collapse mitigation in RC and precast structures: a selective review and the potential of stainless-steel wire mesh
abstract: This paper presents a review of strengthening and retrofitting techniques used to improve the progressive collapse resistance of reinforced concrete (RC) and precast structural assemblies. The retrofitting strategies include fiber-reinforced polymer (FRP) systems applied as near-surface mounted and externally bonded reinforcement, steel plate systems, engineered cementitious composites and hybrid solutions. title: Laser Additive Manufacturing of Copper and Its Alloys: Challenges, Process Innovations, and Future Perspectives
abstract: Abstract Copper possesses exceptional thermal and electrical conductivity, making it valuable in applications ranging from electronics and heat exchangers to aerospace and energy systems. However, its high reflectivity, thermal conductivity, and susceptibility to oxidation present significant challenges in laser additive manufacturing (AM). This review presents a comprehensive overview of the current state of laser AM of copper and copper alloys, with a focus on laser powder bed fusion (LPBF) and laser directed energy deposition (LDED) techniques. journal: International Journal of Precision Engineering and Manufacturing-Green Technology

title: Large constructed treatment wetlands for decentralized wastewater treatment: an integrated decision-support framework for design, operation, and governance
abstract: Introduction Large treatment wetlands (TWs) can provide decentralized wastewater treatment at infrastructure scale, but successful implementation requires the integration of site conditions, wastewater characteristics, treatment-train design, operation, financing, and governance across the project lifecycle. Methods We developed an integrated decision-support framework based on a structured qualitative evidence synthesis and a comparative assessment of 64 large-scale TW projects. title: Catalyst-driven predictive functions for Fischer–Tropsch selectivity and conversion
abstract: The Fischer–Tropsch (FT) process remains a central pathway for producing low-carbon synthetic fuels from CO and CO 2 feeds, yet predicting product distributions and conversion remains challenging because operating conditions and catalyst composition interact strongly. Existing empirical correlations often rely mainly on temperature, pressure, and feed ratio, which can limit their transferability across catalyst families and reaction conditions. title: Fire‐Atmosphere Coupling Starts Upwind: Selective Redistribution of Turbulence at the Fire‐Induced Rear Inflow
abstract: Abstract Wildfires alter local atmospheric conditions, yet the spatial extent and frequency‐dependent characteristics of fire‐induced inflow perturbations remain largely unquantified. This study applies Multivariate Empirical Mode Decomposition (MEMD) to analyze high‐frequency horizontal wind speed data from a tower positioned at varying distances (∼80–410 m) upwind of three wind‐driven experimental burns in gorse shrub fuels in Rakaia Valley, New Zealand. Measurements at 3‐m, 15‐m, and 30‐m above ground level (AGL) captured rear‐inflow variability across three distinct fire‐atmosphere regimes

title: Evaluating the compatibility of predictive coding as a model of linguistic predictability effects in reading
abstract: Emerging work suggests that the computational architecture of predictive coding (PC), widely studied in visual perception, may be an appropriate model for understanding predictability effects in real-time reading (i. e., the influence of a preceding sentence context on current word processing via putative anticipatory mechanisms). We evaluated four hypotheses derived from PC models focused on: (1) bottom-up prediction error, (2) top-down sensory prediction, (3) biological plausibility, and (4) hierarchical inference. title: Energy field-assisted technology for ceramic/metal joining: a review
abstract: Joining ceramics to metals is essential for advanced composite components that combine the superior high-temperature and corrosion resistance, and the mechanical strength of ceramics, with the toughness and machinability of metals, thereby enabling applications in aerospace, electronic packaging, and thermal management. title: Nationwide economic impacts of sea level rise and storm surge from global warming in Australia
abstract: Driven by global warming and thermal expansion of the oceans, ice loss from glaciers and ice sheets will continue to increase sea levels and the risk of storm-surge, threatening coastal regions worldwide. This study presents the first national-scale assessment of SLR/S impacts on land use and assets across Australia, covering 1,156 coastal sub-regions in six states and the Northern Territory under RCP4.5 and RCP8.5 scenarios. title: Intercontinental evidence of the iconic genus Diplodocus Marsh, 1878 (Dinosauria, Sauropoda)
abstract: The sauropod Diplodocus is one of the most iconic dinosaurs, with fossils traditionally known from the Morrison Formation (U.S.A.; Kimmeridgian–Tithonian). Here, we describe a new diplodocid specimen recovered from the Villar del Arzobispo Formation (El Castellar, Teruel, Spain; upper Kimmeridgian–Tithonian). This specimen represents one of the most complete diplodocid skeletons discovered in Europe, consisting of 14 caudal vertebrae and several chevrons. title: Biofilm formation and dynamics in the marine cyanobacterium Prochlorococcus
abstract: The picocyanobacterium Prochlorococcus is responsible for ~10% of annual marine carbon fixation and plays a role in the global carbon budget. While these phototrophs are primarily considered free-living and neutrally buoyant in the euphotic zone, we observe that they can form biofilms on diverse substrates. This trait is conserved across Prochlorococcus ecotypes, and populations continuously transition between planktonic and biofilm states via a non-genetic heritable mechanism. title: Speciation of gadolinium-based contrast agents in wastewater and seawater: a case study in the northern Adriatic Sea
abstract: Coastal environments receiving treated municipal wastewater are increasingly exposed to anthropogenic gadolinium derived from gadolinium-based contrast agents (GBCAs). However, information regarding the occurrence and fate of individual GBCAs in Mediterranean marine waters remains scarce. This study investigated total gadolinium and GBCA speciation in raw and treated wastewater from an advanced wastewater treatment plant and in the receiving waters of the Gulf of Trieste (northern Adriatic Sea). title: First documentation of humpback whale (Megaptera novaeangliae) post-mortem attendance of a stillborn
abstract: Cetaceans are some of the most charismatic marine species receiving regular widespread public attention. They display highly complex behaviour including post-mortem attentive behaviour sometimes referred to as grieving behaviour. Post-mortem attentive behaviour in cetaceans has been documented predominantly among odontocetes and remains largely absent from the literature on baleen whales, limiting current understanding of the cognitive and emotional dimensions of death-related responses in mysticete cetaceans. title: A Bibliometric Analysis of Marine and Coastal Tourism Development
abstract: This study aims to analyze the evolution, structure, and research trends in global marine and coastal tourism development between 2020 and 2025, as well as to identify key research themes, influential contributors, leading countries, and collaboration networks shaping the field. A descriptive bibliometric analysis was conducted using data retrieved from the Scopus database, combining quantitative performance analysis through the Bibliometrix R package with network visualization using VOSviewer, including the application of Lotka’s Law to examine author productivity patterns. title: Redox-controlled restructuring of marine microbial ecosystems during oceanic anoxic events
abstract: Abstract During the Phanerozoic, the ocean repeatedly experienced periods of widespread deoxygenation known as oceanic anoxic events. Geological records from these events indicate a profound shift in marine microbial ecosystems. While cyanobacterial biomarkers are found broadly, those of anoxygenic photosynthetic green sulfur bacteria are restricted to upwelling regions or topographic highs. However, the quantitative mechanisms triggering this transition and the spatial heterogeneity of primary producers remain ambiguous. title: Limited atmospheric iron availability increase during the Younger Dryas in the Northern Hemisphere
abstract: Iron (Fe) availability modulates phytoplankton blooms in High-Nutrient Low-Chlorophyll (HNLC) regions, i.e., ocean areas characterized by an abundance of major nutrients but low marine productivity. Fe can be delivered to the oceans through atmospheric dust deposition, making ice cores unique archives for reconstructing past changes in aeolian Fe deposition. However, while it is known that during dustier periods atmospheric Fe depositions increased, uncertainties remain regarding the fraction of Fe actually available to phytoplankton. Satellite-Derived Relative Bathymetry Mapping of Kopa Dam Using Sentinel-2 Level-2A Imagery and GIS Techniques
abstract: Satellite-derived bathymetry (SDB) provides a remote-sensing approach for characterizing spatial variations in water depth-related information without requiring complete conventional hydrographic coverage. This study developed a relative satellite-derived bathymetry map of Kopa Dam, Tafa Local Government Area, Niger State, Nigeria, using Sentinel-2 Level-2A imagery and ArcGIS 10.8. Sentinel-2 Bands 2 and 3, representing the blue and green portions of the visible spectrum, were used to derive a logarithmic spectral-ratio called Relative Bathymetry Index (RBI). journal: African Journal of Environmental Sciences and Renewable Energy

title: Genomic separation of Salish Sea and Pacific outer coast populations of the keystone sea star Pisaster ochraceus
abstract: Environmental boundaries shape genetic diversity through the interacting effects of geographic distance, local adaptation, and constraints on gene flow. The ochre sea star (Pisaster ochraceus), an intertidal keystone predator, has long been considered to have limited spatial genetic structure along the North American Pacific coast, likely due to its extended larval dispersal period and high potential for gene flow. title: Region-specific LOI–TOC conversion models for marine sediment blue carbon assessment in the Western Irish Sea
abstract: Continental-shelf sediments (< 200 m water depth; ~ 9% of the global seafloor) store large amounts of organic carbon (OC) and accumulate OC annually, but management and accounting applications require regional evidence and transparent uncertainty. Loss-on-ignition (LOI) is a rapid, low-cost proxy for organic matter and OC, but LOI-to- total organic carbon (TOC) conversions vary with sediment type and analytical protocol. This study used multiagency Western Irish Sea data to test whether region- and sediment-specific LOI-to-TOC regressions improve OC estimation relative to a pooled conversion.

title: Lebanese faunal legacy collections uncover 400,000 years of woodland resilience and distinct hominin ecological strategies
abstract: Abstract The Levant is a key biogeographic corridor, yet historical instability has limited research creating a polarization toward its southern region. To address this geographical bias, we reassessed three legacy faunal collections from Lebanon: Naame, Nahr Ibrahim, and Ras el-Kelb. For the first time, we obtained direct dates for these assemblages and, through zooarchaeological methods, dental wear analysis, and landscape modeling, reconstructed aspects of ungulate and hominin ecology and behavior. title: Identification of Marine Borer Species on Ternate Beach, North Maluku, Indonesia
abstract: The Ternate coast is a tropical marine area characterized by warm temperatures and high salinity, supporting various marine organisms, including borers that cause wood biodeterioration. These organisms inflict severe damage on wood-based coastal infrastructure, including piers, stilt houses, and vessels. This study aimed to identify marine borer species in Ternate and determine the infested coastal wood types. title: Ultrasonic parametric investigation of a coral slab: prospects for in situ non-destructive testing of coral microatolls.
abstract: Coral microatolls are natural tide gauges whose growth records provide valuable information on long-term sea-level variations that may be linked to global climate change. At present, investigating coral microatolls requires cutting a slab with a hydraulic chain saw to analyze their growth patterns. This approach is logistically demanding, damages both the coral and the surrounding ecosystem, and is inherently destructive. title: Net ecosystem production of coral communities persisting under marginal environmental conditions
abstract: Coral communities in Hong Kong persist under a range of local stressors, including strong subtropical seasonality, chronic low light, and high turbidity, resulting in patchy, compositionally constrained communities relative to typical tropical reef systems. These challenging environmental conditions provide an opportunity to better understand how coral ecosystems may respond to changing ocean conditions in the future. title: ASSESSING WATER QUALITY FOR BLACK SEA ROMANIAN TRIBUTARIES AND COASTAL LAGOONS IN THE CONTEXT OF ARMED CONFLICT
abstract: The overlap of armed conflict-related activities with industrial and domestic human actions is raising serious environmental concerns about potential contamination in the studied area and surrounding regions. This study assessed the quality of water and sediment quality in the Razim-Sinoe lagoon complex, as well as the Danube River mouths—Sulina, Sfântul Gheorghe, and the Chilia/Bystroe—located in close proximity to the conflict zone and the ecologically sensitive Danube Delta. title: Two-stage stochastic programming for resource allocation in mobile underwater acoustic networks
abstract: Underwater Acoustic Networks (UANs) enable long-range communication for a range of applications. However, UANs are severely limited by scarce acoustic spectrum, which is shared with marine animals and can lead to disruptive interference, contributing to anthropogenic ocean noise. In addition, the underwater environment is highly dynamic, where: marine-animal presence is uncertain, channel conditions fluctuate, and Doppler effects degrade communication reliability. title: EVALUATION OF SEAWATER INTRUSION VULNERABILITY USING THE G-ALDLcR METHOD, CASE STUDY: KRUI, PESISIR BARAT, LAMPUNG
abstract: Coastal areas play a crucial role in social, economic, and ecological activities, but are vulnerable to environmental degradation due to seawater intrusion, which occurs when seawater infiltrates inland aquifers as a result of hydraulic pressure imbalances between freshwater and saltwater. Excessive groundwater exploitation leads to a decline in the water table, which in turn opens up opportunities for seawater to enter the aquifer system, thereby reducing groundwater quality in several coastal areas. title: Deep Sea hydrothermal vent habitats support gravid Antarctic krill
abstract: The long-term resilience of the Southern Ocean ecosystem relies on healthy populations of Antarctic krill, but climate change and increasing fishing pressure are placing this species at risk. Protecting Antarctic krill requires identification of key habitats for critical life history stages. Here, we present multiple lines of evidence that reproductively active female Antarctic krill utilize deep-sea hydrothermal vent habitats. title: Blue mind, healthy life and well-being: the therapeutic benefits of coastal living in Ghana
abstract: Abstract Coastal environments are traditionally characterized by relaxation and wellness but are empirically short of therapeutic research on the health value in Ghana. The blue mind concept suggests that being near water is healthy and beneficial to well-being. This qualitative study investigates the psychological, physical, and social therapeutic benefits of coastal residents living in Akosua Village, Ghana, through the Blue Mind Theory, Biophilia Hypothesis, Social Capital Theory, Therapeutic Landscapes Theory and Ostrom’s Social-Ecological Systems (SES) Framework. title: A GIS-Based Comparative Environmental Sustainability Assessment of an Underground Metro Corridor in Coastal Mumbai
abstract: Coastal cities are also experiencing growth in their urban areas, and hence the need to develop alternative and better transportation facilities. The underground metro rail is a viable alternative for the population and is also beneficial for environmental sustainability. However, there are major challenges to be addressed while constructing such facilities. For instance, excavation in such regions demands thorough analysis, and tracks cannot be laid without a thorough understanding of the regions beneath the earth’s surface. title: Epifaunal communities differ between tropical and polar mesophotic marine animal forests
abstract: Understanding marine biodiversity in polar regions remains limited compared to tropical ecosystems, where coastal habitats have been more extensively studied; however, both regions exhibit a substantial lack of knowledge regarding mesophotic marine biota. Marine Animal Forests (MAFs), key components of oceanic biodiversity, remain largely unexplored at mesophotic depths (30–200 m) due to accessibility constraints. title: Visualizing the barely detectable: Particle characteristics of the elusive aquatic gel phase in the northeastern subtropical Atlantic
abstract: Marine gels constitute a large yet poorly explored ocean carbon pool. Shadow imaging was tuned to detect particles at two sensitivity levels: high–optical density particles (HODP), resembling the particles captured by most imaging systems, and low–optical density particles (LODP), representing a vastly more abundant and gel-dominated pool. This method enabled us to map and characterize a portion of oceanic gels without filtration and staining. abstract: Endemic species are animals that are limited by geographic latitude and are not found in other locations. The Halmahera Walking Shark (Hemiscyllium halmahera) is an endemic species found in the sea of the Halmahera Islands. North Maluku, Indonesia. The research objective is the aspect of habitat connectivity that occurs based on morphometric characters. Sampling locations were Morotai Island, Kao Bay, and Tawabi Island. Kayoa. title: Cradles of the sea: a global review of shark nurseries
abstract: Conservation requires the management and protection of not only wildlife populations, but the habitats they rely on. The identification and characterization of these essential habitats is a key first step. For many sharks, nurseries increase juvenile survival and recruitment, and in this review, 443 nurseries were identified globally across 62 countries for 94 species of sharks based on an analysis of peer-reviewed literature. title: An advanced modelling study on the role of dimethyl sulfide in new particle formation in the pristine marine boundary layer
abstract: New particle formation (NPF) enhances the concentration of cloud condensation nuclei (CCN) over the oceans, thereby affecting the radiative balance and, consequently, Earth's climate. The literature suggest that marine NPF predominantly occurs in the free troposphere, as the extensive surface area of sea spray aerosols and limited precursor gases suppress NPF in the marine boundary layer (MBL). However, such interpretations do not fully account for the observations on nucleation and Aitken-mode particles within the MBL. title: Generation and Preservation of Submarine Terraces: Insights From Records Imprinted on the Topography of Dokdo Volcano
abstract: Abstract Marine terraces archive sea‐level and tectonic history, yet their relationship to individual highstands remains contentious. While most studies focus on subaerial terraces in uplifting settings, submerged terraces in subsiding settings are less explored. We develop a 1‐D wave‐erosion model and apply it to Dokdo — a subsiding volcanic island in the East Sea (a semi‐enclosed marginal sea bordered by Russia, Korea, and Japan) — using high‐resolution bathymetry to evaluate terrace generation and preservation. title: Is Gillnet Prey Subsidizing Ontogenetic Diet Shifts and Early Weaning in Common Coastal Bottlenose Dolphins From the Southwestern Gulf of Mexico?
abstract: ABSTRACT Artisanal gillnet fisheries can concentrate prey and provide incidental food subsidies to marine predators, but their effects on early‐life foraging behavior and demography remain poorly resolved. The Alvarado bottlenose dolphin population that lives off the coast of Veracruz, Mexico, is well known for having chronic, frequent, and recurring interactions with artisanal gillnet fisheries. abstract: Octocorals are vital components of tropical, temperate, and cold-water benthic marine ecosystems. Their associated microbiomes, comprising microeukaryotes, prokaryotes, and viruses, are increasingly recognised as central to host health, nutrient cycling, and chemical defence. Metagenomics and amplicon sequencing have uncovered taxonomic and functional complexity within these microbial communities, revealing patterns of host specificity and health status, along with seasonality and geographic structuring. abstract: Dar es Salaam Metropolitan City, Tanzania, faces an emerging tropical-cyclone threat because of its coastal setting, dense population, low-lying terrain, and uneven adaptive capacity. Using the Intergovernmental Panel on Climate Change framework, this study assessed vulnerability through 17 indicators grouped under exposure, sensitivity, and adaptive capacity. abstract: Abstract During a 2023 survey of higher crustacean biodiversity along the reefs of Mayotte, small fish-baited bottle traps were deployed. One of these traps contained a considerable number of a previously unknown amphipod species. Although the specimens were readily recognized as belonging to the superfamily Lysianassoidea Dana, 1849, their assignment to family and genus was initially uncertain. title: Far-Field Tsunami Observations of the 29 July 2025 Mw 8.8 Kamchatka Earthquake and Comparison with other Far-Field Tsunamis on the Mexican Pacific Coast
abstract: The Mw8.8 Kamchatka earthquake occurred offshore southern Kamchatka on July 29, 2025, generating a tsunami that propagated across the Pacific Ocean and produced a measurable sea-level disturbance along the Mexican Pacific coast. In this study, we analyze tide-gauge records along this coast to document the arrival times, duration, maximum wave-heights, and spatial variability of this far-field tsunami. In this study, we evaluated the relationships between climate-related environmental variables and the breeding distribution of the Antarctic shag ( Leucocarbo bransfieldensis ) along the Antarctic Peninsula and explored how future environmental change may affect habitat suitability by the end of the 21st century (2090–2100). abstract: ABSTRACT Biophysical processes associated with large‐scale nearshore oceanographic upwelling can influence coral reef communities by increasing the delivery of nutrient subsidies and food resources to reefs. However, these processes occur alongside anthropogenic activities that may alter ecological patterns across coral reef ecosystems. These shifts collectively modify sediment source-to-sink dynamic processes in the Arctic Ocean. While surface sediments in this semi-enclosed basin integrate complex signals from diverse Eurasian and North American source regions, disentangling these provenance signatures requires a robust, multi-proxy framework that has historically been hampered by fragmented, heterogeneous datasets. abstract: The world is experiencing notable increases in the duration, intensity and frequency of marine heatwaves (MHWs). Documented effects of MHWs on fishes encompass various population- and community-level impacts, ranging from localized mass mortalities to transient or semi-permanent range shifts, while some populations show little measurable change. abstract: With many functions attributed to drone use, different applications have been employed along the coastal environment. Most studies have focused on quantifying live and non-live cover, without measuring or quantifying species at the individual level. Thus, we proposed the Drone-Transect method, which, based on aerial images captured by drones, can identify benthic organisms on a broad spatial scale, determining abundance and spatio-temporal distribution. abstract: Abstract As coastal communities confront accelerating sea-level rise, planning practice faces a growing tension between preserving heritage and ensuring climate resilience. A critical gap exists regarding how designation practice has hampered the integration of community-defined historic places (sites whose significance is rooted in local narratives, social relationships, working landscapes, and social continuity) into local hazard resilience planning systems. title: Underwater Archaeology in Archives: Georeferencing and Spatial Validation of Archival Documentation at the Medieval Harbour of Puck (Poland)
abstract: This study presents a workflow for georeferencing legacy underwater archaeological plans from the medieval harbour in Puck (Poland) and integrating them into GIS. Archival drawings from the 1980s and 1990s, based on different local grids, were digitised, spatially reconstructed and validated against multibeam echosounder (MBES) data with RTK positioning. abstract: With its abundance of minerals identified as essential for the green transition, the ocean floor is regarded by Deep-Sea Mining (DSM) proponents as the new “green frontier” of resource extraction. This framing of DSM is particularly significant for the Pacific Island Countries (PICs), which are positioned at the geographic center of DSM pursuits. abstract: Evidence-informed architectural heritage planning requires a robust understanding of long-term urban morphogenesis. This paper reconstructs the spatial evolution of Bejaia (Bougie), Algeria, from 1833 to 1962 and tests how diachronic Geographic Information System (GIS)-based indicators can substantiate safeguarding priorities in Mediterranean coastal historic centres. title: Observational Evidence for Accelerated Warming and Salinification Propagating Into the Deep Mediterranean
abstract: Abstract Acceleration, rather than a gradual linear response, is emerging as a defining feature of ocean change in the Anthropocene. Surface‐forced warming propagates into the deep ocean over decades to centuries, but semi‐enclosed basins such as the Mediterranean Sea may respond more rapidly. Here, we analyse an in situ Mediterranean‐wide multiplatform data set spanning 1950–2025 and show that warming and salinification of the upper 1,000–2,000 m are not only continuing but accelerating, at increasing rates over the record. title: Bacterial inoculation elicits changes to the coral epigenome
abstract: Environmental shifts can cause epigenetic modifications in corals associated with changes in gene expression and physiology, although it remains unclear if associated bacteria can also induce such changes. Here, we inoculate nubbins of the coral Pocillopora verrucosa with an opportunistic pathogen, Vibrio coralliilyticus, and/or a coral probiotic, Cobetia sp., and subject the nubbins to heat stress. abstract: Abstract Recent oligotrophication and rising water temperatures in the Seto Inland Sea of Japan have led to a decline in oyster production in Hiroshima Prefecture. This study developed and evaluated the “Seawater Pump-up Apparatus for Localized Oceanic Warming-mitigation” (SPALOW), a device designed to supply cool and nutrient-rich bottom water and diatom resting cells from the sediment to the surface layer. title: Ant Diversity of the Xisha Islands: Community Structure, Exotic Species Colonization, and Ecological Functions in a Tropical Coral Archipelago
abstract: ABSTRACT The Xisha Islands in the South China Sea are a typical tropical coral archipelago at the forefront of global climate change and anthropogenic disturbance, yet their ant diversity and ecological functions remain uncharacterized. In this study, we systematically surveyed ants across seven islands, integrating morphological identification with molecular species delimitation (based on COI barcodes, with ABGD, ASAP, and bPTP methods) to compile the species inventory, and analyzed the effects of island geographic traits, anthropogenic disturbance, and vegetation type on ant communities. title: Immersive human–computer interaction simulation and emergency buoyancy control of submerged body in the South China Sea internal solitary wave
abstract: Oceanic internal solitary waves (ISWs) produce strong nonlinear variations in density stratification and flow fields, posing considerable risks to submerged body navigation. In this study, high-resolution ISW data in the South China Sea were simulated using the Massachusetts Institute of Technology General Circulation Model (MITgcm), and a continuous three-dimensional visualization of ISWs was developed based on isopycnal depth extraction. abstract: BACKGROUND: Talaromyces C. R. Benj., is a large and taxonomically important genus within Ascomycota, established to accommodate the teleomorphs of certain Penicillium Link, species and is now recognized as a monophyletic lineage distinct from Penicillium. abstract: ABSTRACT Uranium extraction from seawater represents a vital route for exploring non‐conventional uranium resources. Enhancing the mass transfer performance and antifouling capabilities, and constructing synergistic promotion are crucial for improving adsorption efficiency and durability of uranium extraction materials in large‐scale marine tests. Herein, a novel adsorbent PAO‐G‐SBMA was developed by introducing zwitterion and polyguanidine groups into polyamidoxime fibers. title: Feeling the noise: behavioural responses in ascidians are associated with substrate-borne vibrations rather than sound pressure alone
abstract: Abstract Marine anthropogenic noise pollution has increased substantially in recent decades, raising concerns about its effects on marine organisms. While research has primarily focused on marine mammals and – to a smaller extent – on fish, comparatively little is known about how sessile benthic invertebrates perceive and respond to underwater vibroacoustic stimuli. abstract: Abstract Increasing larval settlement can substantially accelerate coral reef restoration by overcoming a key bottleneck in coral population recovery. Successful settlement depends on biological and chemical cues associated with microbial biofilms and crustose coralline algae that are often reduced or absent on degraded reefs. title: Respiratory virology dashboards for primary care and public health insight in England
abstract: BACKGROUND: Effective community surveillance of respiratory diseases relies on the timely collection and analysis of high quality clinical and virology data. The aim was to develop interactive dashboards for general practice, public health, and researcher groups. This would improve the visualisation, utilisation, and quality of virology data from an English sentinel network, support disease trend monitoring, early outbreak response, and thereby reduce poor health outcomes and their societal impact. abstract: ABSTRACT Bangladesh's coastal zones face compounding threats from climate change, sea-level rise, and the resulting intensification of salinity intrusion, critically jeopardizing freshwater security, agriculture, and local livelihoods. This study presents a spatial multi-criteria analysis using a Geographic Information System (GIS) integrated with the Analytic Hierarchy Process (AHP) to systematically assess and map the hazard, vulnerability, and exposure dimensions driving flood-induced salinity intrusion risk in Satkhira District. abstract: The Comoé Estuary, located in Grand-Bassam, Côte d'Ivoire, is a coastal ecosystem of major ecological and socio-economic importance. Since the permanent opening of its mouth in September 2023, the estuary has experienced hydrological and environmental disturbances whose magnitude remains poorly documented. abstract: Carijoa riisei is a branching colonial octocoral widely distributed in reef and estuarine environments along the coast of Pernambuco, northeastern Brazil. Owing to the structural complexity of its colonies, it provides both habitat and substrate for a diverse assemblage of associated organisms. This study investigated the structure of the amphipod community associated with C. riisei in two contrasting environments on the southern coast of Pernambuco: Porto de Galinhas Beach and the Rio Formoso Estuary. abstract: Floods can be very destructive natural hazard; it causes significant environmental, social, and economic impacts. title: The contribution of marine benthic habitats for maintaining fish biodiversity
abstract: Abstract Elucidating how biodiversity is distributed across marine habitats is essential to guide conservation efforts at a time of unprecedented anthropogenic impacts. However, the relative importance of different benthic habitats for maintaining fish biodiversity remains unclear because studies have typically focused on a single marine substrate. title: Dynamic emperor penguin colonies
abstract: Abstract Understanding how species respond to environmental change is critical for predicting their resilience to future climate impacts. For emperor penguins, relocation of breeding colonies may provide an important mechanism for coping with changing sea ice conditions. Using medium and very high-resolution satellite imagery, we study penguin colony locations in West Antarctica and show that five colonies have moved significant distances over the last decade. abstract: Coastal areas play a strategic role and possess significant potential in achieving national economic development goals. However, economic development in coastal regions faces various challenges, including limited knowledge regarding sustainable development roadmaps for these areas. This study aimed to develop a conceptual hierarchical model to guide coastal economic development based on the Natural Resources-Based View and Blue Growth approaches. abstract: This study analyzes the spatial patterns of marine vessel accidents, examines their determinants, and forecasts future casualties along inland waterways in Rivers State, Nigeria. The study adopts a retrospective longitudinal research design integrating Geographic Information Systems (GIS), statistical techniques, and time-series forecasting. abstract: High-precision real-time observation of sea surface height and wave parameters is essential for maritime safety, offshore engineering, disaster warning, and marine resource development. However, studies focusing on the capacity for governance in relation to the development of blue economy development policies are scarce. abstract: Understanding migratory connectivity is important for conserving highly mobile marine species facing escalating threats. Establishing baseline information on migratory connectivity is necessary for identifying species and regions requiring transboundary cooperation for their conservation. abstract: Abstract Grey seals in German waters harbour a diverse array of parasites, including the endoparasitic nasal mite Halarachne halichoeri , which underwent a long evolutionary parasite-host adaption in the marine environment. abstract: Between 2015 and 2024, a series of five shipborne gravimetry campaigns was conducted within the German exclusive economic zone of the North Sea and adjacent waters. title: From sea to farm: Repurposing invasive macroalgae into biocidal and defense-enhancing tools against tomato late blight (Phytophthora infestans)
abstract: Marine seaweeds are increasingly recognized as sources of bioactive compounds with potential applications in sustainable agriculture, including as biocontrol agents. The selection of invasive species such as Asparagopsis armata and Sargassum muticum offers a dual benefit: obtaining bioactive metabolites from a low-cost resource while simultaneously mitigating their ecological impacts using this harmful biomass.
