title: Determinants of behavioral intentions to reduce single-use plastic among Rohingya refugees in Bangladesh using an extended theory of planned behavior model
abstract: Despite the growing recognition of single-use plastic (SUP) pollution as a substantial environmental challenge, there is limited understanding of the behavioral and socio-demographic factors influencing individuals’ intentions to reduce SUP usage, particularly in refugee populations. This study investigated the determinants of behavioral intentions (BI) to reduce SUP usage among the Rohingya refugee population in Cox’s Bazar, Bangladesh, using an extended Theory of Planned Behavior (TPB) model. A total of 304 respondents from 15 refugee camps were surveyed through face-to-face interviews. Part

title: Post With Care: How Language Use Influences the Effectiveness of CEOs' Climate‐Related Messages on Social Media
abstract: ABSTRACT Chief executive officers (CEOs) play a pivotal role in shaping public discourse on climate change through social media, yet how their language use affects the effectiveness of climate‐related posts remains unclear. Drawing on schema‐congruity theory and leader role expectations, we conceptualize certainty in language as congruent and anxiety as incongruent CEO language. Using automated text analysis of 5544 posts on X by 50 CEOs of Global Fortune 500 companies, we examine how (in)congruent language use influences public engagement and how climate content moderates these effects. title: Waterbird Diversity as an Indicator of Ecosystem Sustainability in Kuala Bubon Mangrove Forest Indonesia
abstract: The Kuala Bubon mangrove ecosystem in West Aceh serves as an important habitat for various waterbird species that are highly sensitive to environmental changes, making them reliable indicators of ecosystem sustainability. This study aims to assess waterbird diversity and identify dominant species as a basis for evaluating the ecological condition of the mangroves. Observations were conducted at six points using point count and transect line methods during July–August 2023. title: A network analysis of failure pathways for fish and fish habitat offsets
abstract: Abstract Biodiversity offsets are a primary tool to compensate for environmental impacts, especially in aquatic ecosystems, yet a comprehensive understanding of the factors that lead to aquatic offset failure is lacking. We address this gap by identifying co‐occurrence patterns among the direct failures and indirect consequences, restoration methods, and risk‐reduction strategies in aquatic ecosystems, specifically for fish and fish habitat. title: Cave gudgeon (Milyeringa spp.) eDNA assay for rapid detection in the dark
abstract: Australia has two eyeless cave gudgeons ( Milyeringa justitia and M. veritas ) which are restricted to subterranean waters and listed as vulnerable and endangered. Despite being a priority conservation target species, they are inadequately monitored as their restricted distribution in groundwater ecosystems impedes conventional surveying methods, constraining effective monitoring and conservation. As part of ongoing efforts to improve monitoring and conservation of these subterranean fish species, we developed and validated a genus-specific eDNA assay for detecting species of Milyeringa . title: Microplastic and potentially toxic element Co-contamination in semi-arid agricultural and peri-urban soils of Tamansourt (Marrakech Region, Morocco)
abstract: Microplastics (MPs) are an emerging soil contaminant, whereas potentially toxic elements (PTEs) are long-recognized persistent pollutants; their co-occurrence and potential interactions in terrestrial ecosystems are of growing concern. In semi-arid regions such as Marrakech (Morocco), where wastewater reuse and plastic-intensive agriculture are common, their accumulation in soils may pose long-term ecological risks. title: Global Research Trends on Mining Activities and Environmental Impacts
abstract: This study utilized the Scopus database to examine 2,626 publications published between 2014 and 2024, involving 7,712 authors from 797 different sources, with an annual growth rate of 11.48%, focusing on the environmental impacts of mining activities. The analysis revealed the evolution of scientific research over time by identifying the most influential journals, as well as the most active countries, while highlighting the core concepts that define this research field. title: BiOS: An open-source framework for the integration of heterogeneous biodiversity data
abstract: The era of Big Data has reshaped biodiversity and ecological research. Nevertheless, much of the potential held within these data is still constrained by their heterogeneity, database-incompatible schemas, and fragmentation of resources. abstract: Since 2020, Iberian orcas have repeatedly interacted with sailing vessels, often targeting rudders. These well-documented interactions have been discussed primarily as play, exploration, maladaptation, or a product of cultural transmission. Here, I argue for a complementary interpretation. This phenomenon also exposes a broader explanatory issue in animal cognition: complex animal behavior in the wild is often described without an explicit theory of action. title: Regulation of interfacial microstructure and mechanical properties of CuNi/X65 cladding fabricated by pulsed GTAW
abstract: Direct fusion of corrosion-resistant copper–nickel (CuNi) cladding to X65 steel can cause Fe–Cu intermixing, segregation, and interface-associated cracking. This study comparatively evaluates whether an ERNiCu-7 transition layer regulates the interface more effectively than preheating/slow cooling under otherwise comparable pulsed gas tungsten arc welding conditions. title: Spatial and temporal patterns of ichthyoplankton assemblages across a large flow-regulated Amazonian river system
abstract: Abstract Dams may significantly affect fish reproduction and the natural drift of ichthyoplankton. Here, we investigated fish egg and larval dynamics in the area affected by the Belo Monte Dam. Ichthyoplankton was surveyed daily during an entire flood-pulse cycle, across three sectors: upstream of the main reservoir (UP), within the reservoir (MR), and in the reduced-flow sector (RF) downstream of the dam. abstract: Functional Group V (FG V), which comprises anoxygenic phototrophic purple and green sulfur bacteria, has traditionally been associated with stratified lakes, where pronounced vertical redox gradients are typically described. Here, we report the repeated occurrence of anoxygenic phototrophic sulfur bacteria in two shallow riparian wetlands, suggesting that the ecological context of this functional group may extend beyond classical stratified systems. title: Amphibious Movement of Microrobots Inspired by Water Spiders
abstract: Magnetic actuation provides an effective means for tetherless control of microrobots in complex environments. Inspired by the morphology and interfacial flotation mechanism of water striders, we design a four-legged microrobot with small ribs on its feet to mimic the structure of water striders. Through an asymmetric magnetic response between its poles inside four legs, two bio-inspired motion modes and three extended modes are controlled by the magnetic field during complex amphibious locomotion. title: Seasonal and hydrological dynamics of pharmaceutical occurrence and risk in a mixed-use subtropical river basin: insights from the Fortaleza River, Southern Brazil
abstract: Abstract This study provides the first evaluation of pharmaceutical contaminants in the Fortaleza River sub-basin, southern Brazil, a mixed agro-urban watershed characterized by overlapping domestic and agricultural pressures. Surface water samples were collected during three sampling campaigns conducted in December 2023, January 2024, and February 2024. title: Managed aquifer recharge for climate adaptation in Somalia: Opportunities, barriers, and a roadmap toward water security
abstract: Groundwater sustains most rural and urban water supply across Somalia, yet it remains poorly mapped, weakly regulated, and increasingly stressed by rising demand and erratic rainfall. Managed aquifer recharge, a set of techniques that deliberately directs surplus water underground for later use, offers a way to turn seasonal floodwater into a stored buffer against dry seasons. title: Microbial diversity of camel milk production environments in Xinjiang, China: a full-length 16S rRNA survey of farm environmental matrices across Altay and Hami regions
abstract: Introduction Camel milk production in Xinjiang, China is predominantly managed under extensive pastoral systems, yet the taxonomic and functional profiles of key production-associated environmental matrices remain poorly characterized. Methods This study employed PacBio Single-Molecule Real-Time (SMRT) full-length 16S rRNA gene sequencing to characterize microbial communities across five environmental matrices (bedding, feces, teat skin, feed, and soil) from camel breeding farms in the Altay and Hami regions of Xinjiang. title: Effects of temperature and density on mercury accumulation in Atlantic salmon ( Salmo salar )
abstract: Environmental temperature is a master variable governing growth and metabolism of fishes in aquatic food webs, which in turn influences the flow and accumulation of trace elements, including toxic forms of mercury (Hg). Growth can be influenced by population density, with high densities consistently associated with lower growth rates. title: Impact of Flooding on Practical Agricultural Training Delivery: Resilience Strategies for Vocational Education in Bayelsa State
abstract: Flooding remains one of the most devastating environmental challenges affecting Bayelsa State, with far-reaching implications on agricultural education and skills development. As a low-lying, riverine state, recurring floods disrupt practical agricultural training, hinder access to farmlands, damage infrastructure, and compromise learning outcomes. title: Mixed microbial consortia combined with low-cost electrodes synergistically enhance the performance of bioelectrochemical systems
abstract: Microbial Fuel Cells (MFCs) have gained significant attention as a sustainable technology for simultaneous wastewater treatment and bioelectricity generation via the metabolic activity of electroactive microorganisms. This study focused on the design and optimization of a laboratory-scale dual-chamber MFC to enhance its electrical performance. The system was constructed using graphite electrodes, a proton exchange membrane, and a mixed microbial consortium obtained from anaerobic sludge that was used as the biocatalyst in the anodic chamber. title: Directional Erosion and Weathering Analysis Using Digital 3D Model Surfaces: A Free and Open Add-On for Calculating Recession Amounts with Blender™
abstract: Abstract This paper describes a methodology based on a software tool to optimize the analysis of the erosion of historic monuments and to quantify its extent and distribution. It applies to the digital models of monuments, generated either with photogrammetry or Lidar data. The tool is an add-on for Blender™, a popular and free software for 3D editing. Before running it, the user is expected to generate a surface representing the theoretical original surface of the monument, in contact with the areas of the monument not affected by erosion. title: Isotope analysis reveals mobility of the earliest cattle herds in northern Europe
abstract: Abstract Human mobility was intrinsic to the farming communities of the Linear Pottery culture (c. 5500 − 4900 BCE). Much less is known about the mobility patterns of the earliest farmers north of the Linear Pottery zone, particularly in the Netherlands. Here, people of the Early Neolithic Swifterbant culture combined farming, hunting and gathering from c. 4240 BCE. While human remains for mobility studies are scarce, livestock offer a promising yet underexplored proxy. title: Bacterial succession and formation of aggregates on roots following indoor willow growth in sand
abstract: Various willow species are used for stabilization of slopes and dunes in different climatic conditions due to their resilience and ability to form new roots on cuttings. From existing studies, it is unclear if the soil stabilizing effect is driven by mechanical root enmeshment or due to chemical changes following root growth. The objective of this study was to investigate how the chemical and microbiological properties of sand change during willow growth, and how this contributes to the structural transformation of root-reinforced sand. title: Aligning stakeholders’ perceptions, policy and practice towards sustainability: Evidence from the EU Transition Pathway for Tourism
abstract: This paper examines how the perceptions of tourism experts are reflected in the discourse and implementation of European sustainable tourism policy—an aspect that has received limited attention in tourism policy research. To bridge the gap between stakeholder perspectives, policy discourse, and practice, the study develops and applies an exploratory methodological framework based on a dual alignment analysis. title: Integrated geochemistry, geostatistics, and sedimentology to identify potential gold-bearing zones at Bipindi, southern Cameroon
abstract: This study integrates petrography, sedimentology, stream-sediment geochemistry, and exploratory geostatistical modelling to assess gold dispersion in the Bipindi area, southern Cameroon. The work addresses the limited constraints on the spatial distribution of Au in a small alluvial system developed on the northwestern margin of the Congo Craton. The exposed basement comprises pyroxene-epidote gneisses, amphibolites, and quartzites. institutions: Institut de Recherches Géologiques et Minières

title: REDUCTIONS IN ENGINE EXHAUST EMISSIONS IN A HYBRID FLETTNER ROTOR POWER-ASSISTED VESSEL
abstract: With the increase of Greenhouse Gas (GHG) emissions, the maritime industry has seen an influx of low emission and environmental protection solutions to reduce the GHG-, Hydrocarbon (HC)-, Nitrogen oxides (NOx)-, Sulphur oxides (SOx)-, and particulate matter (PM) emissions. The Flettner rotor is a technology that utilizes wind and the Magnus effect to generate lift for propulsion assist of the vessel. title: Chondrichthyan cartilage: new discoveries in morphology and the composition of the extracellular matrix
abstract: Many chondrichthyans, or cartilaginous fishes with skeletons made entirely of cartilage and known for their regenerative abilities, inhabit high-hydrostatic-pressure environments. We hypothesise that basic research on chondrichthyan cartilage will fill knowledge gaps currently holding back progress in cartilage tissue engineering. title: Microplastic behaviors and ecological risks in extreme arid hypersaline ecosystems: Qarhan Salt Lake on the Qinghai-Tibet Plateau
abstract: Although numerous studies have examined microplastic (MP) environmental exposure and contaminant characteristics, understanding of MP pollution in extreme saline environments remains limited. This study systematically investigated the distribution, migration, and potential ecological risks of MPs in the ultra-saline Qarhan Salt Lake, where intensive resource development occurs. MPs were widely detected, with higher abundances concentrated in the core industrial zones, including factories, salt ponds, and the eastern shore of Dabuson Lake. title: Environmental vulnerability and governance in the Red River Delta, Vietnam: analysis and strategic recommendations
abstract: Environmental vulnerability in deltaic regions is increasingly associated with governance failures rather than biophysical exposure alone. This study aims to examine how institutional arrangements shape household environmental vulnerability in Vietnam’s Red River Delta. An integrated mixed-methods approach was employed, combining household surveys (n = 1,000) across three provinces (Hanoi, Hung Yen, and Nam Dinh) using an adapted Household Vulnerability Assessment Tool (HVAT) with qualitative policy document analysis Results reveal that food security vulnerability (CVI2 = 0.245) is elevated ac

title: A multicriteria assessment of rural reservoir landscape performance using stakeholder evaluations in Banshan Village, China
abstract: Rural reservoirs increasingly function as multifunctional landscape systems, yet methods for assessing their ecological, environmental, economic, and social performance remain limited. This study assessed the performance of the rural reservoir landscape as a stakeholder-rated, multidimensional construct in Banshan Village, Xuzhou, China. Field observations and secondary sources informed indicator selection and interpretation but were not used for numerical scoring. title: The Misunderstood Risk of Mineral Raw Materials. A lithium and cobalt case study
abstract: As the transition to a low-carbon economy accelerates, the mineral raw materials supply chain is being severely strained. Ensuring a clean energy supply chain entails a comprehensive assessment of various factors that are not always properly weighed. The risks involved in ensuring access to critical raw materials are not only confined to the natural world in terms of geological conditions or geographical distribution. title: Characterizing long-term trends and spatiotemporal dynamics of ambient gamma radiation dose rates alongside exploratory meteorological factors
abstract: Ambient gamma radiation constitutes an important component of environmental background radiation and is crucial for evaluating public exposure. In China, a nationwide survey conducted between 1983 and 1990 established the baseline for ambient gamma air-absorbed dose rates, with a nationwide range of 2.4-340.8 nGy/h. However, long-term spatiotemporal variations remain poorly documented due to limited publicly available monitoring data. title: Assessing a low-dose copper treatment for dreissenid mussels: Effects on zebra mussel (Dreissena polymorpha) population
abstract: We conducted and evaluated a low-dose copper treatment (applied as EarthTec QZ) to suppress zebra mussel (Dreissena polymorpha Pallas 1771) veliger abundance and settlement in a 66.3 ha bay in Lake Minnetonka (Hennepin County, MN) over a 3-y period. We maintained a mean (standard deviation [SD]) concentration of 83.0 (10.3) µg/L as copper over the 10-d treatment period, much lower than the maximum allowable 1 mg/L as copper. title: Environmental aging and ecotoxicological evaluation of jute cellulose-based biodegradable biopolymer (Sonali Bag®): A potential sustainable alternative to single-use plastics
abstract: Biodegradable biopolymers are increasingly promoted as sustainable alternatives to single-use plastics due to their renewable origins, degradability, and potential to mitigate plastic pollution. However, concerns regarding their degradation products and ecological effects highlight the need to evaluate their environmental aging and ecotoxicity prior to large-scale adoption. title: The projected risk of plant invasions on the peri‐Antarctic islands under climate change
abstract: The peri‐Antarctic islands have largely been shielded from alien plant species due to low human pressure, limited introduction pathways, and local harsh climates. However, climate change is expected to lower these barriers. We assess the vulnerability of 12 peri‐Antarctic islands to invasion by 2220 plant species invasive in at least one region of the globe by projecting their climatic suitability under recent climate (1981–2010) and three future (2071–2100) climate change scenarios, ranging from mild to severe. title: Aquifer characterization and parameter estimation using surface geophysical method in Haramaya well field, Eastern Ethiopia
abstract: Groundwater is the primary source of water supply for over three hundred thousand people in Harar town and its environs since 2004/2005 with the demise of Lake Haramaya. Drilling of wells in the area has therefore started as an emergency water supply without good understanding of the aquifer system. This study was thus initiated to understand the full nature of the hydrogeological set up and hydraulic properties of the aquifer system. title: Cladocera responses to ~200-year history of environmental stressors on Rideau Canal (Ontario, Canada) lakes
abstract: Five lakes within the Rideau Canal system (Ontario, Canada) were studied ~25 years ago using lake sediment cores for diatom analysis. More recently, new sediment cores were collected to assess limnological changes linked to more contemporary stressors, such as accelerated regional climate warming. However, long-term changes in the cladoceran assemblages remained unstudied in the earlier collections. title: Chromosome-scale genomes and population resequencing resolve subgenome diversity and halophyte adaptation in Salicornia
abstract: Amid escalating water scarcity and groundwater depletion, halophytes such as Salicornia (Amaranthaceae) represent valuable models for extreme salt tolerance and hold promise for saltwater-based agriculture. Here, we show chromosome-scale genome assemblies for six Salicornia species, revealing four distinct subgenomes, reconciling our assemblies with two existing reference genomes (S. ramosissima UK and S. europaea China), correcting chromosome numbering and orientation. title: Plastic and Anthropogenic Particles in the Reproductive Tissues of Feral and Domestic Felines
abstract: Feral and domestic felines are continuously exposed to meso- (polymer length: 5-25 mm) and microplastics (polymer length < 5 mm) from environmental or household contaminants. Ingestion and inhalation are the primary pathways for internalization of plastic, non-plastic anthropogenic (e.g., rayon, AP), and natural cellulose particles. However, contamination information is limited for companion animals. title: Time dependent assessment of glacier recession in the Indian Central Himalaya
abstract: In recent decades, the Himalayan cryosphere has been subject to significant changes as a consequence of regional climate warming. The glaciers within the Indian Central Himalayas are vital to the maintenance of the major river systems of South Asia and are sensitive indicators of climate change. Various studies have reported considerable glacier recession, thinning, and mass loss within the region, though the extent and velocity of change vary considerably among glaciers because of climatic and topographic conditions. title: REPURPOSING THE VESSEL EXPERIENCE FACTOR AS A STATISTICAL PROCESS CONTROL TOOL FOR TANKER CARGO MEASUREMENT
abstract: Accurate reconciliation of cargo quantities measured on board a tanker with those declared by shore terminals is central to reliable tanker operations and to the prevention of commercial disputes. The Vessel Experience Factor (VEF), provides a historical, vessel-specific relationship between shipboard and shore measurements and is traditionally used as a cargo-reconciliation and loss-control tool. abstract: Parametric roll is a nonlinear ship-motion instability triggered when the encounter frequency approaches twice the natural roll frequency, causing periodic modulation of restoring moment and possible amplification to large roll angles. This paper develops and exploits a compact, one-degree-of-freedom roll model to numerically detect the principal nonlinear phenomena associated with parametric roll in a modern containership. title: Comparative evaluation of socioeconomic vulnerability assessment methods for disaster risk reduction: Evidence from a national-scale assessment in India
abstract: Hydro-climatic hazards in India are intensifying, amplifying socioeconomic disruption and regional inequalities, consistent with IPCC AR5 and AR6 assessments. However, existing socioeconomic vulnerability (SEV) assessments remain methodologically inconsistent and insufficiently evaluated, limiting their usefulness for disaster risk reduction and risk governance. title: Holocene summer and winter temperature trends and excursions in East-Central Europe from Carpathian pollen records
abstract: This study reconstructs summer and winter temperatures for East-Central Europe (ECE) over the last 12 ka using pollen records from five mid-altitude sites in the Carpathian Mountains. Seasonal reconstructions were combined into composite records and statistically evaluated to identify significant long-term trends and short-term excursions. title: Quantifying microplastics in native and farmed fish: Evidence from Orestias agassii and Oncorhynchus mykiss in Lake Titicaca
abstract: Orestias agassii (black carachi) and Oncorhynchus mykiss (rainbow trout) are key fish species in the diet of local populations surrounding Lake Titicaca. However, recent studies have raised concern about the presence of microplastics (MPs) in this high-altitude aquatic ecosystem. Hence, this study aimed to quantify MPs in the gastrointestinal tracts of black carachi and rainbow trout from the Chucuito and Uros Chulluni areas of Lake Titicaca. title: Effect of soil sampling methods on physical soil parameters and carbon stock in Madagascar’s open ecosystems
abstract: Soil organic carbon (SOC) storage is fundamental for climate change mitigation and food security and more precise and detailed SOC stock data are required to accurately assess the main ecological functions on climate regulation. However, soil sampling for SOC stock assessment is labor-intensive when conducted according to international standards using the cylinder method for measuring bulk density (BD) and coarse fragment (CF) which are key components of SOC stock. title: Internet of Smart Environment (IOSE) and Pollution Monitoring in Nigeria
abstract: This study examined the relationship between Internet of Smart Environment (IOSE) and Pollution monitoring in Nigeria. Specifically, it explored the relationships between environmental monitoring and data analytics, environmental monitoring and pollution control measures, energy efficiency and data analytics, and energy efficiency and pollution control measures. abstract: 3D reconstruction of sites and objects using devices equipped with LiDAR scanners is becoming increasingly popular. However, the costs associated with purchasing such equipment remain very high. For this reason, consumer mobile devices such as the iPhone, into which Apple Inc. has been integrating LiDAR sensors since 2020, are worth considering. title: Ecological risk assessment and spatial distribution of heavy metals in soils surrounding urban abattoir waste systems in southwestern Nigeria
abstract: This study investigated the accumulation and ecological risk of heavy metals in soils surrounding a major open dumpsite adjacent to the New Abattoir in Akerebiata Harmony Estate, Ilorin, Southwestern Nigeria. title: “Space-sky-ground-Lake” four-dimensional monitoring technology for water quality in Baiyangdian - a new model for future environmental monitoring
abstract: The “Space-Sky-Ground-Lake” four-dimensional integrated water quality monitoring system in Xiong'an New Area, represents a significant innovation in environmental monitoring. By combining satellite remote sensing, unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs), unmanned ships, and automatic water quality monitoring stations, the system achieves comprehensive, three-dimensional oversight of Baiyangdian's water quality. title: Rooted Currents: Research-through-design for regenerative urbanism in Changzhou Island
abstract: Changzhou Island in Guangzhou’s Pearl River Delta represents a site of both cultural significance and environmental vulnerability, facing increasing pressures from flooding, rapid urbanization, and the erosion of Lingnan architectural heritage. This article reframes the award-winning design proposal of the student competition Rooted Currents as a research-through-design (RTD) inquiry into regenerative urbanism in deltaic environments. abstract: This paper presents preliminary results of a development-led archaeological investigation conducted in the Bay of Greifswald, Mecklenburg-Vorpommern, Germany, which led to the identification of a previously unknown shipwreck site. The site was accidentally discovered in 2023 during pre-construction works for the LNG pipeline. title: Management shapes sustainable aquaculture across environmental and social outcomes
abstract: As global aquaculture production continues to increase rapidly, there is growing interest in strengthening aquaculture’s performance across multiple sustainability dimensions. However, there has been limited effort to understand the link between different governance factors and the multiple objectives of sustainability, as well as the relative importance of different factors. title: Comparative genomics and tadpole intestinal metabarcoding suggest a potential cyanobacteria-amphibian trophic link in hot-spring ecosystems
abstract: Hot-springs are accessible yet extreme environments for studying thermophilic microbial communities and their ecological interactions. Here, we isolated and characterized two thermophilic filamentous Leptolyngbya -related cyanobacterial strains, Akita and Seranma, from geothermal hot springs in Japan. The two strains differed in morphology and pigmentation: L. sp. Akita formed linear blue-green filaments, whereas L. sp. Seranma formed loosely coiled brown filaments. title: Returning an extirpated native carnivore to its former range: a habitat suitability analysis of Kangaroo Island for spotted-tailed quolls (Dasyurus maculatus)
abstract: Native predators have declined significantly in range and abundance globally. In Australia, the spotted-tailed quoll's (Dasyurus maculatus) range has contracted by up to 30% since Europeans arrived in the late 1700s, with its extirpation from Kangaroo Island sometime after 1837. A feral cat eradication program is currently underway on Kangaroo Island which, if successful, will leave a vacant predator niche. title: A CELESTIAL NAVIGATION APPROACH TO SALAH TIMEKEEPING FOR SEAFARERS
abstract: Ensuring religious practices on board ships is essential for the wellbeing of practicing seafarers. Around 18% of seafarers on board merchant ships are Muslim, and practicing seafarers perform Salah – five prayers a day. The prayers must be performed at appointed times during the day, times which depend on the movement of the sun; this is why astronomy is essential for the Islamic world. title: The place bonding potential of nature‐based citizen science with refugee children and youth
abstract: Abstract Nature‐based citizen science often involves close interaction with places. In addition to providing benefits, such as learning opportunities and contact with nature, it can facilitate and shape bonds between people and places. Research exploring the place bonding potential of such projects is still in its infancy. This paper addresses this gap by exploring nature‐based citizen science with youth who are temporarily displaced due to the war in Ukraine. title: Genomic detection of highly pathogenic avian influenza H5N1 in Antarctic seabirds reveals connectivity with South American viral lineages
abstract: Emerging avian viruses increasingly threaten Antarctic wildlife, raising concerns about ecosystem health and biodiversity. In this study, we conducted a comprehensive investigation of avian influenza virus (influenza A virus, IAV) in both resident and migratory birds inhabiting the South Shetland Islands, Antarctica. During the 2024-2025 austral summer, 278 samples were collected and screened using real-time RT-PCR targeting the IAV M gene. title: Complex Network Analysis of Urban Road Systems: A Case Study of Bandar Lampung, Indonesia
abstract: Urban road networks can be examined as complex systems in which the arrangement of intersections and road segments determines how different parts of a city are connected. The Bandar Lampung road network is treated as a directed graph derived from OpenStreetMap data. The largest weakly connected component contains 23,920 nodes and 58,492 directed edges, with a density of 0.000102 and an average total directed degree of 4.89. title: Mechanism study of low-ambient-pressure effects on the efficiency of cavitation erosion mitigation by air bubbles in gas-liquid two-phase flow
abstract: Ambient pressure variations alter cavitation bubble dynamics, thereby affecting cavitation erosion on solid boundaries and the efficiency of aeration-based mitigation. In this study, the cavitation erosion mitigation efficiency and underlying mechanisms of entrained air bubbles in gas-liquid two-phase flow under varying ambient pressures were systematically investigated by combining macroscopic investigation and mesoscopic analysis. title: Differential inactivation of microalgae and cyanobacteria by UV-C and hydrogen peroxide treatments in natural freshwater communities
abstract: Aquatic ecosystems provide water for multiple purposes and serve as venues for recreational activities. However, the phytoplankton community in these ecosystems may be a source of economic and health problems, particularly during episodes of harmful algal and cyanobacterial blooms. These episodes are especially concerning when involving potentially toxic cyanobacteria. title: From immature to mature epithelium: unveiling structural dynamics and transcriptional programs in rainbow trout intestinal barrier
abstract: Abstract The intestinal epithelium is crucial for nutrient absorption, immune defense, and barrier function in farmed fish. However, the molecular mechanisms underlying its development and maturation in salmonids remain poorly characterized, hindering our ability to address pervasive gut health challenges in aquaculture. In this study, we use the RTgutGC cell line to implement an epithelial maturation model with the aim of characterizing the global transcriptional program in rainbow trout ( Oncorhynchus mykiss ). title: The colorless dictyochophyte Ciliophrys sp. Baltic has lost a plastid but hosts a bacterial endosymbiont
abstract: Organelle loss represents an extreme case of reductive evolution, with very few cases of plastid elimination known in free-living ancestrally photosynthetic taxa. Here we show that Ciliophrys sp. Baltic, representing a poorly studied non-photosynthetic lineage within the stramenopile algal class Dictyochophyceae, has undergone a secondary loss of its plastid. Genomic and transcriptomic analyses demonstrate the absence of both a plastid genome and nuclear genes critical for plastid biogenesis, although a few original plastid-targeted enzymes persist with a changed localization. title: A Spatial-Simulation-MCDM Framework for Prioritizing Vaccine Cold-Chain Resilience Strategies in Libya
abstract: Vaccine cold chains preserve vaccine potency across storage, transport, and service-delivery points. In geographically dispersed health systems, cold-chain planning requires spatial, operational, and strategic evidence because storage failure, transport delay, and demand pressure can affect service continuity. This study proposes a decision-support framework for prioritizing vaccine cold-chain resilience strategies in Libya. journal: Spectrum of Mechanical Engineering and Operational Research.

title: Spatial Persistence and Interannual Variability of Floating Algae in Kainji Lake (Nigeria): Insights from Multi-Year Sentinel-2 Observations
abstract: Background: Floating algae are increasingly recognized as indicators of ecological change in freshwater ecosystems. Although satellite remote sensing has been widely applied to monitor algal dynamics, little is known about the long-term spatial organization of floating algae in large tropical reservoirs in West Africa. journal: Trends in Ecological and Indoor Environmental Engineering

title: Environmental Impacts and Life Cycle Assessment of Recycled Plastic Bricks
abstract: Abstract This study evaluated the mechanical performance, contaminant release, and life-cycle impacts of recycled plastic blocks manufactured from beach-collected and facility-sourced plastic waste. Four formulations combining polyethylene terephthalate, high-density polyethylene, low-density polyethylene, sand, and glass were evaluated. Unweathered blocks had compressive strengths between 20.6–24.3 N/mm2, suitable for paving applications; however, higher plastic fractions led to lower strength and higher porosity. title: From and for the sake of place: elementary teachers co-designing place-based education climate change curriculum in research-practice partnership
abstract: Place-based education offers a framework and an effective instructional approach to connect the global issue of climate change with students’ and teachers’ local experiences. This study explores the collaboration in the first two cycles of co-design and implementation of five PBE lessons in 4th and 5th grade classrooms in two schools in New Orleans, USA, focused on CC-related hazards. Using a design-based implementation research approach, the study was conducted with a principal, two coaches, four teachers, and their 64 students who lived in an area with frequent CC disasters. title: Does higher bird richness correspond to more positive Weibo-derived bird-related sentiment? Spatial mismatch between bird species richness and Weibo-derived sentiment
abstract: Introduction As urban development intensifies, the relationship between urban bird diversity and bird-related emotional expression on social media has attracted increasing attention. However, evidence remains limited regarding their intra-urban spatial correspondence and underlying drivers. Methods Taking Shanghai as a case study, we integrated 4,142 bird-related Weibo comments from 2022 to 2024, 524,005 citizen birdwatching records, Baidu street-view images, and multisource environmental data. Bird-related emotional expression and species richness were measured at a 500 m × 500 m grid scale.

title: Polydopamine‐Wool Textiles for Sustainable Interfacial Solar Vapor Generation
abstract: ABSTRACT Interfacial solar vapor generation (ISVG), which harnesses sunlight for water distillation, presents a promising strategy to address global water scarcity. While conventional 3D evaporators offer high evaporation performance, their widespread implementation remains constrained by material selection, cost, and fabrication methods. Herein, we present a nature‐inspired, polydopamine (PDA)‐dyed wool textile as a 2.5D evaporator for ISVG, leveraging its double‐sided evaporating surfaces to maximize overall evaporation performance. title: Ecological Epigenetics: Research Fronts, Taxonomic Gaps, and a Five-Year Forecast
abstract: Ecological epigenetics investigates the role of molecular modifications, including DNA methylation, in heritable phenotypic variation in natural populations, often arising in response to environmental conditions. Because such modifications can respond to environmental change within a single generation, the field has direct relevance for understanding adaptation, plasticity, and the persistence of populations under habitat alteration and climate change. However, bibliometric attention has focused predominantly on the biomedical side of epigenetics, particularly cancer and clinical applications,
journal: Black Sea Journal of Engineering and Science

title: Evaluating farmers' adaptation strategies amid rising heat and climatic extremes in San Diego County, California
abstract: California's agricultural sector faces intensifying climate risks, yet research has concentrated on large commodity production regions, leaving small-farm and specialty crop systems underexamined. San Diego County, home to more than 4000 farms dominated by small-scale operations, high-value perennial tree crops, and the state's largest concentration of certified organic producers, faces compounding drought, extreme heat, wildfire, and high water costs. This study employed an exploratory sequential mixed-methods design integrating projections from the Community Earth System Model version 2 larg

title: Protists introduce distinct temporal patterns in a synthetic bacterial community consistent with known feeding traits
abstract: Through predation, protists act as strong determinants of bacterial communities, yet their role in shaping synthetic communities (SynCom) remains unclear. We present the effects of three predator protists - a ciliate (Colpoda steinii), a flagellate (Neobodo designis), and an amoeba (Acanthamoeba castellanii) on the temporal dynamics of bacterial SynCom using a microtiter plate-based design. We asked whether predation contributes to the maintenance of SynCom richness, alters trajectories, and whether these effects depend on the identity of the protist. title: Characterizing the presence of polychlorinated biphenyls within Biota Found in New Mexico
abstract: Polychlorinated biphenyls (PCBs) are a group of industrial chemicals that were widely used in the United States before being banned by the Toxic Substances Control Act in 1976. Concerns regarding PCBs arose in the 1960s due to their toxicity, classification as a carcinogenic compound, and longevity in the environment. Although the production of PCBs in the United States is currently banned, PCBs can still be found in legacy equipment, and the environment and PCBs are still unintentionally produced in common building materials. title: Curtobacterium uvaldense sp. nov., Falsirhodobacter allii sp. nov., Pseudomonas texasensis sp. nov., Three Novel Species Isolated from Onions in Texas, USA
abstract: Abstract Bacterial strains 20TX0008 T and 20TX0035 T were isolated from the symptomatic onion foliage in 2020, and a bacterial strain 21TX0197 T was isolated from the symptomatic onion bulb in 2021. Pathogenicity assays confirmed the two strains isolated from foliage to be non-pathogenic, while the strain 21TX0197 T was found to be pathogenic. Phylogenetic analysis using the 16 S rRNA gene revealed the closest resemblance of 20TX0008 T , 20TX0035 T , and 21TX0197 T to the genera Curtobacterium , Falsirhodobacter , and Pseudomonas , respectively. title: Digital eco-branding of FMCG companies
abstract: The study examines the formation of eco-brands of FMCG companies in the context of implementing Sustainable Development Goals and digital marke­ting. The relevance of the research is driven by the growing importance of corporate environmental responsibility, the mass production of fast-moving consumer goods, and the need to integrate sustainable development principles into the marke­ting activities of FMCG companies. title: A sustainability-aware optimization framework for port-hinterland truck scheduling
abstract: Abstract Ports are critical gateways for trade and regional growth but also generate substantial externalities such as emissions, congestion, and safety risks. Growing maritime transport and port throughput intensify long-haul diesel truck traffic on hinterland access roads, causing peak-hour bottlenecks, long queues, and higher environmental impacts. Despite many proposed operational strategies, these challenges remain insufficiently addressed. This paper develops a mixed-integer linear programming (MILP) model for sustainable port-hinterland truck scheduling within an integrated chassis-base

title: Anti corrosion and anti-pit resistant munj extract inhibitor for DSS 2205 in chloride contaminated solutions
abstract: Corrosion is the major issue in process industries, causing failure of process equipment due to structural degradation. This can be reduced by protective coating on equipment. In this study, Duplex Stainless Steel (DSS2205) is exposed to a 3.5% brine solution, and munj plant extract was prepared and utilized as a green corrosion inhibitor in various concentrations. The corrosion rate of DSS2205 sample coupons was analyzed by electrochemical techniques such as LPR and EIS. title: A freshwater resilient and connected network to sustain biodiversity under a changing climate
abstract: Over the last century, the integrity of streams and lakes in the U.S. has deteriorated. Our river networks are fragmented by thousands of dams hindering movement and adaptation. Water diversions, groundwater withdrawals, and habitat degradation have depleted flows and altered hydrology. Now climate change is altering precipitation patterns and temperature regimes, sending freshwater species into rapid decline. title: Internal and International Migration of Scholars in Times of Conflict: The Case of Ukraine, 2009‐2022
abstract: Abstract Current migration theories occasionally ignore the potentially negative aspects of scholarly migration as a form of high‐skilled migration, largely viewing it in a positive light. Yet scholarly migration is not always a tale of freedom and innovation, as the labels “researchers at risk” and “scientists in exile” demonstrate. We document the problematic aspects of conflict‐related scholarly migration among researchers with Ukraine‐affiliated publication histories from 2009 to 2022. title: SUSTAINABLE CONSERVATION AND ADMINISTRATIVE LAW: LEGAL FRAMEWORKS FOR ENFORCING ENVIRONMENTAL PROTECTION POLICIES
abstract: This study aims to analyze the administrative legal framework for enforcing sustainable environmental protection policies and identify administrative mechanisms that can optimize the implementation of conservation programs. The research methodology uses a normative juridical approach with descriptive-qualitative analysis, reviewing laws and regulations related to administrative law and environmental conservation, as well as case studies of policy implementation in various jurisdictions. title: Havadaki Silisyum Kirliliğinin Değişiminin İzlenmesi ve Kirliliğin Azaltılmasında Pseudotsuga menziesii’nin Kullanılabilirliği
abstract: Ağır metal kirliliği, son yüzyılda sanayi alanındaki gelişmelere bağlı olarak sürekli artan, insan sağlığını önemli derecede tehdit eden küresel bir sorun haline gelmiştir. title: Standards to Inform an Ecosystem Approach to Deep-sea Bottom Fisheries Management in the High Seas: Examples from the South Pacific Ocean
abstract: The South Pacific Regional Fisheries Management Organisation (SPRFMO) Convention requires consideration of risks and impacts as part of an ecosystem approach to fisheries management. In SPRFMO, assessments of the impact of demersal fisheries are guided by the Bottom Fishery Impact Assessment Standard and the Encounter Review Standard. title: An open-source quality control pipeline for SeaExplorer glider data: a case study in La Palma, Canary Islands
abstract: Autonomous underwater gliders are pivotal for sustained ocean observations; however, maximizing effective data utilization requires highly standardized, end-to-end data processing workflows. Despite the availability of generic glider toolboxes, to our knowledge, no published open-source workflow currently provides an end-to-end, SeaExplorer-specific processing chain from vendor raw files to CF-compliant, quality-controlled outputs. abstract: To investigate both anthropogenic and natural sources of metals in the South China seawater, the study analyzed metal content and Pb isotopic compositions in surface sediment and seawater from Taiwan and Indonesia. This analysis aimed to assess potential environmental pollution in the region. Samples were leached using a microwave digestion technique, and concentrations of metals (Na, Mg, Al, Si, K, Ti, Ca, Fe, and Pb), as well as Pb isotopes (207Pb/204Pb and 208Pb/204Pb), were measured using inductively coupled plasma-mass spectrometry (ICP-MS). title: Data Quality Assessment, Representativeness, and External Consistency of a Coastal Oceanographic Buoy Using Copernicus Marine and ERA5 Products
abstract: Coastal oceanographic buoys provide high-frequency observations, but their scientific use requires channel-specific quality assessment and explicit treatment of representativeness. This study evaluates a coastal buoy deployed off Cabo de Gata, southeastern Spain, during two non-contiguous observation windows in 2025 and 2026. Buoy records were standardized, screened with quality-control tests, aggregated daily without gap filling, and compared with Copernicus Marine and ERA5 products as an external-consistency assessment. title: DCEML: USV anomaly detection via Dual-Channel Explainable Multimodal Learning
abstract: Anomaly detection in Unmanned Surface Vehicles (USVs) is essential for maritime safety and autonomous navigation. Existing methods mainly rely on external observations such as GPS trajectories and navigational images, which are often insufficient for characterizing internal system states and explaining anomalous behaviors under complex marine disturbances. To address these challenges, we propose a Dual-Channel Explainable Multimodal Learning (DCEML) framework for tri-modal anomaly detection in USVs by integrating GPS trajectories, navigational images, and system logs. title: Assessing the consistency of coastal sea surface height measurements from SWOT altimetry and tide gauges along the U.S. East Coast
abstract: In nearshore environments, the limited accuracy of traditional satellite altimetry in monitoring coastal sea-level changes restricts its application. The wide-swath, high-resolution measurements from the Surface Water and Ocean Topography (SWOT) satellite provide a new understanding of coastal sea-level variability. This study evaluates the capability of SWOT to observe the instantaneous sea surface height (SSH) along the U.S. East Coast between August 2023 and December 2025. title: A new bubblegum coral from the Nazca Ridge reveals chitin as the structural scaffold of skeleton-less Paragorgia colonies
abstract: Abstract Bubblegum corals ( Paragorgia ; Corallidae) form among the largest branching colonies in deep-sea environments despite lacking an axial skeleton. How these octocorals maintain structural cohesion using only sub-millimeter sclerites has remained unexplained. Here we describe Paragorgia quitinosa Sánchez & Easton n. sp., collected at 670 m depth on the Nazca Ridge (southeastern Pacific) during the Schmidt Ocean Institute RV Falkor (too) expedition FKt240708, and report the first evidence of visible chitin in octocoral tissues. title: Advancing an Ecosystem Approach to Fisheries Management in the Northeast Atlantic: ICES’s Scientific Framework, Advice Products, and Implementation Pathways
abstract: Achieving marine management objectives and long-term sustainability requires moving beyond conventional, single-species management, towards an Ecosystem Approach to Fisheries Management (EAFM), that accounts for complex ecological interactions, cumulative human pressures, and environmental variability. title: A reliable early warning framework for vessel-bridge collisions via spatiotemporal trajectory prediction and anomaly detection
abstract: Abstract With the growing scale and number of vessels, inland waterway traffic environments have become more complex, especially in bridge waterways where vessel-bridge collisions occur frequently. To enhance navigational safety, this paper proposes a reliable early warning framework based on spatiotemporal trajectory prediction and anomaly detection. abstract: The delimitation of maritime boundaries remains one of the most complex issues in the international law of the sea. The 1982 United Nations Convention on the Law of the Sea (UNCLOS 1982), particularly Articles 74 and 83, mandates coastal states to delimit their Exclusive Economic Zone (EEZ) and Continental Shelf by agreement on the basis of international law to achieve an equitable solution. title: Spatially resolved gene expression analysis illuminates location-specific functions in the reef-building coral Pocillopora acuta
abstract: Reef-building coral polyps contain multiple specialized tissue types with distinct functions, from feeding and defense to symbiosis and skeleton formation. While these cell types have been characterized microscopically and more recently via single-cell RNA sequencing, spatially resolved high-throughput gene expression profiling remains limited in corals. Here we combine Laser Capture Microdissection with RNA sequencing to characterize tissue-specific gene expression in the reef building coral Pocillopora acuta. title: Application of Shotcrete in the Repair and Rehabilitation of Concrete Structures: A State-of-the-Art Review
abstract: This state-of-the-art review critically evaluates shotcrete for concrete rehabilitation using an application-based framework covering buildings, bridges, tunnels and underground works, hydraulic and marine structures, and industrial facilities. The review synthesizes deterioration mechanisms, substrate and interface conditions, material and process variables, mechanical and durability performance, quality control, and alternative repair systems. title: Real-world laboratories in Urban, Rural, and Marine contexts
abstract: Abstract Real-world laboratories (RwLs) have emerged as a scientifically grounded, sustainability-oriented, transdisciplinary approach to support transformative change through the co-production of knowledge via engagement and experimentation. While originally rooted in urban settings, real-world laboratories have increasingly been developed in rural and marine areas. Urban, rural, and marine areas have unique contextual characteristics that remain insufficiently addressed in both research and practice. title: Legacy PCB and hydrocarbon reservoirs in estuarine sediments: from historical contamination to hidden mass hotspots
abstract: Infrastructure-induced sediment deposits are common features in engineered river systems, yet their role as long-term reservoirs of persistent organic pollutants remains poorly quantified. The upper Seine Estuary (France), historically affected by intense industrial contamination and extensive river engineering, provides a relevant example of this issue. abstract: To proactively identify performance anomaly evolution and potential operational risks of marine main engines and reserve a sufficient time window for maintenance intervention, this paper proposes a data-driven multi-algorithm fusion framework for performance evaluation and anomaly early warning of marine main engines. abstract: Human-occupied vehicles (HOVs) provide an ideal platform for high-resolution near-bottom magnetic anomaly detection. However, complex platform-generated magnetic interference severely limits the reliable extraction of weak magnetic signals. The conventional Tolles–Lawson (T–L) model relies on large-amplitude attitude maneuvers to estimate interference coefficients, but such maneuvers are infeasible for HOVs because of their large inertia, hydrodynamic coupling, and deep-sea safety constraints. abstract: Sea moss has gained popularity as a functional food, yet information on the microbial quality, physicochemical characteristics, and heavy metal concentrations of commercially available products remains limited. abstract: Microplastics and plastic additives in rainwater harvesting systems (RWHS) represent a potential emerging concern in coastal urban environments. This preliminary baseline study investigated microplastic polymers and selected plastic additives in rainwater and RWHS water from two coastal sites in the Greater Jakarta coastal region, Indonesia, using pyrolysis gas chromatography-tandem mass spectrometry (Py-GC/MS/MS) for microplastic polymers and ultra-high performance liquid chromatography-tandem mass spectrometry (UHPLC-MS/MS) for plastic additives. title: Species-specific bioassays assess toxicity in sympatric marine turtles
abstract: Chemical pollution in marine environments is an escalating environmental threat, particularly for long-lived species such as marine turtles, which are susceptible to the harmful accumulation of chemical mixtures from terrestrial runoff. Differences in diet and trophic level can lead to differential exposure and accumulation of organic pollutants in marine turtles. Understanding these variations is critical to evaluating toxicological risk at the species level. title: Mapping Oil Spills and Offshore Industrial Activities in the Northwest Atlantic for Marine Conservation and Management
abstract: ABSTRACT Anthropogenic activities such as oil pollution, vessel traffic and artificial light pose growing threats to marine ecosystems across Canada's Exclusive Economic Zone (EEZ) and adjacent Atlantic waters. Despite their importance, data describing the spatial and temporal distribution of these threats have remained fragmented or difficult to access. title: Carbon dynamics and water quality regulation in Ruditapes philippinarum-Chlorella vulgaris co-culture with cardiac monitoring
abstract: Global warming and ocean acidification threaten marine aquaculture. Bivalve-microalgae co-culture is considered a promising approach for low-carbon aquaculture, but its effects on water quality, carbon dynamics and bivalve physiology are not fully understood. This study tested Ruditapes philippinarum and Chlorella vulgaris in sealed static chambers with three treatments: sterile seawater (NP-C), Chlorella monoculture (WP-C) and clam- Chlorella co-culture (WP). title: Spiny lobsters elicit avoidance behaviors in corallivorous invertebrates
abstract: Corallivory (the consumption of live coral tissue) threatens reef health and can undermine restoration efforts, particularly as coral cover declines. Although predators may suppress corallivore populations through direct consumption, their non-consumptive effects remain poorly understood. We tested whether chemical cues from two spiny lobsters, Panulirus argus and P. guttatus , elicit avoidance responses in two Caribbean corallivores: the snail Coralliophila galea and the fireworm Hermodice carunculata . title: From "the Flowery Flag" to"the Beautiful Nation": On the Evolution of Chinese Appellations for the United States from the Perspective of Cultural Psychology
abstract: The Chinese appellation for the United States is a highly frequent term in Sino-American cross-cultural communication, and its evolution reflects profound shifts in China's socio-cultural psychology. Based on a review of historical documents concerning the Chinese translations of the United States since the Ming and Qing dynasties, this paper divides the evolution of the Chinese appellation for the United States into four stages: the stage of neutral transliteration, the stage of derogatory portrayal, the stage of mixed evaluation of praise and blame, and the stage of friendly standardization.

title: Geometry of Breaking Waves Under Natural Sea Conditions
abstract: Abstract Wave breaking geometry is critical for understanding air‐sea interactions, yet its characterization in the field remains limited. This study analyzes the geometry of 16,369 active breaking waves, measured via stereo imagery in the Black Sea under diverse conditions. title: Anchoring in Strong Currents: Strategies for Reflexivity to Enhance Inter- and Transdisciplinary Marine Research
abstract: Marine research increasingly demands that early career researchers collaborate across disciplines, work with diverse communities including Indigenous peoples, and navigate social-ecological challenges characterised by ambiguity, uncertainty, and contested values. abstract: Abstract Binary protocols are widely used in the Internet, industrial control systems, and Internet of Things applications, and vulnerabilities in their implementation can directly affect system security. abstract: Noticastrum hatschbachii is an endemic species of coastal environments in southern Brazil, occurring in the Parque Natural Municipal das Dunas da Lagoa da Conceição (Florianópolis, Santa Catarina). It is currently listed in the Brazilian red lists due to strong anthropogenic pressure on coastal ecosystems. abstract: The fact that digital infrastructures are growing at a high rate has increased the type and frequency of risk to and occurrence of cybersecurity challenges to modern organizations. The conventional surveillance means will tend to either use the predetermined principles of detection or separate anomaly detection models that limit their ability to effectively prioritize security occurrences and respond to the appeared threats. abstract: The study examined the influence of availability of early warning systems and disaster management in public senior schools in Uasin Gishu County, Kenya. abstract: ABSTRACT The origin of the mafic–ultramafic rocks within the Babu ophiolitic mélange of southeastern Yunnan remains debated, leaving the timing and tectonic setting of mafic oceanic‐crust formation in the eastern Paleo‐Tethyan domain poorly constrained. title: Türkiye’s Compartmentalized Hedging and Multi-Crisis Diplomacy: Ukraine, Gaza, and the Black Sea
abstract: This article examines Türkiye’s multi-crisis diplomacy in a multipolar international order by examining its engagement with the war in Ukraine, the war in Gaza, and the Black Sea region. While studies on middle powers and hedging explain strategic uncertainty, they offer limited insight into how states manage multiple crises simultaneously. To address this gap, the article develops the concept of compartmentalized hedging, defined as distinct alignment strategies across geopolitical theaters while maintaining strategic coherence. title: Advancing sustainable cruise tourism
abstract: This work examines the European Union (EU)’s contribution to the transition towards more sustainable cruise tourism. Against the backdrop of the sector’s continued expansion and the growing concerns surrounding its environmental and social impacts, it analyses how the EU is influencing the sustainability of cruise activities. The work first outlines the EU’s general framework for addressing the sustainability of cruise tourism, identifying the Union’s competences and the main sustainability frameworks of its regulatory approach. title: Harnessing the ocean’s chemistry: ecological functions and therapeutic potential of phlorotannins
abstract: Phlorotannins are unique polyphenolic compounds produced exclusively by brown algae, functioning as adaptive marine metabolites that mediate ecological defence, environmental stress responses, and species-specific biological functions. Their biosynthesis is regulated by ecological pressures such as UV radiation, herbivory, and oxidative stress, linking marine adaptation with biomedical relevance. title: From flows to events: spatiotemporal insights into Bologna’s mobility using mobile networks
abstract: Abstract Mobile network data represent one of the most powerful emerging sources for large-scale mobility analysis. This paper proposes a complete data-driven pipeline to understand, detect, and predict population movement patterns within a region using anonymized origin–destination data provided by mobile phone operators. The dataset, covering 60 consecutive days in 2019, reports millions of daily flows between census areas together with demographic information. abstract: Abstract This article reconstructs how a Ligurian seafaring community moved from communal, profit-sharing forms of maritime enterprise to salaried and increasingly stratified labour during the transition from sail to steam. It traces Camogli’s trajectory from locally crewed vessels in cabotage and Black Sea grain trades to late-century oceanic tramping. Three shifts stand out. Frequency and phase tracking for excitation capacitor fault detection in a self-excited induction generator using the ZCT method
abstract: This paper presents a methodology for detecting excitation capacitor faults in self-excited induction generators (SEIGs) used in wind energy systems operating in isolated or rural areas. The proposed approach combines frequency and phase tracking with zero-crossing time rate analysis for real-time anomaly detection. The SEIG is modelled using the finite element method (FEM) to simulate its electromechanical behaviour under various fault conditions. title: Difficulties Experienced by Maritime Students During Shipboard Training: Basis for an Intervention Program
abstract: This study examined the difficulties experienced by maritime students of EXACT Colleges of Asia, Inc. during shipboard training as a basis for developing an intervention program to strengthen cadet readiness, resilience, well-being, and training experiences. Anchored on Bandura’s Social Cognitive Theory and an Input-Process-Output model, the study employed a quantitative descriptive-correlational design involving 100 maritime cadets who had completed shipboard training under the Bachelor of Science in Marine Transportation and Bachelor of Science in Marine Engineering programs. title: Design for Maintainability (DFM) of Living Building Envelopes
abstract: The integration of vegetation into building envelopes through green façades and living walls offers established thermal, environmental, and economic benefits, yet these benefits depend on maintenance performance that is rarely addressed at the design stage, particularly in high-humidity coastal environments where salt-laden air, wind-driven rain, and cyclical wetting accelerate corrosion, biofouling, and substrate degradation. title: Woodland platform mounds made of feasts: an example from Mound II at Garden Patch, Florida Gulf Coast
abstract: Platform mounds in the Woodland Southeast were often associated with feasting, including prior to and during coordinated ritual construction events and in ceremonies on their elevated summits. We observe that while many inland platforms were made for feasts, some coastal platforms were made of feasts. We argue this detail is an underexplored basis for understanding Woodland platforms’ significance as monuments. title: Dynamics of distant water fishing fleets in Southeast Asian countries
abstract: Industrial distant-water fishing (DWF) fleets increasingly operate within the Exclusive Economic Zones (EEZs) of developing coastal states, raising critical concerns about ecological impacts, governance capacity, competition, and distributional equity. Yet assessments of DWF impacts frequently rely on aggregate catch metrics, potentially underestimating scale-dependent ecological pressure and institutional vulnerability. abstract: Microneedle patches (MNPs) have emerged as versatile platforms for minimally invasive transdermal drug delivery, biosensing, and point-of-care diagnostics by transiently breaching the stratum corneum while minimizing pain and tissue damage. Recent advances in biomaterials, microfabrication, additive manufacturing, and bioelectronics have expanded MNP functionality beyond drug delivery to include controlled therapeutic release, interstitial fluid sampling, wearable biosensing, and closed-loop therapeutic systems. title: Ground-breaking fishing subsidy treaty undercut by holdouts
abstract: The World Trade Organization’s new Agreement on Fisheries Subsidies (AFS) officially entered into force in September 2025. As the first global treaty to restrict the use of harmful fishing subsidies, this is a landmark agreement for trade, development and the environment. It is a critical step towards reigning in the destructive subsidies that have fueled a global fisheries crisis and ensuring the sustainability of the world’s oceans. title: Regional fidelity vs dispersal of capelin (Mallotus villosus) in the Gulf of St. Lawrence, inferred from otolith chemistry
abstract: Capelin (Mallotus villosus), a key forage fish in the Northwest Atlantic, links zooplankton to predators including commercial fishes, seabirds, and marine mammals, yet its life-cycle connectivity in the Gulf of St. Lawrence (GSL) remain poorly understood. Between 2022 and 2024, otoliths from 927 individuals collected during and after spawning were analysed by Laser Ablation Inductively Coupled Plasma Mass Spectrometry (LA-ICP-MS), and seven trace elements (Li, B, Mg, K, Zn, Sr, Ba) were used to discriminate three chemically distinct regions within the GSL. abstract: Abstract In this work, an in-situ method is presented for rapid mapping of natural gamma-ray radionuclides in order to study the sediment characterization in beach sand area. The idea of the proposed work is to present demonstration exercises using the underwater low-resolution gamma-ray spectrometer named KATERINA II to evaluate the sediment characterization and its granulometry. The detection system is integrated in mobile platforms for continuous operation to be applied as a manned surface vehicle. title: Beyond Export Volume: Value Capture, Trading Hubs, and Equitable Upgrading in the Global Cinnamon Value Chain A Review
abstract: Cinnamon illustrates a persistent paradox in global agricultural trade: the countries that cultivate and supply a commodity do not necessarily capture the largest share of the economic value generated from it. Indonesia, particularly the Kerinci highlands of Jambi and neighboring areas of Sumatra, is a major source of Cinnamomum burmannii, yet cinnamon is also exported by non-producing economies such as Singapore. title: From Discursive Exclusion to Rights Empowerment: Legal Dilemmas and Policy Governance of Youth Intercultural Communication under the SDG Framework
abstract: Under the normative framework of United Nations Sustainable Development Goal (SDG) Target 4.7, cultivating global citizenship and ensuring inclusive cultural participation constitute imperative legal commitments for contemporary higher education. However, within the global governance architecture, youth from non-elite Higher Education Institutions (HEIs) encounter structural 'discursive exclusion'—a covert systemic dilemma denying substantive equality in cultural expression and transnational rights-claiming. Metal bioaccumulation and oxidative stress in the southern sand flathead (Platycephalus bassensis, Teleostei) across an urbanised embayment
abstract: Urbanised embayments worldwide are increasingly affected by anthropogenic release of metals and other contaminants into their surrounding waters, posing risks to both marine and human health. This study assessed metal bioaccumulation and associated sublethal effects in the benthic fish Platycephalus bassensis across eight sites in Port Phillip Bay, Australia. title: Investigating Formation Cycles in Lithium-Ion Pouch Cells Using in Operando Chromatic Confocal Microscopy.
abstract: Abstract Chromatic Confocal Microscopy (CCM) is an optical, non-contact method that can be used to monitor changes in Lithium-ion cell thickness in operando. Additionally, this method is ideal for quality control of cells as the equipment used is compact and can be deployed in research environments as well as production lines. title: Sustainable tourism for whom?
abstract: In his lecture Of other spaces: Utopias and heterotopias, the French philosopher Michel Foucault introduced the concept of “heterotopias”, identifying the ship as hétérotopie par excellence due to its unique characteristic of floating piece of space deviating from and subverting the socio-legal norms governing society. title: Development and application of a blubber-based detection protocol for phthalate ester metabolites in bottlenose dolphins (Tursiops truncatus)
abstract: Phthalates (PAEs) are high production volume plasticizing chemicals linked to endocrine disruption in mammals. Phthalates are released from the products to which they are added, leading to environmental exposure for humans and wildlife. Recent studies of bottlenose dolphin (Tursiops truncatus) urine have demonstrated prevalent exposure to phthalates. abstract: ABSTRACT While the Antarctic region has experienced significant climatic changes over the Holocene, few high‐resolution records have examined their effects on the local biota. In order to understand past ecological shifts and forecast future changes, it is important to obtain high‐resolution palaeoecological records from this region. abstract: ABSTRACT Spatial geography, ontogenetic movement, and trophic patterns of mobile species are key elements of species life history, and knowledge of them is critical for effective marine resource management. For yellowfin tuna ( Thunnus albacares ; YFT) and blackfin tuna ( Thunnus atlanticus ; BLFT), residency durations and ontogenetic movements in the Gulf of Mexico (Gulf) are uncertain. title: An annual rainfall metric integrates daily magnitude and frequency
abstract: Characterizing annual precipitation requires consideration of both daily magnitude and frequency. We introduce the Rainfall Magnitude–Rank Index (RMRI), a simple annual metric that requires no user-selected threshold or tuning parameter. RMRI is the largest integer k such that at least k days in a year record precipitation of at least k mm. For example, an RMRI of 26 indicates that at least 26 days recorded rainfall of 26 mm or more during that year. title: Untargeted metabolomics reveals chemical variation and antimicrobial biomarkers in Dodonaea viscosa var. angustifolia (L.f.) Benth
abstract: Dodonaea viscosa var. angustifolia (L.f.) Benth is a widely used medicinal plant with reported biological activities, however few studies have identified marker compounds for quality control of the plant and interspecies chemical variation. The aim of this study was to investigate chemical variation in the non-volatile constituents of D. viscosa var. angustifolia collected from different locations, using high-performance thin layer chromatography (HPTLC) and untargeted ultra-performance liquid chromatography–mass spectrometry (UPLC–MS) metabolomics, and to identify chemo-biomarkers for quality

title: LINGUOCULTURAL AND DISCURSIVE ASPECTS OF THE NATIONAL IMAGE
abstract: The article provides a comprehensive analysis of the linguocultural and discursive representation of national identity in Kazakhstan’s media discourse. In the context of a multiethnic and multilingual society, mass media play a strategic role in strengthening national unity and shaping a holistic image of the nation. The study is based on a corpus of Kazakh- and Russian-language media texts published between 2020 and 2024. The analysis includes news reports, editorials, official statements, and televised materials that address issues of national values, national identity, and collective memory

title: Research into the production of structural elements for low-pressure polyethylene vessels
abstract: Most small vessels have been constructed using wood or fiberglass-/carbon fiber-reinforced polymer composite materials. Increasingly, low-pressure polyethylene, or high-density polyethylene (HDPE), has been adopted as an alternative material. It combines enhanced resistance to marine environments with full recyclability, as well as a low density and competitive price. abstract: This article examines the experiences of Australian sailors and marines who travelled to China to fight in the Boxer Rebellion between 1900 and 1901. It analyses their diaries and correspondence to explore individual responses to one of the earliest instances of large-scale, cross-cultural encounter for colonial Australians in Asia. abstract: Many river deltas are aquatic hot spots for carbon dioxide (CO 2 ) emissions to the atmosphere. Their patchwork of wetlands, lakes, channels, and river reaches often complicates the analysis of CO 2 sources such as ecosystem respiration or lateral water transfer. Sensing techniques offer the opportunity of measuring the CO 2 , O 2 and DIC concentrations at high temporal resolution for periods from days to months. title: Carbon dioxide (CO₂) dynamics in Exhaust Gas Boiler (EGB) systems: Distinguishing measurement artifacts from true emission reduction
abstract: Implementing Exhaust Gas Boilers (EGBs) for waste heat recovery is a key strategy to improve thermal efficiency in power generation and thereby reduce carbon dioxide (CO₂) emissions. However, field measurements often show a misleading decrease in CO₂ concentration downstream of the EGB, which can be misinterpreted as direct emission removal. This study distinguishes genuine CO₂ mitigation, achieved through fuel savings, from apparent reductions due to measurement artifacts. title: Biofloc‐based aquaculture: From monoculture to integrated systems
abstract: Abstract The demand for high‐quality protein has been growing in recent years, led by population growth. The development of aquaculture has been considered one of the solutions to ensure food security worldwide. New farming technologies have been promoted to increase productivity and, at the same time, minimize environmental impacts. During the past decades, biofloc technology (BFT) has emerged as a sustainable and cost‐efficient culture method. title: Aflatoxin contamination in dried fish: Sources, health impacts, Detection, Detoxification, and Control strategies in developing countries
abstract: Aflatoxin contamination in dried fish is a growing food safety concern with significant implications for human and animal health. This review highlights the key factors contributing to aflatoxin contamination in dried fish, including its sources, influencing factors, health impacts, detection methods, and prevention and mitigation strategies. abstract: Hairpin winding technology has emerged as a transformative structural design paradigm for new energy vehicle traction motors, enabling slot fill factors exceeding 70% compared to 35%–45% for conventional round-wire windings, thereby delivering significant improvements in power density, thermal management, and manufacturing automation. abstract: Fennel (Foeniculum vulgare Mill.) is one of the economically important seed spices grown across arid and semi-arid India, and Rajasthan remains its leading producer. Ajmer Fennel-2 (AF-2), released by ICAR-National Research Centre on Seed Spices (ICAR-NRCSS), was developed specifically to replace ageing, disease-prone farmer-saved seed stocks with a higher-yielding, Ramularia blight-tolerant alternative carrying elevated essential oil content. abstract: The Six Dynasties period (AD 222–589) witnessed political fragmentation alongside expanding ceramic production and exchange in early medieval China. This study integrates typological assessment, LA-ICP-MS trace-element and rare-earth element analyses, and SEM-EDS observations of six celadons from three tombs at Dengfushan cemetery in Nanjing (ancient Jiankang). abstract: The study investigated the concentration of heavy metals in fish sold across selected Nigerian markets, focusing on public health implications and environmental safety. Fish is a major source of protein and essential nutrients for a vast majority of Nigerians, yet increasing industrialization, poor waste management and agricultural runoff have led to the contamination of aquatic ecosystems. abstract: Background and Objectives: Aflatoxins are toxic secondary metabolites produced by certain Aspergillus species and are frequently found in contaminated food and herbal products. abstract: Cetaceans exhibit rapid wound healing in marine environments characterized by hypoxia and high pathogen loads, yet the adaptive mechanisms underlying their coagulation system remain poorly understood. We integrated evolutionary analyses with functional experiments to elucidate the molecular basis of specialized coagulation in cetaceans.
