title: Competing Visions for Venezuela
abstract: Venezuela’s transformation depends on how the divergent visions of chavismo and the opposition align with the Trump administration’s interests and goals. Although the US has played a decisive role following the capture of Nicolás Maduro, it does not wield absolute control, and the results have not been widely accepted by Venezuelans. Lasting change is unlikely without broader scrutiny and recognition, including from international actors such as the European Union.

title: Normative Legal Analysis of Corporate Legal Responsibility for Greenwashing Practices and Environmental Damage: Case of Dayak Kanayat’n
abstract: This study investigates corporate legal liability for greenwashing practices that cause environmental harm in Indonesia. Growing global pressure for sustainable business practices has prompted many corporations to publicly commit to protecting the environment, but such narratives often serve as public relations efforts rather than genuine ecological responsibility. Using a normative juridical method with statutory and conceptual approaches, this research identifies the patterns and defining features of greenwashing while assessing the sufficiency of Indonesia's existing legal framework. title: Effect Of Intellectual Capital Disclosure on Financial Reporting Quality of Listed Deposit Money Banks in Nigeria
abstract: The study examined the effect of intellectual capital disclosure on financial reporting quality of listed deposit money banks in Nigeria. The study employed panel data obtained from the annual reports of selected listed deposit money banks in Nigeria over the study period. Panel regression analysis was used to examine the relationship between the components of intellectual capital disclosure employee management, intellectual capital performance, and customer capital and financial reporting quality. title: Detection and genomic characterization of West Nile virus lineage 2 in captive harbor seals in southern Italy
abstract: Introduction West Nile virus (WNV) is a mosquito-borne flavivirus maintained in bird–mosquito cycles, with occasional spillover events causing neuroinvasive disease in humans and animals. This study describes two fatal cases of WNV lineage 2 infection in captive harbor seals housed in a zoological park in southern Italy, together with genomic characterization and phylogenetic analysis of the detected strains. title: The Green Upgrading of Digital Infrastructure: The Impact of Green Data Centers on Air Pollution
abstract: The rapid expansion of the digital economy coincides with escalating environmental challenges, making Green Data Centers (GDC) an important form of digital infrastructure with potential implications for environmental governance. However, existing studies mainly evaluate data centers from the perspectives of energy efficiency, electricity consumption, and carbon emissions, while city-level evidence regarding their effects on ambient air pollution remains limited. title: Short-term rentals and the housing market: evidence from Portuguese metropolitan areas
abstract: Abstract In this paper, we study the impact of short-term rentals (STR) on housing markets in Portugal, exploiting a 2014 policy reform that eased registration requirements. Using a novel dataset of property transactions from 2010 to 2017 for the Lisbon and Porto metropolitan areas, we estimate the effect of STR expansion using a two-way fixed effects model and a difference-in-differences design that leverages staggered treatment across postcodes. title: Methodological Variations in Environmental Justice Screening Tools and Their Impact on Disadvantaged Community Designations
abstract: Government agencies in the United States have developed environmental justice screening tools (EJSTs) and designations to promote equitable distribution of benefits from environmental policies to disadvantaged communities (DACs). However, the methodological choices embedded in these tools, including the selection, weighting, and aggregation of environmental justice indicators, vary across EJSTs, and their implications for DAC designation outcomes are poorly understood. title: From brain drain to geopolitical talent competition: scientific diasporas and the future of Global South development
abstract: Scientific diasporas have emerged as increasingly important actors in global science, technology, and innovation (STI) ecosystems. In the context of geopolitical fragmentation, technological competition, and intensifying global inequalities, talent mobility is no longer solely a migration issue but a strategic dimension of development, science diplomacy, and international influence. title: Disaster Resilience in Mountainous Regions of India
abstract: Disaster Management, a part of the Next Generation Administrative Reforms, focuses on mainstreaming disaster management in development plans and ensuring effective governance. This includes improving government structures and processes, promoting citizen-centric governance, and innovations in e-governance. We present in our paper the research on catastrophe resilience in India’s mountainous regions. title: FACTORS INFLUENCING THE SPATIAL LABOR EMPLOYMENT STRUCTURE IN THE DIGITAL ECONOMY: BASED ON A SPATIAL PANEL MODEL
abstract: In the context of the rapid development of the digital economy, global labor markets and employment structures are undergoing profound transformations. This study focuses on the interactive relationship between the digital economy and labor employment structures, exploring the impact of digital economy development on the labor employment structure across different regions in China. title: Desnutrición crónica infantil en Pastaza: entre el hipergarantismo legal y la desprotección territorial de la niñez amazónica
abstract: Este artículo examina la desnutrición crónica infantil (DCI) en la provincia de Pastaza, Ecuador, analizando la brecha entre el marco normativo garantista y la realidad territorial. La DCI afecta al 29,5 % de los menores de cinco años en la provincia, ubicándola como la segunda con mayor prevalencia en el país. title: A sophisticated multilevel thresholding optimizer for diagnosing breast cancer disease
abstract: Abstract Breast cancer is one of the leading causes of mortality among women worldwide, and early detection is essential to improve survival rates. Among various imaging techniques, thermography is a promising noninvasive, non-ionizing, and cost-effective modality for real-time diagnosis. This study proposes a multilevel threshold segmentation approach based on Enhanced Hippopotamus Optimization (EHO) for breast thermographic images. title: Conflict between farmers and Barbary macaques (Macaca sylvanus) in Northern Algeria: threats and conservation implications
abstract: Abstract Human-wildlife conflict is a major challenge in conservation biology with ecological and socioeconomic consequences. The problem is particularly delicate when the animals involved are threatened with extinction and experiencing rapid habitat loss due to climate change and anthropogenic actions. Here, we examined crop-foraging on farms in Central North Algeria by the Endangered Barbary macaques ( Macaca sylvanus ) to understand the conflict severity. title: Sustainable Tourism as a Driver of Local Own-Source Revenue in Regional Development: A Case Study of Klaten Regency, Indonesia
abstract: This study examines the contribution of sustainable tourism to increasing Local Own-Source Revenue (LOSR) in Klaten Regency, Indonesia. The analysis is based on four key dimensions of sustainable tourism: economic, social, environmental, and institutional. A mixed-methods approach was employed, combining quantitative data collected from 100 respondents with qualitative insights obtained through in-depth interviews with key stakeholders. abstract: Objective This study aims to examine how members of Generation Z perceive sustainability within the context of sport and which communication factors influence their decision-making processes. It focuses on identifying barriers that hinder responsible consumption and on analyzing the role educational institutions play in this process. abstract: The brush-and-ink system of Chinese painting is a systematic psychological symbol system deeply rooted in Confucian, Dao , and Chan , where lines, ink tones, and composition, respectively, embody painters’ personality traits, emotional states, and mental patterns. abstract: This study examines the distribution of transportation discretionary grants under the Infrastructure Investment and Jobs Act (IIJA) using state-level data from FYS 2021–2023. Using award data from the BILLaunchpad and applying negative binomial and multiple linear regression models, along with panel analysis of the popular RAISE (Rebuilding American Infrastructure with Sustainability and Equity) program, the study evaluates the roles of political alignment, equity merit, prior application experience, and program engagement while controlling for state fiscal and physical resources. title: The Influence of Work-Life Balance and Career Development on Employee Performance Mediated by Job Satisfaction at the Semarang Tengah Primary Tax Service Office
abstract: This study investigates the direct and indirect impacts of work-life balance and career development on employee performance at the Semarang Tengah Primary Tax Service Office (KPP Pratama Semarang Tengah), utilizing job satisfaction as a mediating variable. An explanatory quantitative design was applied. Data were gathered via a five-point Likert-scale questionnaire administered to all 78 employees using a census technique. title: Urban flood modelling and evaluation of nature-based solutions at the neighbourhood scale: The case of the Tirakaa Wadi, Nador (northeastern Morocco)

abstract: Malnutrition in toddlers remains a public health concern in Indonesia. East Java reports a relatively high prevalence of wasting (7.2%), while Lumajang Regency recorded a severe wasting prevalence of 6.9% in 2022, exceeding WHO public health thresholds and increasing from the previous year. The 2021 eruption of Mount Semeru disrupted food systems and limited access to health and nutrition services, increasing nutritional risks among affected toddlers. title: Language shifts as a catalyst for social and educational cohesion in multilingual societies
abstract: Although the Indonesian New Capital City, or Ibu Kota Nusantara (IKN), is a potential living laboratory of a multilingual society, studies investigating the extent to which language shift conditions stimulate educational cohesion remain limited. To fill this gap, this research aims to investigate language shifts at schools in IKN to achieve equitable education. title: Agent-Centred Nuclear Safety Principles for Small Modular Reactors
abstract: Abstract Small Modular Reactors (SMRs) are among the new designs that promise more compact nuclear power plants (NPPs) with scalable generation capacity and shorter construction time, while retaining emission-free electricity in exchange for small amounts of manageable radioactive waste per kWh of generated electricity. Their size and modular design contribute to the growing popularity of SMRs. title: Would-be Émigrés: Navigating the Academic Job Market Under Fascism
abstract: Abstract What defines an émigré scholar? Drawing on personal correspondence between members of the Unity of Science movement, this article emphasizes the contingency of the category by reconstructing the social and material conditions that shaped academic life under fascism. When scholars became refugees, they had to find ways to move their knowledge with them. title: Post-COVID-19 structure of international trade and its impact on sustainable development in Arab countries
abstract: The purpose of this study is to analyze the effects of post-COVID-19 structure of international trade on multiple aspects of sustainable development in selected Arab countries (Jordan, Saudi Arabia, United Arab Emirates, Qatar, Morocco, Egypt, Kuwait and Tunisia) over the period 2014-2024. To achieve the purpose of the study, we employed the fixed-effects panel EGLS and the dummy interaction approach to estimate some equations where it used GDP pair capita, unemployment rate and CO2 emissions as indicators of the economic, social and environmental aspects of sustainable development. title: Congestion-Triggered Electric-Vehicle Charging Station Assignment Using Short-Term Cumulative Demand Forecasts
abstract: Short-term congestion at public electric-vehicle charging stations depends on both near-future demand and how vehicles are distributed across the network. We forecast cumulative station-level charging initiations and use the forecasts in congestion-triggered station assignment. title: Uses of Native and Exotic Palms in Ecological Restoration
abstract: For its outstanding biodiversity Ecuador has been designated as one of ten megadiverse countries. Due to its location on the equator, it enjoys many climates, soils and diverse geological processes. In Ecuador, palms represent the group of native plants with the greatest diversity of uses per species. At the Mashpi Shungo Reserve in the Ecuadorian northwest, the authors have been working to restore degraded areas using regenerative practices through diverse agroforestry systems. abstract: Successfully addressing and resolving water challenges, in a global context where the vectors of population growth, urbanisation, climate change and globalisation are at work, is a key element to foster sustainable development and achieve an improvement in the quality of life of societies and people. It is essential that water is on the political agenda and that many actors play their role properly, with the appropriate governance. title: Plant part substitution as a sustainable conservation strategy for some medicinal plants based on phytochemical equivalence
abstract: Abstract Medicinal flora represents an essential source of bioactive substances for both conventional and contemporary medicine; nevertheless, excessive extraction of non-renewable parts such as roots, bark, and heartwood has led to significant reductions in wild populations, especially among endemic and slow-growing species. This review proposes and evaluates the substitution of plant parts by replacing vulnerable bark and roots with renewable aerial parts, using published evidence of phytochemical equivalence for sustainable conservation of medicinal plants. abstract: This article presents an integrative review of offshore wind farms connected via high-voltage direct-current (VSC-HVDC) transmission systems based on voltage-source converters. This review focuses on power transmission technologies, wind turbine converter interfaces, VSC-HVDC system architectures, control strategies, fault ride-through (FRT), and protection standards. abstract: Objective To establish age- and body surface area (BSA)-specific ultrasound percentile charts for thyroid volume (Tvol) in Polish school-aged children born after the introduction of mandatory iodine prophylaxis, and to compare these values with previous national, WHO, and recent European reference data. abstract: Abstract Drought is an increasingly important driver of tree mortality, but its long-term impacts on trait expression remain poorly understood. Leaves are a key interface at which trees respond to abiotic stress, and foliar traits such as chemical defenses and microbial communities may play an important role in determining post-drought resilience. title: Integration over intensity: field-experimental evidence on phygital design in heritage tourism
abstract: Abstract This study investigates whether increasing digital intensity actually improves heritage tourism experiences, or whether the real value driver is how well technology is integrated with the tour guide. We report a Latin-square quasi-experiment conducted in the Gothic Cathedral Tower of Oviedo (Spain) with 135 paying visitors distributed across nine guided groups. abstract: Severe sedimentation in the Sengguruh Reservoir has reduced its effective storage capacity to approximately 24% of the original value, creating persistent dredging and spoil bank management problems. abstract: Abstract Wireless sensor networks (WSNs) require secure and energy-efficient communication because sensor nodes operate with limited battery power, constrained communication range, and high vulnerability to interception, spoofing, and malicious forwarding. abstract: The Lower Koshi Basin (LKB), a transboundary river basin covering parts of India and Nepal, is impacted by multiple hazards, predominantly floods, landslides, droughts, earthquakes, and others. Studies have established that socio-economic conditions, ecological sensitivity, transboundary setting, and institutional arrangements increase Disaster Risk Reduction (DRR) complexities. Building on this context, this research examines whether governance-related issues make disasters more enduring. title: Edadismo invisible: voces y experiencias en la atención hospitalaria
abstract: El objetivo fue analizar la presencia de prácticas edadistas en la atención sanitaria en el Pius Hospital de Valls (Tarragona), explorando cómo el trato, el lenguaje y las dinámicas asistenciales reflejan posibles actitudes discriminatorias hacia los pacientes mayores. Se examinó la influencia del contexto sociocultural y profesional en su manifestación y en la calidad del cuidado. Se adoptó un enfoque cualitativo descriptivo de carácter exploratorio, basado en entrevistas semiestructuradas a diez profesionales sanitarios. title: Spatiotemporal autocorrelation of landslides in neighborhoods of Recife, Brazil (2015–2024) based on the Moran and Lisa index
abstract: This study analyzes the spatiotemporal dynamics of landslide occurrences in neighborhoods of the municipality of Recife (PE), from 2015 to 2024, using spatial analysis techniques based on the Global Moran’s Index and Local Indicators of Spatial Association (LISA). Official data from the Recife Civil Defense, as well as landslide susceptibility maps prepared by CPRM and municipal monitoring information, were used. title: Inteligencia artificial en educación superior: transformación sociotecnológica y desafíos éticos-regulatorios
abstract: Este ensayo reflexivo de corte documental examina la evolución histórica, los fundamentos técnicos y las implicaciones socioeducativas de la inteligencia artificial (IA), con énfasis en educación superior. Se parte de la trayectoria de la IA desde sus bases formales y hitos fundacionales hasta su consolidación contemporánea mediante aprendizaje automático, redes neuronales y aprendizaje profundo. A continuación, se analiza la incorporación de la IA en educación, confrontando la promesa de personalización y analítica del aprendizaje con críticas sobre tecnocratización, reducción del aprendizaje

title: Modeling determinants of women’s decision-making autonomy on agriculture and household matters in rural Ethiopia: a mixed effects beta regression tree analysis
abstract: Despite existing research on women's decision-making autonomy (WDMA), there remains a significant gap in understanding the complex factors influencing women's autonomy. This study investigated the determinants of WDMA in agriculture and household matters in rural Ethiopia. The study used data from nine rural districts in the Oromia and the former Southern Nations Nationalities and Peoples region in Ethiopia. title: Learning to start a new business with values: the challenge of sustainable entrepreneurship in university teaching
abstract: Purpose This study aims to present a teaching methodology that integrates sustainability and the Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs) into entrepreneurship education to foster the development of sustainable business models (SBMs) through challenge-based learning (CBL) in higher education. Design/methodology/approach The methodology was implemented over five years at the University of Valencia and the University of Turku, combining CBL with a proprietary framework for designing, testing and scaling SBMs. A systematic literature review (2003–2024) was conducted to support the approach. title: Adjudication Where Negotiation Is Required: Community Initiation in Taiwan's Renewable Energy Siting
abstract: ABSTRACT Renewable energy projects continue to fail at the local level despite enjoying broad public support and successive rounds of participatory reform. This article asks what institutional pattern produces this persistent gap and what kind of response would address it. title: Arab nationalism and historicity in the 1980s novel: Haydar Haydar’s Walīma li-aʿshāb al-baḥr and Rachid Boudjedra’s Maʿrakat al-Zuqāq
abstract: Two 1980s novels from the Maghreb and Mashreq, respectively – Algerian writer Rachid Boudjedra's Maʿrakat al-Zuqāq (Battle of the Strait, 1986) and Syrian writer Haydar Haydar's Walīma li-aʿshāb al-baḥr (Banquet for Seaweed, 1983) - offer formal and thematic critiques of a regime of historicity that they link to Arab nationalist states after decolonization. Using François Hartog's regimes of historicity, this essay reads these modernist novels as sites of delayed processing for the thwarted hopes of progressive, anti-colonial emancipation. title: A Writer’s Universe: John Updike on Physics and Astronomy
abstract: Abstract Among the many twentieth-century authors who have been inspired by developments in science, the American novelist and poet John Updike stands out as a fascinating example. Interested in science and its history, he was well informed by his reading of popular science books and journals. From where did he get his information? How did scientists respond to his literary works referring to science, if at all? This paper offers a critical survey of Updike’s science-related writings from the mid-1950s to his death in 2009. title: Puesta a disposición, gobernanza algorítmica e intermediación en el streaming musical
abstract: Este artículo analiza cómo la transición desde la distribución analógica hacia el streaming reconfiguró la cadena de valor de la música. Lejos de eliminar la intermediación: emergen agregadoras y nuevos contratos de distribución digital como respuesta a costos de transacción, asimetrías negociales y exigencias técnicas del entorno online. En paralelo, el eje regulatorio se desplaza desde la mera puesta a disposición hacia un problema de visibilidad: la recomendación algorítmica asigna atención y, por esa vía, condiciona ingresos con opacidad y dificultades de verificación para los creadores. title: Improvement of chaotic maps for k-NN classification using Lévy-flight whale optimization: multiple dataset comparison
abstract: Metaheuristic feature selection is frequently used to improve distance-based classification on tabular datasets, yet the empirical value of adding chaotic dynamics to already enhanced optimizers remains unclear. This paper presents a controlled multi-dataset benchmark of a binary Whale Optimization Algorithm (WOA) feature selector combined with Lévy-flight refinement and a k-nearest neighbors (k-NN) classifier. title: TOURISM SITUATION IN THAILAND AND APPROPRIATE STRATEGIC ADJUSTMENTS
abstract: Tourism serves as a vital engine for the Thai economy, contributing significantly to national wealth; however, persistent disparities exist in income distribution between primary and secondary provinces. This study aims to analyze the current tourism situation in Thailand and identify appropriate strategic adjustments to enhance the industry’s resilience and sustainability. By evaluating the concentration of visitors and revenue, the research seeks to provide a roadmap for more equitable economic growth through tourism. This research utilizes secondary time-series data from 2012 to 2023 obtain

title: Climate change education and learner competency: Evaluating pedagogical approaches in Kenyan schools
abstract: This article evaluates pedagogical approaches for climate change education (CCE) and learner competency in Kenyan schools. It combines narrative synthesis and a purposively delimited corpus of contemporary scholarly literature on the topic of climate pedagogy, learner competency, and African or Global South education contexts. The study was anchored in Epstein’s Overlapping Spheres of Influence Theory. A systematic source-identification process screened 72 records and retained six article documents for analysis. title: Practical flow state detection: Entropy-based EEG classification from portable EEG headbands
abstract: Flow state, characterized by deep engagement and immersion during challenging activities, represents a valuable mental state with significant implications for learning, performance, and rehabilitation outcomes. While flow has been extensively studied behaviorally, objective neurophysiological detection methods suitable for real-world deployment remain limited. Electroencephalography (EEG) offers a promising avenue for flow detection due to its accessibility, portability, and superior temporal resolution; however, the utility of consumer-grade EEG devices for robust, and subject independent flo

title: Modeling the pathway from transformational leadership to innovative work behavior via AI readiness: advancing SDG 4 and SDG 8 in Indonesian higher education
abstract: Drawing on a cross-sectional survey of 250 lecturers and administrative staff from Indonesian higher education institutions (HEIs), this study examined the statistical relationships among transformational leadership, AI readiness, and innovative work behavior (IWB) using partial least squares structural equation modeling (PLS-SEM). The findings showed that transformational leadership was positively associated with AI readiness (β = 0.654, p < 0.001) and IWB (β = 0.322, p < 0.001), while AI readiness was positively associated with IWB (β = 0.451, p < 0.001). title: Assessment of Household Water Security in Makurdi Town, Benue State, Nigeria
abstract: Makurdi town is contending with many water related issues that impede efforts targeted at achieving water security for the growing population. Water security is a multidimensional concept that seeks to address the array of issues related to water. Previous studies in Nigeria and Makurdi in particular, employ a methodology for water security assessment that merely accounts for water access or water scarcity, thereby limiting the scope of the concept. title: Robustness Evaluation of Hyperspectral Image Classification Models Using Degradation-Aware Metrics
abstract: Hyperspectral image classification studies are generally evaluated on clean benchmark datasets and often report high-accuracy values. However, because real sensor data can be affected by different degradations, such as Gaussian, impulse, stripe, dead-line, and mixed noise, clean-data performance alone may be insufficient to explain the reliability of models under practical conditions. In this study, SVM, k-NN, 1D-CNN, 2D-CNN, 3D-CNN, Hybrid CNN, Dense CNN, and a transformer-based model were evaluated on the Indian Pines, Pavia University, and Salinas datasets under controlled noise scenarios.

title: Enhancing wear resistance of tool steel materials for industrial automobile component using cryogenic treatment
abstract: The durability of sheet metal punching tools depends largely on their wear resistance and frictional behaviour during service. Deep cryogenic treatment (DCT) has emerged as an effective post-heat-treatment process for improving the tribological performance of tool steels. This study experimentally investigates the influence of DCT on the wear characteristics and service life of three commercially used tool steels, namely EN31, AISI D2, and OHNS, employed for punching and piercing 4.5 mm thick SAPH440 sheet steel. title: Multi-trait Analysis of Pigmentation Traits in Relation to Skin and Ocular Cancers: Relevance for Evolutionary Medicine
abstract: Abstract Background and objectives Pigmentary traits (skin, hair, eye colour, tanning response) are epidemiologically linked to skin and ocular cancers, but the extent and nature of shared genetic architecture remain incompletely defined. In this study we explored to what extent pigmentation- and cancer-associated variants exhibit pleiotropy. title: Delivering sustainable food: exploring college students’ willingness to pay for carbon labels in China via a choice experiment
abstract: The rapid expansion of online food delivery has intensified concerns about packaging waste and carbon emissions, making sustainable consumption an increasingly important component of the sector’s low-carbon transition. Whether environmental information disclosure can shift consumers’ choices toward lower-carbon alternatives is therefore an important issue for improving the sustainability of digital food-delivery platforms. title: Green Accounting and Economic Sustainability of listed Oil and Gas Firms in Nigeria
abstract: This study evaluated the effect of green accounting on economic sustainability of listed oil and gas firms in Nigeria. Specifically, the study examined the effect environmental pollution prevention disclosure, waste management disclosure and carbon emission on the economic sustainability of listed oil and gas firms in Nigeria. The study deployed ex-post facto research design. Eight listed oil and gas firms made up the population of the study while the sample size was six oil and gas firms. title: The carbon content of billionaire wealth: composition, concentration and taxation
abstract: Abstract How large are billionaires' carbon footprints? While increasing evidence highlights large disparities in emissions between and within countries, detailed individual‐level data on emissions portfolios remain scarce. In this paper, we analyse the wealth composition of the top 500 billionaires and construct a dataset linking each of their assets to emissions. abstract: Malaria remains a major public health concern in Benin, and its seasonal pattern may be influenced by local climate. This study examined associations between bioclimatic conditions and reported uncomplicated and severe malaria cases in the second district of Cotonou. Monthly temperature, relative humidity and rainfall data for 1995-2024 were obtained from Météo-Bénin, while monthly malaria data for 2005-2024 were obtained from the Littoral Departmental Health Directorate. abstract: Biomass-based hydrogen production represents a promising pathway to reduce the environmental impacts associated with fossil-based hydrogen. In thermochemical pathways, biomass is typically converted into intermediate streams such as bio-oil prior to hydrogen production. title: The population dynamics in China: understanding the role of spread and backwash effect
abstract: Considering the declining population growth and increasing intra-provincial migration in China, the population issue becomes crucial for the sustainable development of the Chinese economy. We utilize data of 2010 and 2020 China Census to study the impact of the “spread-backwash” effects of large cities on county-level population dynamics over the past decade and investigate the potential mechanisms. title: Análisis informétrico del impacto social en la producción científica de Argentina, Brasil, Chile, Colombia y México (2016–2024)
abstract: En el contexto de los debates recientes sobre la función social de la ciencia, el impacto social ha adquirido una presencia creciente como categoría discursiva en la evaluación de la ciencia, especialmente en América Latina. Este artículo analiza, desde un enfoque informétrico, la manera en que el impacto social es tematizado en la literatura científica producida en Argentina, Brasil, Chile, Colombia y México durante el periodo 2016–2024. title: Digital Trust as Halal Tourism Infrastructure: A Documentary Framework for SME Competitiveness in the Hat Yai–Songkhla Border Economy
abstract: Halal tourism scholarship documents how faith-aligned service quality shapes satisfaction and trust, while e-commerce research establishes the structural role of trust, perceived risk, and information quality in online transactions. These two literatures have developed largely in parallel. title: Catalyst or constraint? Academic independent directors and corporate consciousness of climate change under ESG practice
abstract: This study investigates the role of academically experienced independent directors (AIDs) in shaping firms’ climate risk consciousness in Chinese listed companies. Using a panel dataset from 2008 to 2023 and fixed effects regression models, we find that a higher proportion of AIDs significantly enhances firms’ climate risk consciousness. The effect operates through two mechanisms: improving the quality of corporate information disclosure and shaping executives’ environmental cognition. title: Platformed citizenship rupture: Nepal’s Generation Z protest and the governance consequences of youth digital activism
abstract: This article develops the concept of platformed citizenship rupture to explain moments when digitally mediated protest unsettles established relations of political legitimacy and moves toward provisional debate over leadership, representation, and governance. Using Nepal’s 2025 Generation Z protest as an illustrative case, it operationalizes this concept through the Digital Momentum–Governance Translation Model. abstract: Abstract This study presents a systematic bibliometric framework to evaluate global morphometric research on Apis mellifera published between 1982 and 2024. Using a PRISMA-guided screening process and bibliometric analysis conducted with the Bibliometrix R package, a total of 199 peer-reviewed studies were analyzed to identify publication trends, methodological shifts, thematic structures, and geographic patterns. abstract: Abstract Accurate modeling of multi-timeseries measurements (MTM) is the key to remaining useful life (RUL) prediction of advanced equipment. title: Organizational Culture as a Driver of Employee Performance: The Mediating Effects of Job Satisfaction and Motivation
abstract: This article examines the effect of organizational culture on worker performance through worker motivation and job satisfaction. The research used a quantitative approach with a cross-sectional strategy. Primary data were collected from 291 employees across various organizations using a structured questionnaire. Each construct was measured with a five-point Likert scale, and the measurement scales were adapted from previous reliable studies. abstract: William Shakespeare is renowned in English and world literature for his masterful ly crafted characters. In this paper we will explore all textual indicators of characterization in William Shakespeare’s play Richard III, used for the construction of Richard`s character, based on the method proposed by the classical narratology theorist Shlomith Rimmon-Kenan in her study Narrative fiction (1983). abstract: West Africa in the past decade has witnessed an alarming resurgence of military coups. This article examines the implications of this coup wave for regional integration as it affects Economic Community of West African States (ECOWAS) using democratic theory as its framework. This article is predicated upon qualitative method of research, utilizing secondary sources of data collection from Journals, newspaper publications, online news outlets, official documents, etc. Anchored on the preceding methodology, we reviewed the literature on African coups and regional integration. title: El dinero endógeno como teoría del capitalismo
abstract: This paper explains that money has always been an endogenous magnitude within any economic systems. Money’s endogeneity means that the supply of money results from a demand for it. In particular, when a bank provides a credit line to any kind of borrowers, the payment by the latter gives rise to a new bank deposit, which increases therefore the money supply. This causality is the opposite of what mainstream economists believe, as both Joseph A. Schumpeter and Basil J. Moore explained famously. title: Listening to the mountain: oral history, biocultural heritage, and sustainability transitions in Serra da Estrela
abstract: This article draws on a corpus of oral history interviews collected in Serra da Estrela, Portugal, to examine how community memory, territorial knowledge, and lived relationships with the mountain contribute to understanding socio-ecological change and rethinking sustainability in a context of climate disruption. abstract: This study examined school principals’ achievement motives and leadership styles in Olutanga Island District Schools, Division of Zamboanga Sibugay, as a basis for developing a school leader development program. It was anchored on McClelland’s Achievement Motivation Theory, Achievement Goal Theory, and Path-Goal Theory of Leadership. title: The Negotiation of New Heights and Essence by Bakossi Traditional Authorities Under Colonial Rule
abstract: This paper aims to present the pride and prejudice of the Bakossi traditional authority in the south-west region of Cameroon. It shows how the imposition of colonial rule led to a systematic abuse and disregard for the local institutions that were so dear to the people. title: Board Composition and Strategic Decision Making: A Study of Diversity and Expertise in Nigeria
abstract: Board composition plays a critical role in shaping corporate governance and strategic decisionmaking. This study examines the impact of board diversity and expertise on organizational effectiveness, particularly in the Nigerian business landscape. The research highlights that board diversity—encompassing gender, age, professional background, and ethnicity—enhances innovation, risk-taking, and decision-making quality. title: Nexus Between Participation in Non-Formal Adult Education Programmes and Women’s Empowerment in Turkana County, Kenya
abstract: Education plays a critical role in promoting women’s empowerment, yet women in nomadic pastoralist communities in Kenya continue to face barriers such as poverty, cultural restrictions, early marriage, domestic responsibilities, and limited access to formal schooling. In Turkana County, these challenges contribute to low literacy levels and limit women’s economic participation, decision-making, and social and political engagement. title: From ownership to stewardship: reimagining intellectual property governance through the Knowledge Commons Framework
abstract: Contemporary intellectual property (IP) governance remains strongly shaped by proprietary logics of exclusivity, control, and rights allocation, even as knowledge production becomes increasingly collaborative, cumulative, and digitally mediated. This study examines how the Knowledge Commons Framework can inform a stewardship-oriented reconceptualization of IP governance. title: Lévy Opposition-Based Learning Bat Algorithm for Combined Economic and Emission Dispatch
abstract: Electricity demand is increasing daily due to the growth of industries. To meet this demand, it is essential to increase power generation, improve economic efficiency, and control pollutant emissions. A power system focuses on grid stability, which neglects economic efficiency and pollutant emissions. To overcome this problem, a Combined Economic and Emission Dispatch (CEED) problem is proposed. title: Digital traceability systems in multi-tier supply networks: an information integration perspective from the fashion industry
abstract: Purpose This study investigates how digital traceability systems operate as inter-organisational information systems (IOS) enabling information integration, visibility, and coordination across multi-tier fashion supply networks. Focusing on how firms build digital traceability infrastructures in anticipation of forthcoming regulatory requirements, the study examines the strategic, institutional, and operational drivers, socio-technical mechanisms, and traceability configurations that shape data integration and governance across organisational tiers. title: Same event, different stories: a corpus-assisted critical discourse analysis of the 20th CPC National Congress in Chinese and US mainstream media
abstract: As China’s first major national congress in the post-pandemic era, the 20th CPC National Congress has considerable domestic and international influence. This study employs a corpus-assisted critical discourse analysis to investigate the divergent discursive constructions of the Congress across six mainstream Chinese and American media outlets. title: A Review of Sustainable Trade Practices and Employment in Uganda
abstract: The intersection of sustainable trade governance and labour-market outcomes has become a central concern for low-income, agriculture-dependent economies, yet the evidence base linking specific sustainable trade practices to employment changes in Uganda remains fragmented. This narrative review synthesises the available literature across five dimensions: voluntary sustainability certification schemes, environmental provisions in trade agreements, gender-differentiated employment outcomes, Aid for Trade and green trade facilitation, and skills development for sustainable production. title: Violence at Peekskill! Paul Robeson, Anti-Communism, and Populist Fascism Among Veterans
abstract: In 1949, two riots rocked Paul Robeson concerts in Peekskill, New York. The riots were provoked by local veterans’ organizations and were not anomalous, as the American Legion and other groups intentionally targeted Robeson and his public appearances. Though scholars have examined the Peekskill riots and their relationship to Paul Robeson’s increased radicalism and his declining popularity, this article centers veterans’ organizing against Robeson as intentional, and the violence as unexceptional. abstract: Given the activities of industries in Rivers state, residents are exposed to the consequences of climate change, yet, how they view the phenomenon of climate change can be influenced by how Port Harcourt-based newspapers treat climate change in terms of importance and frames, hence, this study, which is aimed at comparatively analysing how the following Port Harcourt-based newspapers, The Tide, National Network, Weekly Star and the Port Harcourt Telegraph, framed climate change in their reportage from January 2023-December 2024. title: Brazil’s Rare Earth Elements Landscape: From Geological Endowment to Mine-to-Magnet Integration—Operations, Resources, Bottlenecks, Market Prospects, and Research Gaps
abstract: Brazil has re-emerged as one of the most consequential rare-earth jurisdictions outside Asia, but geological scale alone does not determine whether it can capture strategic and economic value from rare earth elements (REEs). abstract: Abstract Carbon dioxide (CO 2 ) utilization has emerged as a promising pathway to convert a major greenhouse gas into value‐added products, offering both environmental and economic benefits. title: Environmental law as developmental infrastructure: conditions for green trade compliance and firm upgrading in Vietnam
abstract: In Vietnam’s export-oriented economy, environmental law now operates at the intersection of domestic regulation, trade governance and corporate organization. This article develops developmental compliance capacity as a firm-level construct explaining how enterprises interpret green requirements, build routines and evidence, coordinate suppliers and, where organizational conditions permit, turn compliance into learning and upgrading. abstract: Where should one look for fungi in a bog? Historically, fungal diversity in peatlands has been studied primarily in peat itself – understandably, given that peat is the defining feature of these ecosystems – using methods such as sporocarp-based observations and microfungal culturing. Although informal science learning is increasingly recognized as important, limited research has examined how knowledge and authority are constructed and negotiated among family members in daily life. abstract: Abstract Background Out‐of‐hospital cardiac arrest (OHCA) is a leading cause of death worldwide. abstract: ‘Brainrot’ is a relatively new concept within fields such as anthropology, cognitive science, and psychology. title: Individualism Without Individuality: Friedrich Hayek and the Neoliberal Citizen
abstract: ABSTRACT Critics of neoliberalism increasingly examine its corrosive effects on democracy. Scholars often turn to Friedrich Hayek's political theory, arguing that it produces citizens who passively conform to spontaneous social orders. abstract: The Challenger expedition marked a turning point for marine biology, revolutionizing the scientific research of ocean life. title: The dynamics of early transoceanic voyages: A resource-coupled model of crew health and survival
abstract: The great transoceanic voyages of the Age of Discovery imposed severe human costs on the crews that sustained them. Long travel durations, deteriorating sanitary conditions and finite food and water supplies created an environment in which disease, exhaustion and mortality became central features of maritime expansion. abstract: This study evaluates quality-related characteristics of a long-cycle engineering education model from the perspective of education for sustainable development. The aim was to assess whether the model's documented curricular architecture, its interpretive alignment with international engineering-education benchmarks, and student self-assessments provide convergent evidence of its relevance for sustainability-oriented engineering training. title: Global Black Speculative Collage
abstract: Abstract Since the turn of this century, artists of African descent have worked to refract the relation between Black Studies and African Studies, often blurring the lines between these two fields. Braiding together the speculative mode and the practice of collage, Chino Amobi’s 2017 electronic music album Paradiso and Wangechi Mutu’s 2014 multimedia painting series Nguva na Nyoka cultivate opacity, otherworldliness, fragmentation, and disorder. The author examines how these works offer singular lenses into questions of gender, antiblackness, and global black belonging that reframe distinction

title: From Anthropocentrism to Hydrocentric Ethics: A Qur’anic Reading of QS. Al-Anbiya’ [21]:30 and the Global Water Crisis
abstract: The global water crisis raises fundamental questions about how human relationships with water should be understood beyond its treatment as an economic resource. This study examines QS. Al-Anbiyā’ [21]:30 and related Qur’anic passages to develop a water-centered ethical perspective in response to contemporary ecological challenges. Employing qualitative library research and tafsīr mawdū’ī (thematic exegesis), the study analyzes classical and contemporary interpretations by al-Qurtubī, Tantāwī Jawharī, Ibn ‘Āshūr, and M. journal: Al-Fahmu Jurnal Ilmu Al-Qur an dan Tafsir

title: Under pressure: Use of hyperbaric chamber therapy for management of dissolved gas disorders in fish—15 cases (2015–2025)
abstract: OBJECTIVE: Our objective was to describe clinical findings, treatment protocols, and outcomes in captive fish presenting with ocular and/or buoyancy disorders attributed to dissolved gas disease undergoing novel treatment with hyperbaric therapy. METHODS: Electronic medical records were reviewed for 15 teleost fish comprising 10 species housed at a public aquarium and treated between 2015 and 2025 with hyperbaric chamber therapy for exophthalmos (n = 8), intraocular gas (n = 5), buphthalmos (n = 5), and/or positive buoyancy (n = 7). title: PROCEDIMENTOS DE SEGURANÇA EM SERVIÇOS COM ELETRICIDADE EM CONDIÇÃO SUBAQUÁTICA
abstract: Este artigo analisa os procedimentos de segurança relacionados ao uso de eletricidade em operações subaquáticas, considerando a crescente complexidade do mergulho profissional e a ampliação do uso de equipamentos elétricos nesse ambiente. abstract: Abstract Corporate psychopaths, identifiable as ruthlessly unethical leaders in business, have regularly appeared throughout recent history. However, in this current paper, we explore what may be the World’s earliest identified corporate psychopath operating within a multinational company: the ‘Vereenigde Oostindische Compagnie’ (the VOC or Dutch East India Company). abstract: Type of the article: Research ArticleAbstractGrowing competition among global tourism destinations has made it essential to understand what drives tourists to intend to return and recommend a place. This study aims to examine the direct and indirect relationships among destination image, tourist motivation, perceived value, destination experience, destination satisfaction, and destination loyalty intentions in Da Nang, Vietnam, in order to identify the key drivers of self-reported tourist loyalty in an emerging tourism destination. title: Self-consistent fragmentation in dynamically dense turbulent fibre suspensions
abstract: Fragmentation of slender fibres by turbulence controls length distributions in many natural and industrial suspensions, yet most theories assume a prescribed carrier flow, and treat fibres as dilute and dynamically passive. Here, we develop a self-consistent kinetic description for fragmentation in the opposite limit of sufficiently dense fibre suspensions that back-react on the turbulence. title: Four new species and new distributional records for Australian caddisflies in the genus Ecnomus McLachlan (Trichoptera: Ecnomidae)
abstract: A recent surge in collection of fresh caddisfly material for molecular studies resulted in the discovery of four new species of Ecnomus, the first since a major review of Australian members of the genus by Cartwright in 1990. Three of the new species are from north-eastern Queensland: E. giblini sp. nov., E. lesteri sp. nov. and E. mundyi sp. nov., the latter resulting from recognition that E. apiculatus Cartwright, 1990 comprises two distinct species. The fourth new species, E. barwonensis sp. nov., also derives from a split from another species, the very similar E. continentalis Ulmer, 1916.

title: ‘From humanitarian catastrophe to planetary armageddon: plotting the 1922 Smyrna “holocaust” through an Anthropocene lens’
abstract: How should we understand the Asia Minor catastrophe as encapsulated in the Smyrna ‘holocaust’ of September 1922? As a specific tragedy inflicted on Greeks, Armenians and the other peoples ethnically cleansed and/or, genocided by Kemal Atatürk, and, thus, forever engraved within their specific cultural memories? Or as something over and beyond genocide; a powerful indicator, perhaps, of the trajectory of twentieth-century prometheanism and ‘development’, of system dysfunction, even of the cul-de-sac condition of human society in its Anthropocene twilight? title: Between Segregation and Permeability: The VOC’s Spatial Dilemma in Zeelandia Facing External Actors and Intervening Groups (1624–1662)
abstract: Abstract This study re-evaluates the “dual city” model through the case of the VOC’s Zeelandia in the seventeenth century. It argues that the settlement’s spatial order was crucially shaped not only by Dutch-indigenous relations but also by an external force: Chinese pirate-merchant confederations. This Chinese intermediary group, forming the socio-economic core, fostered a colonial dynamic of simultaneous dependence and distrust. title: Movilidad, subsistencia y uso del espacio en el valle Lapataia–Acigami: aportes desde el sitio PNTF1 (Holoceno tardío, Tierra del Fuego)
abstract: El objetivo de este trabajo es efectuar una evaluación sobre las estrategias de movilidad, subsistencia y uso del espacio de las poblaciones cazadoras-recolectoras que ocuparon el valle Lapataia-Acigami (canal Beagle, Tierra del Fuego) durante el Holoceno tardío. title: From one tree to the canopy: an evolutionary design trajectory for tethered robotics in forest environments
abstract: Forest robotics has largely evolved along a ground-first and flight-dominant trajectory, treating the canopy as a region to observe or briefly access rather than a habitat to inhabit. In this Perspective, we propose an alternative canopy-first framework in which robots operate through anchoring, suspension, and tension-mediated interaction with the environment. We trace the progression from ground and aerial systems to perching mechanisms, identifying their shared limitation as transient canopy interaction. title: Late Permian core-surface-magnetosphere conditions revealed by single crystal paleointensities from the Emeishan large igneous province
abstract: The Late Permian encompasses the end-Guadalupian and end-Permian extinctions, commonly linked to emplacement of the ca. 260 million-year-old Emeishan and ca. 252 million-year-old Siberian large igneous provinces, respectively. During this interval, geomagnetic intensity declined from the strong Permo-Carboniferous Reversed Polarity Superchron (PCRS) state, yet the magnitude and potential biological consequences of this weakening remain unclear. title: Development of a Multiplex Polymerase Chain Reaction Assay for Differentiating Three Lactococcus Species Associated With Piscine Lactococcosis
abstract: Piscine lactococcosis is an important bacterial disease of farmed fish. The causative agents, Lactococcus garvieae, Lactococcus petauri and Lactococcus formosensis, are closely related, which complicates species-level identification. We developed a conventional multiplex PCR assay targeting species-specific genes identified by comparative genomic analysis. Average nucleotide identity reassignment of 441 publicly available genome assemblies identified 111 L. garvieae, 255 L. petauri and 75 L. formosensis genomes. title: The Stability‐Instability Paradox and the Evolving Balance of Terror in the Middle East
abstract: Abstract In launching its war on Iran, Washington has committed a grave mistake by allowing a weakened Islamic Republic to reconstitute a regional balance of terror. This article shows how the Cold War‐era stability‐instability paradox has been restored in a new form, creating an equilibrium that discourages open warfare while reducing the advantages Israel and the United States had gained over Iran during the previous two years. title: Contributions from a small collection of carnivorous snails of family Streptaxidae (Eupulmonata, Streptaxoidea) from Cambodia, with description of new species
abstract: The present study substantially expands the known streptaxid fauna of Cambodia, raising the total richness to seven species across five genera. Four new species from Stung Treng Province are described, and two new country records are reported and re-described. title: Stephanie L. Watwood, 1975-2026
The global cost of automobility
abstract: This study quantifies the private and social costs of global automobility and evaluates the potential economic benefits of a transition to shared electric autonomous mobility-as-a-service (E-AV-MaaS). Using comprehensive cost components, including accidents, emissions, air pollution, noise, infrastructure, land use, and resource impacts, it is estimated that private car travel currently incurs approximately USD 0.16 per vehicle-kilometer in private costs and USD 0.55 per vehicle-kilometer in social costs. title: Evidence of genome-wide relaxed selection on mildly deleterious mutations in an ancient subterranean catfish
abstract: About one hundred subterranean catfish species have been described, resulting from repeated colonization of cave environments by multiple surface lineages. Most cave-dwelling species are found in the Americas, in particular in South America, but a few species also live in Central and North America. title: Facial emotional responses to visual representations of deprived experiences in ICE environments: an exploratory analog space mission case study
abstract: Isolated, confined, and extreme (ICE) environments, such as space analog habitats, expose individuals to prolonged sensory and social deprivation, posing risks to psychological well-being. This exploratory study examined whether visual representations of everyday experiences unavailable during isolation elicit measurable facial emotional responses in analog astronauts. Data were collected from eight participants during two 14-day missions at the LunAres Research Station. title: “Women of the Happy Life”: Prostitution, Public Morality, and Venereal Disease in US‐Occupied Nicaragua, 1912–33
abstract: ABSTRACT During the years of the US occupation (1912–33), Nicaragua's government legally regulated prostitution. Convinced of their objectives to protect society's moral and public health, politicians embarked on a long struggle to apprehend, quarantine, and segregate female prostitutes nationwide. Through a comparative analysis of these codes, this article discusses the language and changes in these regulations to examine the extent to which the broader context of US intervention shaped local perceptions and actions regarding non‐elite female sexuality. title: Cultural heritage objects in lack of anchoring communities. An unfinished reflection on a relational ethics of care
abstract: The return of cultural artefacts taken during the colonial era seems to be a matter of course in our time. But what happens if the communities to whom these objects should be returned have for long ceased to exist and their successors are involved in a civil war? At the example of manuscripts taken from Ethiopia after the Battle of Maqdala, this contribution discusses ethical, legal and social issues (ELSI) surrounding such cultural heritage objects and calls into question the premises of recent calls for their return. abstract: Introduction Commercial hypersonic point-to-point (P2P) travel promises intercontinental flights in under 90 min, yet viability depends on systems-level integration of advanced technologies and infrastructure. This paper addresses the critical question of whether such travel can be technically feasible, economically viable, and environmentally sustainable within the coming decades. title: Builders, Building, and the Built
abstract: Motorable roads have become such an essential part of the Himalaya that they are celebrated and prayed for. But who are the people who build them? The army, engineers, and the state are usually credited with the construction of high-altitude roads in India, but the road workers who often endure significant hardship while performing this labor have largely remained invisible in both national discourses and academic scholarship. abstract: Abstract The Pamir, located at the northwestern margin of the Tibetan Plateau, is undergoing E–W extension within its interior, accommodated by micro‐block motions along major fault systems; however, the mechanisms governing this modern block kinematics remain elusive. Here, we present an updated crustal shear‐wave velocity model of the region, developed via adjoint‐state surface‐wave traveltime tomography. title: Research on immersive emotional experience design of interactive digital video art
abstract: With the comprehensive popularization of media digitalization and interactive technology, new art forms such as VR documentaries, interactive videos, film-game integration animations, and immersive light and shadow installations have emerged rapidly. title: “Not All Smugglers are the Same: Some are Righteous and Some are Crooked:” Paternalistic Patriotism, Race, and the Syrian Migrant Smuggling Industry (1900-1914)
abstract: Abstract Smugglers dominated the major routes of migration from the Ottoman Empire to the United States starting from the second half of the nineteenth century. Using the Syrian American press in New York, this article explores how Syrian diasporic activists in the United States married smuggling with patriotism against the backdrop of anti-immigrant nativism. It demonstrates the diasporic impulse to reform the Syrian migrant smuggling economy in line with the racial prerequisites of transatlantic border regimes. title: Health Care Corporate Sponsorships in North American Professional Sports Leagues
abstract: This cross-sectional study examines trends in professional sports league jersey sponsorship by health care delivery organizations across 4 major North American professional sports leagues.

abstract: African literature critically interrogates Eurocentric discourses, ideologically driven narratives that construct black subjectivity as the subordinate Other within a white-normative epistemology. This white-supremacist ideology emerges as an exclusionary system of identification that fragments the reality of African people, subjecting them to alienation, segregation, and violence. title: FROM SCANDINAVIA TO THE LEVANT: THE LATE BRONZE AGE METAL TRADE AND NURAGIC SARDINIA
abstract: Summary A growing body of evidence suggests that Nuragic Sardinia played a role, as yet poorly understood, in the metal trade between Scandinavia, Atlantic Europe, and the Mediterranean during the Bronze Age. Provenance studies based on lead isotope and chemical analyses of copper‐based – and to a minor extent lead – artefacts from both continental Europe and the Mediterranean indicate that metals of Sardinian origin were exported and used in different and far apart regions over the second half of the second millennium BC. title: A new Lecidea species from Dismal Island (Antarctic Peninsula, Antarctica) supported by morphological, chemical, and nrITS phylogenetic evidence
abstract: Antarctica remains one of the least explored regions of the world in terms of lichen diversity, and many remote localities still harbor undescribed taxa. In this study, a new saxicolous lichen species belonging to the genus Lecidea is described from Dismal Island, located in the East Antarctic Peninsula region, based on an integrative taxonomic approach combining morphological, anatomical, chemical, and nrITS phylogenetic evidence. title: Menu Engineering for Competitive Advantage: Optimizing Sales Performance in Star-Rated Hotels in Bali
abstract: Background: While F&B outlets are recognized as critical revenue drivers, menu management has often been treated as an operational function rather than a strategic capability. Building on the Resource-Based View (RBV), the Service-Profit Chain (SPC), and Integrated Marketing Communication (IMC), this study reframes menus as dynamic revenue systems that integrate analytics, customer voice, and design interventions. title: Entwining sound, space and narratives. Sound design approaches in exhibitions
abstract: This article explores the evolution of exhibition design, focusing on the integration of sound as a key narrative and experiential element. In recent decades, technological advances and discoveries in neuroscience have influenced the design of exhibition spaces, transforming them into multimodal experiences that go beyond mere visual engagement. Sound emerges as a central tool, capable of shaping the emotional, spatial, and narrative dimensions of exhibitions. title: Unravelling gas-particle partitioning dynamics in cooking aerosol oxidation through FIGAERO-CIMS analysis
abstract: Cooking emissions are increasingly important sources of organic aerosol in densely populated urban areas as clean-air actions reduce emissions from industrial activities and fossil-fuel combustion. Their atmospheric evolution and environmental and health effects remain difficult to assess because of the complexity of their composition and transformation pathways. title: Lichens and lichenicolous fungi of Prins Karls Forland (Svalbard Archipelago)
abstract: The paper presents data on lichens and lichenicolous fungi for Prins Karls Forland (NW of Svalbard archipelago). For the island, 283 species of lichens and 21 lichenicolous fungi have been identified to date. Seventy species of lichens and 17 lichenicolous fungi are listed for the first time for the study area, of which Arthonia epipolytropa, Gyalecta peziza, Lasiosphaeriopsis christiansenii, Porpidia rugosa, and Sclerococcum protothallinum are reported for the first time for the Svalbard archipelago. abstract: Abstract The semiarid landscapes of Northeastern Brazil host disjunct savanna formations, often broadly categorized under the term ‘northeastern cerrados’, whose biogeographical connections with the core Cerrado and Caatinga domains remain debated. While savanna formations on sedimentary basins have been extensively characterized, those established on crystalline substrates remain poorly understood. title: Rare and delicious: from monster to meal in Japanese gourmet fantasy manga
abstract: This study examines how gourmet fantasy manga, particularly Delicious in Dungeon and Campfire Cooking in Another World with My Absurd Skill, reconfigure monstrosity through the act of cooking and consumption. Drawing on textual, semiotic, and cultural hermeneutic analysis, the study argues that such transformations are not merely aesthetic, but grounded in deeper symbolic and cultural logics. title: Personal health impacts of adventurous outdoor learning
abstract: Abstract This article examines the burgeoning field of study exploring links between health, wellbeing, and adventurous outdoor learning. Key terms (outdoor learning, adventure, nature, health, wellbeing, and wellness) are defined before delving into dimensions of wellbeing that contribute to human health, with specific outdoor learning components for meaningful development of these dimensions. title: Morphological diversity and phenotypic characterization of Styrax spp: Implications for conservation and breeding strategies
abstract: Abstract The lack of knowledge about phenotypic variation in Styrax spp. is a major constraint to efforts aimed at improving its resin yield, adaptability, and sustainable utilization. This study assessed the morphological diversity of Styrax spp. populations collected from both Humbang Hasundutan and Tapanuli Utara Regencies, North Sumatra, Indonesia, using correlation analysis, Principal Component Analysis (PCA), and Agglomerative Hierarchical Clustering (AHC). abstract: Abstract Ctesiphon, the capital of the Sasanian Empire (ca. 224–651 CE), was a major center of political power and artistic production in Mesopotamia. Excavations conducted in the 1920s–30s by the Staatliche Museen zu Berlin and the Metropolitan Museum of Art revealed an extensive corpus of stucco decorations from Sasanian and Early Islamic contexts. abstract: Este artículo estudia el contenido feminista presente en los debates constitucionales de 2022 en Chile, a través de un conjunto heterogéneo de textos publicados entre 2018 y 2022. title: Two new species of the genus Eremiothrips Priesner (Thysanoptera, Thripidae) from Saudi Arabia
abstract: The genus Eremiothrips Priesner, which inhabits xeric environments, is studied. The male of E. brunneus (zur Strassen) is described for the first time. Two new species, E. tetraenae sp. nov . collected from Tetraena simplex and E. xerophilus sp. nov . from Tamarix sp., are also described. A key to the Eremiothrips species lacking drepanae on abdominal tergite IX is provided.

title: Insights into morpho-biochemical characterisation and β-ODAP profiling of diverse genotypes of grasspea
abstract: Grasspea (Lathyrus sativus L.) is a versatile, climate-resilient legume valued for its nutritional richness and low input requirements. However, the presence of the neurotoxin β-N-oxalyl-L-α, β-diaminopropionic acid (β-ODAP) has limited its popularity. The present study aimed to identify promising low-ODAP grasspea genotypes for rice-fallow ecosystems of the Gangetic Plains of India through comprehensive morpho-biochemical characterisation. Fifteen genotypes of diverse origin were evaluated in a randomized complete block design (RCBD) with 3 replications and observations were recorded from fiv

title: Distributed Agent-Based Scheduling of Smart Port Operations under Cost and Emissions Constraints
abstract: Abstract This paper presents a distributed, emission-aware scheduling framework for smart port energy management, designed to coordinate heterogeneous flexible electric loads under operational, economic, and environmental constraints. The proposed approach addresses the coordinated scheduling of refrigerated containers (reefers), plug-in electric vehicles (PEVs), and shore-to-ship power supply systems, with the objective of reducing total operational cost while satisfying asset-level constraints and ship-level and port-level emission limits. title: From forbidden site to global attraction: Alula's narrative re-engineering
abstract: This paper examines the socio-political and religious transformations in Saudi Arabia's AlUla region, with a focus on Hegra. Once avoided for religious reasons, the site has been repurposed within Vision 2030. This study offers a systematic textual account of this narrative shift using Critical Discourse Analysis (CDA) on three corpora: state documents (including the tourism website), media, and religious texts. abstract: Las interacciones y el vínculo generado entre los seres humanos y los animales domésticos han perdurado a lo largo del tiempo. Este vínculo ha estado relacionado con la compañía, la reducción de los niveles de estrés y el apoyo social que representan. title: A Perspective on the Historical Role and Future of Bactris Gasipaes as a Food Crop
abstract: Peach palm (Bactris gasipaes) is a domesticated perennial of the tropical Americas historically cultivated within Indigenous agroforestry systems. Interdisciplinary evidence indicates that it functioned as a staple in pre-Columbian Amazonia, embedded in diversified, human-managed forests. Despite its nutritional and agronomic potential, modern development efforts have not integrated it into contemporary food economies, largely due to a mismatch with prevailing models based on annual monocultures. title: Analysis of the current state and medium-term forecast of transport system development parameters up to 2028
abstract: The article presents an analysis of the dynamics of key indicators of the development of the Russian transportation industry in 2023–2025. It provides forecast values for the period up to 2028, taking into account current trends and exogenous macroeconomic parameters defined in the latest Forecast of the Social and Economic Development of the Russian Federation for 2026 and for the Planning Period of 2027 and 2028, as well as in other strategic documents.

title: Gleb Wataghin and his mission in Brazil: a memoir
abstract: Abstract This contribution, based on a talk delivered at the Workshop Ukrainian Contributions to Particle Physics: History and Prospects, offers a personal memoir of Gleb Wataghin (1899–1986) and his role in the institutional development of modern physics at the University of São Paulo and in Brazil. Born in what is now Ukraine and educated in Turin, Wataghin joined the newly created university in São Paulo in 1934, where he helped establish a physics department and research school. title: Global Sensitivity of Constraint Analysis method: Drag coefficient and Stall Speed selection for Small UAVs
abstract: The Constraint analysis method is applied in the early stages of aircraft conceptual design for determining preliminary sizing parameters such as wing loading and power loading. However, its application to small UAVs is challenged by uncertainties in several key input parameters, particularly those that require detailed geometric or aerodynamic information that is typically unavailable during the early design stages. title: A Multiplatform Chemical Perspective on Coffee Identity: Interplay Between Origin, Cultivar, and Fermentation Time
abstract: Abstract Green coffee bean chemistry is shaped by the geographic origin, plant genetics, and post-harvest processing, but their relative contributions across complementary chemical layers, within a single, tightly controlled context, remain comparatively underexplored. We applied a multiplatform strategy utilizing ICP-based multielement profiling, UHPLC-HRMS/MS polyphenolic analysis, 1 H NMR metabolomics to investigate the contributions of farm, cultivar, and fermentation time of green coffee. title: Contribution to the Phylinae Douglas & Scott, 1865 (Hemiptera: Heteroptera: Miridae) fauna of Türkiye with two new records from Northeastern Anatolia
abstract: This study is based on material of the subfamily Phylinae Douglas & Scott, 1865 collected from agricultural and non-agricultural habitats in the provinces of Ağrı, Ardahan, Iğdır, and Kars (Northeastern Anatolia, Türkiye) between 2021 and 2024. A total of 30 species belonging to 21 genera were identified. Among them, Oncotylus (Oncotylus) vitticeps Reuter, 1879, and Solenoxyphus candidatus (Reuter, 1879) are recorded from Türkiye for the first time. title: Nature-based Learning of Adults: A Scoping Review
abstract: Background Nature-based learning (NBL) has gained attention across experiential, outdoor, and sustainability-oriented education; however, research on adult learning in natural environments remains fragmented. Purpose This scoping review synthesizes 32 empirical studies published between 1996 and 2025 examining how adults learn in and with nature when natural environments function as active components of the learning process. title: The Legality of US-Israeli Joint Decapitation Operations in Iran: Crime of Aggression or Self-Defense?
abstract: Background: Following 2025's failed negotiations, the US-Israeli military operation Epic Fury on 28 February 2026 marked a sharp escalation against Iran's nuclear and military infrastructure and leadership through a major regional force build-up. Methodology: The study employs a legal doctrinal method, utilizing Article 8 bis of the Rome Statute, the Caroline Test, and International Humanitarian Law (IHL). title: Austrocedrus from the Late Cretaceous of Antarctica and its implications for the early evolution of southern cypresses (Callitroideae, Cupressaceae)
abstract: PREMISE: The modern distribution of the southern cypresses, Callitroideae (Cupressaceae), reflects a classic Gondwanan distribution. The initial diversification of Callitroideae is estimated to have occurred during the Cretaceous, yet fossils from this period are rare, hampering our understanding of its early evolutionary history. title: Empowering leadership as a pathway to enhance job satisfaction among college employees
abstract: The study aimed to determine the effect of empowering leadership on employees' job satisfaction. To support the purpose, the literature was reviewed, and theories were established to strengthen the study's title. The study employed a descriptive and correlational research design. To gather the data, validated questionnaires were used, and descriptive and inferential statistics were used to analyze the data. title: ‘The worst of all Turkish peoples’: Ibn Faḍlān’s travel account as British naval intelligence
abstract: Abstract The tenth-century CE Arabic travel account of Aḥmad Ibn Faḍlān has seen many reactions, receptions, and afterlives in Islamicate languages and in European settings. These relate both to the identity and presumed authority of Ibn Faḍlān as an eyewitness observer and presumed diplomat, and to the contents of his account. abstract: En la presente publicación se realiza una propuesta funcional y simbólica para el conjunto áureo procedente del santuario tartésico de El Carambolo (Camas, Sevilla). Para ello se han tomado como principales referentes las joyas y representaciones iconográficas chipriotas, sirias y asirias de los siglos X-VI a. C., así como el mito del Descenso de Inanna/Ishtar a los Infiernos. Como resultado, se ha dividido el tesoro en dos lotes. title: Ferry Retrouvé : Leaving the History of Empire Out of the “Liberal Moment” in France
abstract: This article examines how and why empire went missing from the liberal revival that began in 1970s France by examining a nineteenth-century political figure “rediscovered” during it: Jules Ferry, who as premier between 1880 and 1885 oversaw not only the creation of a secular school system in France, but also a huge burst of overseas expansion. In their portraits of him starting in the 1980s, historians such as François Furet and Mona Ozouf emphasized the former, while minimizing or excusing the latter. abstract: Contemporary air transport is one of the fastest-growing segments of the transportation market, providing the mobility of passengers and goods on a global scale. In response to increasing demand and growing interest in this mode of transport, the sector must continuously improve and adapt to changing market needs. This process is closely associated with dynamic changes in tax policy. title: Bajo asedio: la defensa de Filipinas de las incursiones neerlandesas (1600-1648)
abstract: La Compañía de las Indias Orientales neerlandesa (VOC), a lo largo de su enfrentamiento con la Monarquía Hispánica, realizó durante casi medio siglo más de una veintena de ataques de diferente índole sobre las Filipinas. El archipiélago se convirtió en un frente estratégico y activo de la guerra entre la Monarquía Hispánica y la República Neerlandesa durante la primera mitad del siglo XVII. title: The first bear raid and squeeze: Isaac Le Maire and the Dutch East India Company
abstract: Abstract In 1609, the Dutch East India Company (VOC) faced a bear raid by a syndicate of short sellers led by Isaac Le Maire, a former director. We reconstruct the forward trade between 1607 and 1611, the actions taken by the syndicate members, and the responses to these actions by the company. We argue that the bear syndicate members aimed for financial gain from share price declines, while their leader, Le Maire, participated for strategic reasons, that is, breaking up the VOC monopoly. With the development of space technologies, interest in them decreased in the second half of the 80s, but in the last decade it has grown again sharply. title: Low frequency offshore wind farm noise affects natural planktonic communities during an in situ microcosm experiment in Norwegian coastal waters
abstract: Abstract The effects of anthropogenic underwater noise, such as operational noise from offshore wind farms (OWFs), on plankton are poorly understood. A significant challenge in assessing the impact of noise on natural communities is the lack of holistic and ecologically relevant experimental setups mimicking soundscapes and communities under close-to-natural conditions. title: Seismic Experiment Studying the Origin of Auckland Volcanic Field: Phase I Seafloor Data Set
abstract: Abstract This article describes an ocean-bottom seismic data set collected offshore New Zealand’s North Island as part of a multinational amphibious experiment investigating the Auckland volcanic field. From August 2023 to September 2024, 20 broadband ocean-bottom seismographs were deployed at water depths of 1200–2700 m, yielding approximately one year of continuous recordings from 15 successfully recovered instruments.
