title: Constructing seascapes and social memory: Coastal burials in Neolithic Korea
abstract: In this paper, I explore how Incipient and Early Neolithic communities in coastal Korea used mortuary practices to make the sea socially meaningful—and how those practices were closely tied to marine adaptation and emerging subsistence strategies. Using a comparative dataset of coastal and island burial sites, I examine where burials were placed and how burial grounds were organized, including cemetery size, burial structure and interment method, body orientation, grave goods, and ritual features associated with funerary ceremonies. title: What are the seasonal changes in eukaryotic plankton communities and their trophic relationships in three Mediterranean coastal lagoons?
abstract: Coastal lagoons are systems threatened by anthropogenic pressures. In order to develop and apply adapted management strategies, it is essential to understand their ecological functioning. In particular, eukaryotic plankton communities play a fundamental role in sustaining the entire trophic network and functioning of the ecosystem. We used DNA-metabarcoding to study seasonal diversity and trophic interactions of plankton communities in three Corsican coastal lagoons with contrasting morphologies and functioning. title: Changing coastal distribution and life-history patterns of Inconnu in northwest Alaska
abstract: Climate change is driving shifts in fish distributions across Arctic ecosystems. Inconnu (Stenodus leucichthys) are an important subsistence and recreational fishing species and depend upon a mosaic of aquatic habitats that are rapidly changing. The freshwater migratory patterns of these fish are well-documented, but information on their coastal movement patterns and life histories are largely unknown. title: At least a fivefold gap in effective global marine protection
abstract: The Convention on Biological Diversity's ambitious target to "effectively conserve" 30% of the world's oceans in protected areas by 2030 risks being undermined by a primary focus on total area protected rather than realized conservation outcomes. Area-based assessments can overstate success because few marine protected areas (MPAs) possess strong restrictions and high compliance. Here, we estimate the extent that conservation outcomes are realized across the global MPA network for shallow reefs using standardized fish survey data. title: Adaptability Research on Different Civil Engineering Materials in Marine Environment
abstract: This study examines the adaptability of civil engineering materials in marine environments, investigating deterioration laws of five material types under multi - environmental coupling effects. title: Bioactive compounds from a soft coral-derived Bacillus sp.
abstract: Marine bacteria are an interesting issue for searching of natural bioactive compounds when rising up of drug resistant bacteria and incurable diseases. This is the first report on pure bioactive compounds from a Bacillus sp. strain C-1-10 isolated from the soft coral Alcyonium digitatum in the Baltic Sea. The strain C-1-10 showed capable of yielding at least 7 natural compounds on both Glucose Yeast Malt medium and Bannett medium. title: A Spatial Footprint Assessment Method for Mapping Port Transformation Areas: An Application to the Italian Ports Database
abstract: The Italian coastal zone is a dynamic and fragile environment that is characterized by high ecological vulnerability and subjected to strong anthropogenic pressures that significantly alter its natural morphology and environmental balance. In this scenario, port infrastructures represent about 35% of the Italian artificial coast and have a significant influence on coastal dynamics and seabed integrity. title: Quantifying Southern Hemisphere dust sources during the Last Glacial-Interglacial Transition using rare earth elements in the EPICA Dome C ice core
abstract: Dust deposits in ice cores provide a valuable archive of past atmospheric circulation, offering insights into climate dynamics during key climate transitions such as the last glacial termination. Here, we present a novel high-resolution reconstruction of dust provenance in the EPICA Dome C (EDC) ice core from 33.7 to 2.8 kyr BP, based on Rare Earth Element (REE) patterns. title: From a rock to a hard place: how carbonate rocks are born and made
abstract: James Hutton recognised that some components of sedimentary rocks have a biological and marine origin as they contain ‘ solid parts ’ (mainly calcite) of past sea life, and so might offer an archive of Earth's history. Much current research effort on carbonate rocks, those that are dominantly calcite and dolomite, has focussed on the application of diverse imaging and geochemical techniques designed to reveal Earth's record of changing oceanic chemistry, climate, tectonics and carbon cycle dynamics. title: Distribution and Diversity of Coral Growth Forms at Different Depths in Badi Island, South Sulawesi, Indonesia
abstract: Coral reefs are marine ecosystems composed primarily of calcium carbonate and characterized by diverse growth forms that reflect environmental conditions. Physicochemical factors, including water temperature, depth, and salinity, may influence coral growth and community distribution. This study aimed to analyze the distribution and diversity of coral growth forms and the physicochemical characteristics of the waters surrounding Badi Island, Pangkajene and Islands Regency, South Sulawesi, as baseline information for the inventory and assessment of coral reef ecosystem conditions. abstract: Human society is facing numerous environmental problems, including climate change, mainly caused by the burning of fossil fuels in power plants to obtain electrical and thermal energy. On the other hand, electricity consumption is increasing due to population growth, urbanization or economic development. In order to reduce greenhouse gas emissions, one of the proposed solutions was the development of renewable energy sources, including oceanic ones. title: Surveying Biodiverse Coral Reef Ecosystems Across the Tree of Life With Environmental DNA
abstract: A central challenge in evaluating biodiversity using environmental DNA (eDNA) metabarcoding is that each primer set has biases resulting in selective amplification of taxonomic diversity. Here we test 11 primer pairs to assess Central Pacific coral reef diversity in the five kingdoms of marine eukaryotes: Chromista, Fungi, Metazoa, Plantae and Protozoa. Zero-width OTUs (ZOTUs) were compared to public sequence databases and resolved to the finest taxonomic rank possible. abstract: Abstract Global sea level rise (SLR) is a widely appreciated threat to coastal wetlands. Modeled estimates of SLR thresholds beyond which coastal wetlands convert to open water suggest that landscape scale estimates of wetland loss vary with geomorphic setting, upland barriers to migration, vegetative tolerances to flooding, sediment supply, and tidal ranges among others. title: Fear, stigma and Uncertainty: The short and long-term effects of Ebola on survivors, affected families, and community in Bundibugyo, Western Uganda
abstract: In 2014, Uganda was identified as a high-risk country for Ebola Virus Disease (EVD), with a series of outbreaks recorded since 2000. In 2007, the second outbreak in Bundibugyo district resulted in 149 reported cases and 37 confirmed Ebola deaths. Through the outbreak response, a new strain of the Ebola virus (Bundibugyo ebolavirus) was discovered. abstract: Predictions about future extreme marine hazard events in the tropical South Pacific require, as a prerequisite, a robust knowledge of similar ancient event locations and frequency over the last millennia. title: The Impact of the Blue Economy on Economic Development in Lagos State, Nigeria
abstract: The blue economy, which involves the sustainable use of ocean and coastal resources for economic growth and environmental sustainability, has increasingly gained global recognition as a strategic pathway for economic development in coastal regions. Lagos State, Nigeria, with its extensive coastline and maritime resources, possesses significant potential for the development of blue economy sectors such as fisheries, maritime transport, and coastal tourism. title: Making the Mediterranean region since the late nineteenth century: From aridity indices to synoptic oscillations and the ‘return of the sea’
abstract: This article reconstructs how climatic sciences contributed to making the Mediterranean region through successive systems of classification, climatic indices, and synoptic circulation metrics. It does not seek to establish a new definitive Mediterranean boundary. Instead, it examines how particular variables, operations, thresholds, temporal scales, observational infrastructures, and institutional uses produced different climatic Mediterraneans. title: Zinc-Nanoparticles Synthesis Mediated by Hexalobus Crispiflorus Bark Extract for Corrosion Inhibition on Mild Steel in Seawater
abstract: Corrosion control has seen a shift from the traditional corrosion control methods to a more plant mediated green approach. The application of plant mediated nanoparticle for corrosion inhibition has received much research interest in recent times. The aim of this study was the green synthesis of zinc nanoparticles mediated by Hexalobus Crispiflorus bark extracts and zinc nitrate hexahydrate as the precursor for corrosion inhibition on mild steel in seawater. abstract: The Sheinwoodian represents a critical interval in the early colonisation of terrestrial environments by vascular plants and associated cryptogamic assemblages. A multidisciplinary re-examination of one of Barrande's original localities, the Sedlec, Stydlé Vody Section, integrating petrography, clay mineralogy, stable-isotope and trace-element geochemistry, and macro- and microfossil data is presented herein. title: Projected Habitat Expansion of the Invasive Striped Eel Catfish Plotosus lineatus in the Mediterranean Sea Under Future Climate Conditions
abstract: The striped eel catfish Plotosus lineatus is a venomous Indo-Pacific species that has rapidly expanded within the Mediterranean Sea following its Lessepsian migration through the Suez Canal. Understanding its current distribution and future invasion potential is essential for evaluating ecological risks under ongoing climate change. In this study, ensemble species distribution models were applied to predict the present and future habitat suitability of P. lineatus across the Mediterranean Sea under the CMIP6 SSP2-4.5 climate scenario. abstract: Abstract Frequent pluvial hydrometeorological disasters in Southeast Asia (SEA) threaten lives and property, yet the region lacks a unified disaster data set for risk management and research. This study develops a provincial‐level data set integrating multi‐source hazard reports with precipitation data and identifies empirical rainfall reference values associated with reported disaster occurrences to inform early‐warning applications. abstract: Aphid samples were collected from bean and brinjal plants in the coastal region (Patuakhali, Barguna, Barishal, Pirojpur, Gopalgonj and Satkhira) of Bangladesh. abstract: Abstract The East Asian brackish-marine taxon Bicornucythere bisanensis (Okubo, 1975) is reported live from the Tagus River, Portugal, apparently transported live in ships’ ballast water, and believed not to occur between Asia and Europe. abstract: In the 17th century the most common transport vessel in the Swedish navy were lodjas. Yet, it has remained a mystery what these vessels looked like. abstract: Environmental DNA (eDNA) is genetic material released by organisms into water, soil, air, and sediment. abstract: Abstract The sawfishes (Pristidae) are a group of large-bodied, shark-like rays that are among the most threatened marine fishes, having experienced substantial population declines over the past century, primarily due to overfishing and habitat loss. title: More often, less each: Averaging can hide opposing trends in prey occurrence and consumer stomach content
abstract: Averages of prey mass in fish stomachs are widely used to track changes in feeding. Yet, a mean over all stomachs is the exact product of two quantities-the frequency of occurrence of a prey and its mean content in the stomachs that contained it-which can move in opposite directions. In Atlantic cod (Gadus morhua L.) in the Baltic Sea, a stable mean benthos content concealed a falling content of consumers and a rising frequency of occurrence, opposing trends that can signal density dependence or responses to hypoxia.

When ignited, peat releases large quantities of greenhouse gases and other species with significant environmental impacts, including hydrogen cyanide (HCN), a sensitive tracer of smouldering combustion. title: Mitochondrial phylogeography and insecticide resistance of Aedes aegypti in Kenya
abstract: Aedes aegypti is the primary vector of arboviruses such as dengue, yellow fever, Zika, and chikungunya. Here, we investigate the mitochondrial DNA (mtDNA) structure and insecticide resistance of Ae. aegypti populations across Kenya. Using 175 newly sequenced Kenyan COI mtDNA fragments, along with global reference sequences, we assess maternal ancestry and phylogeographic structure. Genetic structure across Kenya was not well explained by isolation-by-distance alone, with several populations deviating from this pattern. institutions: International Centre of Insect Physiology and Ecology

title: Cellulose-based adsorbents for sustainable recovery of critical raw materials (CRMs) from aquatic systems
abstract: The sustainable provision of critical raw materials (CRMs) is increasingly constrained by growing demand, supply-chain risks, and the adverse environmental effects of primary extraction. This review evaluates cellulose-based sorbents as renewable and tunable platforms for CRM recovery from aquatic systems, including mining leachates, industrial effluents, desalination brines, seawater, and synthetic aqueous solutions. title: Comprehensive checklist of the flowering plants of the Agasthyamalai Biosphere Reserve, South India
abstract: The Agasthyamala Biosphere Reserve (ABR), situated at the southern extremity of the Western Ghats, represents one of the most important centres of tropical biodiversity and endemism in peninsular India. Despite more than a century of botanical exploration, information on its angiosperm diversity remains scattered across numerous floras, checklists, unpublished reports and continuously changing taxonomic databases, leading to inconsistencies in nomenclature and distributional records. The present study addresses this gap by providing a critically compiled and taxonomically updated checklist of
institutions: Jawaharlal Nehru Tropical Botanic Garden and Research Institute

title: Costumbres, instituciones, creencias de los indígenas de Argelia. Noviciado de Santa María, 1910
abstract: In this annex, we present the Spanish translation of the text of an anonymous fifty-six-page booklet written in French, containing seventy-five topics on customs, institutions, and beliefs in Algiers in 1910, from the general archives of the General House of the Society of Missionaries of Africa, «White Fathers». The most important topics covered are birth and childhood, education, marriage, makeup, tattooing and body care, clothing, greetings, and courtesy formulas. We accompany the translation with an introduction and explanatory notes.

title: Application of sous-vide technology in aquatic products: a review
abstract: Sous-vide (SV) cooking—a technique combining vacuum packaging with precise low-temperature heating—has emerged as a promising mild processing method for aquatic products, yet existing studies remain fragmented across species and lack systematic comparisons of processing parameters and quality regulation mechanisms. This review systematically examines SV applications across four major aquatic taxa (fish, crustaceans, mollusks, and echinoderms), comparing optimal processing parameters and inter-category differences. title: COMPARATIVE ANALYSIS OF PREHOSPITAL HEALTH SERVICES FOR REFUGEES IN TÜRKİYE, GERMANY AND GREECE
abstract: Objective: This study critically synthesises a body of research that documents how national policies affect emergency health service delivery to refugees and asylum seekers in Türkiye, Germany and Greece. A socio - ecological framework is used to analyse a range of factors from policies to local service structures to migrant narratives that create the social context for accessing emergency health. title: Micro-fiction: The Song
abstract: Sadie Beaton is a listener, activist and Dalhousie PhD candidate carrying many generations of colonial entanglement in unceded Mi’kmaq territory. Drawing on her own settler histories, her research engages with embodied archival practices, Indigenous politics of water, and collaborative storytelling to trouble the pioneer lies that stifle settler imaginations about what kinds of relations and futures are possible here

title: Decolonised Gendered Subjects at War for Freedom and Self-Determination: Women in Combat in Real-Time and in Digitalised Memory
abstract: Women’s history has long been marginalised in dominant narratives, with archives and institutional memory omitting or minimising women’s contributions. Recognising and documenting women’s roles across warfare, social movements, science, and culture is essential to shaping collective memory and challenging persistent gender bias. The digitalisation of archives and memory practices has democratising potential, expanding accessibility, diversity, and global engagement with women’s histories. Online platforms transcend geographical and institutional barriers, integrating testimonies and artefacts

title: Foraging Habits of the Smallest Asian Black Bear Population in Shikoku Island, Japan
abstract: We investigated the foraging habits of the Asian black bear, probably the smallest bear population in the world, using 122 fecal samples, foraging signs, and stable isotope analysis of bear hair in Shikoku Island (SI). Fecal analysis revealed obvious seasonal changes, with the dominant food items being green vegetation in spring, soft masts in summer, and soft and hard masts in autumn. To clarify the characteristics of fecal content in SI, we compared it with that of bears in other areas of Japan. title: Impacts of Anthropogenic Aerosol‐Forced North Atlantic SST Variability on the Simulated Historical Global Warming
abstract: Abstract Climate models with identical anthropogenic forcings simulate different historical warming, mainly because aerosol forcing is poorly constrained. The role of uncertainty in regional aerosol forcing, however, has not been systematically studied. Using a large ensemble of CMIP6 models, I demonstrate that anthropogenic aerosol‐forced North Atlantic (NA) sea‐surface temperature variability significantly modulates greenhouse gas‐driven global‐mean surface air temperature (GMST) increases in historical simulations, explaining 6.8 (±0.7)% of the ensemble‐mean GMST change. title: Suicide Prevention in the US Military: Assessing the Impact of the Brandon Act
abstract: OBJECTIVE: To evaluate whether the Brandon Act, a 2021 legislation establishing confidential, self-initiated mental health referral pathways for US military service members, was associated with reductions in medically attended suicide attempts among active duty service members (ADSMs). STUDY SETTING AND DESIGN: We employed an interrupted time series design using person-quarter panel data from the Military Health System (MHS) from 2018 to 2024. Segmented regression and event study specifications estimated immediate and trajectory effects of the Brandon Act on suicide attempt rates. DATA SOURCES

title: Environmental Determinants of Abundance and Distribution of Selected Neuropteran Families in Eastern Libya
abstract: This study investigates the environmental determinants influencing the abundance and distribution of selected Neuropteran families in Eastern Libya. Field surveys were conducted over a full annual cycle across agricultural, coastal, and semi-arid habitats within the Cyrenaica region. Insect samples were collected using light traps, sweep nets, and sticky traps. Environmental variables including temperature, relative humidity, vegetation density, and soil type were recorded. title: Blue innovation and ecological transitions: a realist synthesis of mechanisms and knowledge asymmetries
abstract: Purpose This study aims to synthesize how scientific literature defines and operationalizes blue innovation and to explain the context-dependent mechanisms linking blue innovation to ecological transitions and blue economy outcomes. The study also examines how geographical asymmetries in knowledge production limit the external validity of dominant blue economy models, particularly for Latin America, Africa and the South Atlantic. title: In water, no one can hear you scream: a new species of parasitic isopod from the genus Zeuxokoma Grygier, 1993 (Isopoda: Epicaridea, Cryptoniscidae) infesting a snapping-shrimp (Caridea, Alpheidae) from Brazil
abstract: Isopods of the suborder Epicaridea Latreille, 1825 are obligatory parasites of other crustaceans, using them as intermediate and definitive hosts during their life cycles. All species of the family Cryptoniscidae Kossmann, 1880 are endoparasitic or mesoparasitic, and can be found as direct parasites of decapods or as hyperparasites of rhizocephalan barnacles infesting decapod hosts. title: The Role Geomorphic Origin and Agricultural Legacy on Plant Communities and Surface Soil Organic Matter in Salt Marshes
abstract: Abstract Saltmarsh habitats provide numerous ecosystem services, including carbon storage, but are eroding at increasingly rapid rates due to ongoing sea level rise. Yet, where space and topography permit, saltmarshes are transgressing into adjacent uplands and counterbalancing the lost area. In these areas, older portions of marshes have accumulated more soil organic matter (SOM) over time than more recently formed marshes, though processes driving this pattern can be complex. Sediment deposition dynamics and plant community can influence SOM with both playing important but interacting roles.

abstract: Assessment and digitization of biological collections are critical for maximizing their value as biodiversity repositories and sources of biological public information. By integrating traditional specimen data with their extended digital information, including genetic and genomic data, biological collections can consolidate as dynamic, publicly accessible infrastructures for research. title: Turnover-driven β-diversity reveals conservation priorities in Antarctic intertidal benthic communities
abstract: Abstract Antarctic sedimentary intertidal habitats remain among the most understudied and least represented within protected areas designated under the Antarctic Treaty System. Understanding how biodiversity varies across space and time within these habitats is therefore essential for effective conservation planning. title: Enhanced fish detection sensitivity in aquatic systems using environmental RNA
abstract: Abstract Environmental RNA (eRNA) can potentially augment the biological monitoring ability of the established environmental DNA (eDNA) application in conservation. Despite faster degradation, environmental RNA could offer unique advantages: it may help reduce the legacy signal compared to eDNA, provide insights into physiological status through gene transcription and offer higher detection sensitivity due to the inherent amplification of certain genes in response to physiology and the environmental context. title: Conservation Science and the Knowledge Shortfalls
abstract: There is much data publicly available on the biodiversity of the world. It would appear then that conserving biodiversity is just a matter of using the data. In this contribution I argue that conservation requires not only data availability, but also conversations about purpose, and present examples of how just being able to use large biodiversity databases is seldom enough to achieve successful conservation.

title: The Image of the Danube in Romanian Poetry
abstract: This article surveys the evolving renditions of the Danube in Romanian poetry from the nineteenth century to the present, situating them within broader cultural, historical, and ecological frameworks. Inspired by a personal rediscovery of the river and informed by Bruno Latour’s concept of the “parliament of things,” the study approaches the Danube as a voice-bearing agent, whose meanings emerge from the interaction between natural processes and human histories. title: Comparative effects of herbal supplementation in increasing growth and immunity of Clarias gariepinus (Burchell, 1822)
abstract: Fish farming is the main activity that provides food based on protein. In addition to fish having excellent nutrition for the body, fish farming can reduce fish catches from nature and at the same time maintain its population. However, in fish farming, it is sometimes constrained by water quality and diseases that can reduce quality and productivity in cultivation. To overcome this, herbs that are immunostimulants, attractants, and growth promoters can be given to increase immunity and growth. title: The Proclamation of the Kazakh Autonomous Soviet Socialist Republic snd The Election of its Governing Bodies
abstract: The article explores the 1920 proclamation of the Kyrgyz (Kazakh) Autonomous Soviet Socialist Republic (KASSR) within the Russian Soviet Federative Socialist Republic (RSFSR) and the establishment of its governing bodies. It investigates the political and socio-economic factors behind autonomy, the roles of party structures, and the first elections of executive and legislative authorities. title: Temporality, emotion management and emergency governance in housing safety crises
abstract: This article uses archival methods to explore housing disasters and the governance of emergencies, using two cases – the Ronan Point collapse and the Ledbury Estate post-Grenfell Tower Fire – to locate a contemporary housing safety emergency within longer histories of high-rise unsafety. title: Temporal variability of extreme precipitation in Cotonou: stable climate signal and worsening urban flood impacts
abstract: Urban flooding has worsened significantly in Cotonou (major flood events in 2010, 2018, and 2020), yet this deterioration occurs against a backdrop of largely stable extreme precipitation. This study analyses the temporal variability of extreme precipitation indices in Cotonou over 40 years (1984–2024) in order to explain this paradox. Based on daily rainfall data from the Cotonou synoptic station, eleven standardised ETCCDI climate indices were calculated at four temporal scales (annual, monthly, seasonal, and decadal). title: A non-Vestan, eucrite-like pyroxene grain from asteroid (101955) Bennu
abstract: Exogenous fragments in brecciated planetary materials offer direct evidence of mixing among planetary bodies in the Solar System. Fragments of undifferentiated carbonaceous material are frequently identified in differentiated meteorites. However, differentiated fragments are rarely observed in carbonaceous material. An exception is the exogenous basalt observed by the OSIRIS-REx spacecraft on the carbonaceous asteroid (101955) Bennu, which motivated a search for differentiated material in the returned samples. title: From Book Shelves to Digital Screens: A Sociological Analysis of the Dying Reading Culture and Library Usage Among Nigerian Students
abstract: The widespread growth of digital technologies has reshaped how young people seek information and engage with reading. In Nigeria, academic libraries that were once key hubs of learning are witnessing reduced patronage as students increasingly turn to digital media. This study examines the sociological dimensions of declining reading culture and library usage among Nigerian students and assesses the relationship between digital media use and reading culture. title: Representations of Postcolonial Massacres and Trauma in Chinua Achebe’s There Was a Country: A Personal History of Biafra
abstract: This paper examines how Chinua Achebe represents war and trauma in There Was a Country: A Personal History of Biafra through an integrated psychoanalytic and postmodern framework. Drawing on Sigmund Freud’s concepts of repression, the unconscious, melancholia, and repetition-compulsion, together with postmodern narrative techniques developed by Linda Hutcheon (1988), Jean-François Lyotard (1984), Cathy Caruth (1996), and Dominick LaCapra (2001), the study explores the literary representation of starvation, betrayal, genocide, and displacement as interconnected forms of postcolonial trauma. title: Factors that cause flatfoot in school children
abstract: Background: Flatfoot is a common disorder in children, although it often does not show serious symptoms. Over time, it will affect the development and growth of the arch of the foot. This study aimed to determine the factors that cause flatfoot in school children. Methods: This study used the literature review method by utilizing databases containing research articles related to factors that could cause flatfoot in elementary school children. title: From stench to hygiene? Public toilets as liminal spaces in late Ottoman İstanbul
abstract: Abstract This article examines public toilets in late Ottoman İstanbul as liminal spaces where urban governance, public health, and everyday life intersected. It argues that these sites functioned as arenas through which modern notions of hygiene, order, and civilization were articulated and contested. abstract: Summary Purple dye was an iconic status symbol in the ancient Mediterranean, yet tracing the expansion and shift of production from the Aegean to the Levant encounters substantial methodological difficulties. Using Tel Shiqmona – a unique industrial centre with a continuous Iron Age sequence – as an archaeological benchmark, this study defines detailed and granular criteria for identifying production. abstract: Photography has an important role as a visual communication medium that can preserve historical information and represent cultural identity. However, the use of photography as an instrument for interpreting the traces of Islamic civilization in the Nusantara region has not been widely studied from the perspective of visual communication. This study aims to analyze the role of documentary photography in representing the traces of Islamic civilization and the process of cultural assimilation between Islam and local Nusantara culture. title: Museo de Arte y Diseño Contemporáneo: orígenes, desarrollo institucional y contexto de un museo en movimiento
abstract: Introduction: Founded in 1994, the Museo de Arte y Diseño Contemporáneo de Costa Rica (MADC) emerged within a Central American context marked by institutional fragility and limited infrastructure for contemporary art. Objective: The paper seeks to analyze the evolution of the MADC in relation to its regional context, Costa Rican cultural policies, and founding process, as well as the conceptual and disciplinary tensions between art and design and its curatorial practices. title: Board governance policies and SDG Transformation 4 performance: evidence from the agricultural products & services industry
abstract: This study investigates how board-level governance policies shape corporate sustainability performance related to SDG Transformation 4, which encompasses sustainable food systems, land-use stewardship, water resource management, and ocean protection. Using a cross-country dataset of 620 firm-year observations in the Agricultural Products & Services industry (2019–2023), the analysis integrates governance policy scores from LSEG SDG Analytics with corporate sustainability disclosures. abstract: Abstract This research investigates the intersection of governance, education, and socio-conditions in shaping revolutionary resistance in East Bengal between 1906 and 1917. The colonial rule aimed at centralizing power at Calcutta, and East Bengal was a peripheral province marked by historical marginalization. abstract: The mesa-like volcanic Kerekbükk hill in the Eastern Cserhát Mountains (N Hungary) hosts numerous small lakes linked to postglacial landslides. Double Lake (Kettős-tó), near the mesa summit, occurs in a geomorphologically atypical position and has therefore been debated as potentially artificial, with uncertain hydrological behavior and function. title: From the Ottoman Palace to the Last Resting Place in Bosnia: Silahdar Mustafa Pasha’s Tomb and Career Path
abstract: This article revisits the historical details of Silahdar (Perişan) Mustafa Pasha's tomb (died 1799) in Travnik, central Bosnia, and re-examines previously published information about his career. Mustafa Pasha held roles as governor and district governor in several Ottoman provinces (eyalets) and districts (sancaks). abstract: Bacterial resistance remains a critical global health challenge, driving the continuous search for novel antimicrobial agents. Bacillus amyloliquefaciens is a recognized repository of bioactive metabolites; however, its full biosynthetic potential requires integrated genomic and experimental validation. This study characterized the antimicrobial profile of B. amyloliquefaciens BS4 through a hybrid pipeline. abstract: Information and Communication Technology (ICT) have been recognized as an effective tool that could assist government and its institutions reinvent itself faster, run cheaply, better and produce newer outcomes. The usage of technology has permeated almost all endeavours of life such as banking, education, marine sector, health, environment, transportation etc. by providing ways of ensuring efficient, easy processing and delivery of services. abstract: Vascular interventional procedures are minimally invasive but remain highly dependent on operator expertise and are associated with occupational radiation exposure and technically demanding catheter and guidewire manipulation. By integrating precision motion control, force sensing, haptic feedback, image-guided navigation, and teleoperation, robot-assisted vascular interventional surgery (RVIS) has emerged as an interdisciplinary field spanning robotics, biomedical engineering, and interventional medicine. abstract: The participation of diverse stakeholders is considered essential in building flood resilience. However, empirical studies remain insufficient to clarify the roles and interactions within multi-actor networks and their implications for resilience, especially in the historical contexts. title: Projected intensification of precipitation characteristics and meteorological drought and wetness conditions in Accra Ghana
abstract: Meteorological droughts, wet conditions, and extreme precipitation events pose increasing risks to rapidly urbanizing coastal cities such as Accra, Ghana, where flooding, drought, and water-resource stress remain major planning challenges. This study assessed historical and future precipitation characteristics in Accra using the Korea Meteorological Administration Advanced Community Earth System (KACE) model under the SSP1-2.6 and SSP5-8.5 climate scenarios. title: Biochar and Biochar-Compost Effects on Soil Quality and Maize (Zea mays L.) Performance in Mubi, Northern Guinea Savannah of Nigeria
abstract: An experiment was conducted at the research farm of the Federal Polytechnic, Mubi, in 2025 cropping season to analyzed the effect of biochar, and biochar-compost on maize performance and soil quality in Mubi. Mubi lies between latitude 10’8’ N and N10’30`N of the equator and longitude 13’10’E and 13’25`E at an altitude of 696 m above sea level located in the Northern Guinea Savanna zone of Nigeria with mean annual rainfall of 1000 mm with peak from July to September. title: The dynamics and ambiguities of ‘Chineseness’: Interethnic marriage practices in the Dutch Batavia before 1850
abstract: Abstract This article explores how interethnic marriage produces and governs ambiguous identities within legally pluralist port-city settings. Taking the construction of ‘Chineseness’ in the Dutch Batavia before 1850 as a case study, this article analyses how identity was contested, negotiated, and reconfigured in a colonial legal landscape. title: Scientific Research into Visual Culture and Fine Arts of Independent Ukraine: Main Directions, Issues and Development Trends
abstract: Research on visual culture and fine arts of independent Ukraine has formed an interdisciplinary scientific field, encompassing art history, cultural studies, memory studies, media studies, and sociology of art. The aim of the article is to reconstruct the structure of scientific research on visual culture and fine arts of independent Ukraine; the object of the study is a corpus of publications dedicated to the Ukrainian artistic process of 1991–2026. abstract: A smart parking management application uses IoT sensors, cloud databases, and a mobile app to help drivers find and reserve open parking spots in real time. abstract: River floodplains contribute to river ecosystems by supporting high biological productivity and biodiversity. abstract: Migration to the United States after 1975 reshaped gender hierarchies and family power within Vietnamese households. abstract: Landslides and debris flows are the most frequent and socioeconomically impactful natural hazards in Colombia and Antioquia. title: Rediscovery of the largetooth sawfish Pristis pristis and a historical record of range extension in South Africa
abstract: All five species of sawfishes (family: Pristidae) are currently Critically Endangered. Of the two, P. pristis was by far the rarer, with only seven confirmed records from five specimens since 1951; the most recent was in 1985. abstract: This study aimed to bibliometrically evaluate medical specialty theses completed in the field of neurosurgery in Türkiye between 2016 and 2025, and to examine temporal changes in thesis numbers, topic distribution, and gender distribution of thesis authors. title: Unveiling the club moss (Lycopodium clavatum L.): Ethnomedicinal uses, phytochemistry and pharmacological insights
abstract: Club moss, scientifically known as Lycopodium clavatum L., is a primitive tracheophyte in the family Lycopodiaceae of the pteridophytes. Lycopodium clavatum thrives on exposed, lightly shaded grassland slopes, forest peripheries and disturbed or human-impacted areas such as road cuts. These traits enable them to have widespread distribution in moist forest margins, temperate, subtropical and polar climates. They are documented in Europe, Asia and America. abstract: Abstract Climate change and population ageing are some of the most pressing challenges of the twenty-first century, whose convergence exacerbates the vulnerability of older adults to floods. Nature-based solutions for flood risk reduction (NbS-FRR) is central to China’s “ecological civilization” vision, offering sustainable adaptation. However, empirical evidence of their ancillary health benefits for older adults remains nascent. abstract: Background: Iron Deficiency Anemia (IDA) is a critical global public health challenge among adolescent girls, driven by increased physiological iron requirements during growth spurts, menstrual blood loss, inadequate dietary intake, as well as lifestyle and environmental factors. Schools serve as a strategic platform for delivering broad and sustainable IDA prevention interventions. abstract: In recent years, the health problems attributable to cigarette smoke (CS) have attracted widespread attention. However, the pathogenic mechanisms underlying osteoporosis development induced by nicotine, a neuroactive component of CS, remain unclear. abstract: BACKGROUND: Atopic dermatitis (AD) is a common chronic inflammatory skin disorder with a continuously increasing global incidence. Current therapeutic options are often associated with adverse effects. In recent years, natural products have attracted considerable attention due to their anti-inflammatory and antioxidant properties, which can effectively alleviate the symptoms of AD. abstract: PURPOSE: Postpartum depression (PPD) is a common maternal mental health disorder, affecting up to one in six mothers, with serious consequences for maternal well-being, child development, and economic costs. Media shape public mental health perceptions, and newspapers remain an important information source. Yet systematic analyses of UK newspaper coverage of PPD are scarce. abstract: The rapid expansion in tilapia farming and potential increase in the use of antibiotics to tackle disease outbreaks or enhance productivity may amplify antimicrobial resistance (AMR) and its adverse implications. Efforts to mitigate AMR risks in the sector through the development of alternative non-antibiotic options are ongoing, but the current research landscape is fragmentary. abstract: Direct predation is a major driver of the negative impact of the invasive round goby Neogobius melanostomus on native macrozoobenthic assemblages. However, the presence of N. melanostomus predators represents a possible means of reducing its negative impact via consumptive and non-consumptive effects (NCEs). abstract: Wutou decoction (WTD) is a traditional remedy in Chinese medicine for rheumatoid arthritis (RA). However, its active ingredients are complex, and how it counteracts RA is still not clear. abstract: ABSTRACT Despite an extensive body of environmental law and policy, China's environmental law has long been dubbed a “paper tiger” owning to persistent enforcement failures. Over the past decade, legislative and judicial reforms have substantially strengthened the criminal enforcement of pollution offenses, raising the question of whether Chinese environmental law has grown fierce teeth to generate sufficient deterrence. abstract: Microplastics (MPs) are persistent contaminants of growing concern due to their widespread occurrence and potential ecological risks in aquatic environment. abstract: Enhanced in situ bioremediation is a widely adopted and sustainable means of remediating chlorinated contaminant impacted groundwater utilizing organohalide respiring bacteria. These bacteria utilize chlorinated compounds as terminal electron acceptors to harvest energy, producing partially or fully dechlorinated end products. abstract: Atlantic brant Branta bernicla hrota increasingly use turfgrass fields, such as baseball fields and golf courses, throughout their wintering range. abstract: Global climate change has been linked to faunal turnover throughout geological history, but the effects of regional environmental change remain comparatively less understood. Central Asian environments changed repeatedly throughout the Paleogene (ca. 66 to 23 Ma) due to topographic reshaping and global climate change. abstract: Malathion is one of the most widely used organophosphate insecticides, and its environmental fate is strongly influenced by microbial transformation in the water column and sediments. This review synthesizes current knowledge of the enzymatic and metabolic pathways that govern the persistence of malathion in aquatic, sedimentary, and wastewater systems. abstract: Recent environmental news from 2024–2026 shows that the Kocasu River Basin is experiencing ecosystem collapse, mass fish deaths, industrial contamination, and tourism decline, like global delta degradation trends. abstract: Understanding the spatiotemporal variability of water salinity in estuarine systems is essential for evaluating hydrodynamic and ecological processes. abstract: A major barrier to scaling marine restoration and aquaculture is the lack of reliable tools to induce invertebrate larvae to settle and metamorphose when and where needed. Although microbial cues are known to induce metamorphosis in many invertebrates, existing methods rely on natural biofilms that are variable, difficult to standardize, and unsuitable for large-scale deployment. abstract: Noise from human activities has increased and been shown to negatively impact marine animals. Marine mammals and fish are vulnerable to anthropogenic noise because they rely on sound to communicate, find food, avoid predators and sense their environment. Forage fish are small schooling pelagic fish, important to many predators and instrumental in moving energy to higher trophic levels. abstract: The Ecosystem Approach to Fisheries (EAF) was adopted by the Food and Agriculture Organization of the United Nations (FAO) as a practical framework for fisheries management according to the Code of Conduct for Responsible Fisheries. abstract: The present review provides a concise overview of cyclic peptides as chemical probes, including recent developments in their discovery and applications. abstract: Abstract Seagrasses support highly productive ecosystems in both temperate and tropical waters and provide essential ecosystem services. abstract: Abstract Maritime security in the Western Indian Ocean (WIO) has become a shared concern for the European Union (EU) and India, yet sustained co-presence and overlapping security challenges have not translated into deeper institutional convergence. title: Dynamic response and loads analysis of a large offshore wind turbine under low-frequency wind fluctuations
abstract: Abstract. We investigate the impact of low-frequency wind fluctuations on the loads and response of a large reference offshore wind turbine. Synthetic wind fields containing low-frequency fluctuations down to 1 hr-1 are used in aeroelastic simulations with the HAWC2 code. The dynamic response and damage equivalent loads (DEL) for tower and blade moments are evaluated. title: Automated workflow demonstrates mixed treatment impacts on burn severity across ecoregion scales
abstract: Background Intensifying wildfire activity in western North America has motivated focus on fuel treatments as a tool for moderating fire severity. Treatment effectiveness is influenced by complex interactions among biophysical settings, treatments and weather. Aims This study introduces a standardized, scalable workflow to quantify wildfire-treatment outcomes across diverse landscapes. Methods We evaluated federal fuel treatments across 50 wildfires in southern Oregon and Northern California (2012–2021). title: Representation of the rights of nature and the Mar Menor law
abstract: In 2022, the Spanish Mar Menor, a coastal saltwater lagoon in the Iberian Peninsula, became the first natural entity in Europe to be granted legal personhood. This article examines the Mar Menor law and its institutions in the context of the debate on the rights of nature. Bringing together research on rights of nature and political representation, it explores the potential of the Mar Menor law and its institutions to bridge the gap in the human-nature relationship and address challenges arising from the political representation of nature. title: Potential distribution study of Caragana microphylla in China based on MaxEnt modeling
abstract: Climate, soil factors, and topography play a decisive role in the spatial distribution of species. Predicting the potential distribution of Caragana microphylla Lam. over time is of great significance for maintaining ecological balance, soil and water conservation, and evaluating ecological services in northwestern China. In this study, we used the Global Biodiversity Information Service (GBIF) and SDM Toolbox v2.5 to remove spatial autocorrelation from 103 occurrence records of C. microphylla . title: Bayesian estimation of clustering structures in binned data
abstract: Binned data, a common type of data sets resulting from summarizing the original observations in a sequence of pairs of bins and frequencies, appear in different fields of research. There may exist different reasons to only provide this summary; however, the more important challenge is being able to perform statistical analyses based only on it. We present a Bayesian nonparametric model for clustering applicable to binned data. Clusters are modeled via random partitions, and within them a model-based approach is assumed. title: Molecular basis of N2 fixation in a hyperthermophilic archaeon
abstract: Abstract Exploring the natural diversity of phylogenetically distant nitrogenases is crucial for gaining new insights into the mechanism of atmospheric N 2 fixation and unlocking biotechnological developments in sustainable ammonia production. Here, we investigated the N 2 -fixing system of Methanocaldococcus infernus , a deep-sea hyperthermophilic archaeon growing diazotrophically at 92 °C. This natively isolated nitrogenase has a melting temperature close to the water boiling point, with an extrapolated specific activity superior to mesophilic homologues. title: Hyperabundance of a subordinate herbivorous gastropod causes localised overgrazing within kelp beds
abstract: Herbivory is a fundamental biological process that can determine the structure and functioning of ecosystems. On temperate reefs worldwide, herbivory by grazing macro-invertebrates can cause extensive overgrazing of kelp beds when grazers reach hyperabundance. Rising to local dominance, typically it is the grazing activity of a single species amongst others that is responsible for overgrazed 'barrens'. title: Rapid spontaneous generation of organosulfur from inorganic sulfur in atmospheric microdroplets
abstract: Abstract Organosulfur compounds are important constituents of atmospheric aerosols and have been extensively investigated through field observations, laboratory experiments, and atmospheric modeling. However, the mechanisms underlying their formation and atmospheric abundance remain incompletely understood. Ubiquitous in the atmosphere, micrometer-sized droplets provide unique interfacial reaction environments that may facilitate organosulfur formation. title: Power enhancement of a tuned inerter-equipped point-absorber wave energy converter using deep reinforcement learning
abstract: This study investigates deep reinforcement learning (DRL) control of a point-absorber wave energy converter (WEC) equipped with a tuned inerter (TI) mechanism. The inerter generates an inertial force proportional to the relative acceleration between its terminals, enabling a large effective mass effect, referred to as inertance, with a relatively small physical mass. title: Multirobot Aerial Soft Manipulator for Floating Litter Collection
abstract: Removing floating litter from water bodies is crucial to preserving aquatic ecosystems and preventing pollution. In this work, we present a multirobot aerial manipulator for floating litter collection, leveraging the capabilities of aerial robots. The system is composed of two aerial robots connected by a rope, which supports a hook‐based tool for collecting floating litter. Compared to single‐aerial‐robot solutions, the use of two aerial robots increases payload capacity and flight endurance while reducing the downwash effect at the manipulation point, located at the midpoint of the rope. title: Modelling the impacts of imports and non-native subspecies hybridisation in honeybees
abstract: Human-mediated movement of organisms for agriculture and ecosystem services often results in hybridisation and introgression between populations of native and non-native species. While introgression may increase genetic diversity, it can erode unique adaptations and reduce fitness, threatening the survival of native lineages. Honeybees offer a good model with extensive records, queen trade and migratory beekeeping facilitating genetic exchange among subspecies. title: River and slope molluscan thanatocoenoses in the Mnikowska valley near Kraków (southern Poland): diversity, deposition, and transport
abstract: Accumulations of empty mollusc shells (thanatocoenoses) found in the Mnikowska Valley near Kraków were analysed. The study was based on samples collected from thanatocoenoses accumulating in the Sanka stream bed (river thanatocoenoses – 10 samples) and at the foot of slopes formed by limestone rocks (slope thanatocoenoses – 11 samples). The abundant material identified 66 mollusc species, represented by over 7,000 shells. title: Techno-economic feasibility of riverine hydrokinetic systems under hydrological and financial uncertainty — case study on the Davao River, Philippines
abstract: Transitioning toward sustainable power generation requires robust models for emerging technologies like riverine hydrokinetic energy, which are often hindered by technical and financial uncertainties. This study presents a site-specific techno-economic analysis (TEA) of a conceptual hydrokinetic system for the Davao River, Philippines, utilizing a probabilistic Levelized Cost of Electricity (LCOE) framework. title: Plant‐derived eDNA metabarcoding is an effective approach for monitoring invertebrate rice pests
abstract: Abstract Traditional methods based on morphological taxonomy and visual identification of crop damage are increasingly challenged by the diversity and complexity of current and emerging pest occurrences. Although environmental DNA (eDNA) metabarcoding shows potential for improving agricultural pest management, comprehensive evaluation of its effectiveness in pest identification and monitoring remains scarce, particularly studies integrating controlled laboratory experiments with field monitoring. title: Diversity of endohelminth parasites of fish from Sali-Dulce River tributary (Tucumán province, Northwestern Argentina)
abstract: PURPOSE: Medina-Salas River is a tributary of Sali-Dulce endorheic system, one of the most important basins of Northwester Argentina. Despite, many endemic fish species can be found in this endorheic system, and its ichthyological diversity is affected by anthropogenic activities, the diversity of endohelminth parasite of fish in this river remains unexplored. This study aimed to analyse the structure and composition of endohelminth communities of fish species from lower sector Medina-Salas River. title: Effects of temperature and pH on polyunsaturated fatty acid production by Aurantiochytrium sp. L3W when cultivated on unsterile pomace
abstract: Abstract Aurantiochytrium sp. strain L3W produces polyunsaturated fatty acids, particularly docosahexaenoic acid (DHA). This study investigated the feasibility of unsterile cultivation of strain L3W using pomace from tomato, lemon, and yellow carrot as substrates at different temperatures (25 °C, 30 °C, and 35 °C) and pH (4 and 7). Toward this end, the effects of temperature and pH on the growth of L3W, DHA production, and co-existing bacterial dynamics were examined. abstract: Penelitian ini dilatarbelakangi oleh masih ditemukannya unsafe acts, ketidakkonsistenan kepatuhan terhadap prosedur keselamatan, serta kecenderungan implementasi International Safety Management (ISM) Code yang masih berorientasi pada paper compliance di lingkungan PT Pertamina International Shipping (PIS). abstract: Description of a new species of Myxobolus parasitizing the freshwater fish Rhamdia quelen, in the municipality of Cachoeira do Arari, Marajó Island, Pará, Brazil. Thirty specimens were analyzed, with 60% exhibiting rounded or ovoid, whitish plasmodia containing mature myxospores, scattered across the palate and the lower lip of the hosts. title: Unravelling the impact of nitrogen deprivation on the morphology and nanomechanical properties of Parachlorella kessleri
abstract: Abstract Nitrogen deprivation is commonly applied to enhance lipid accumulation in microalgae for third-generation biofuel production. However, its influence on cell wall morphology and nanomechanical properties, which critically affect downstream processing, remains poorly explored. To address this gap, this study investigated the impact of nitrogen deprivation on these properties of the freshwater microalga Parachlorella kessleri using a multi-microscopy approach. abstract: Abstract Circularly polarized luminescence (CPL) imaging of biomolecules using designed chiral probes holds significant promise for biochemical and analytical applications. In this work, we report two chiral hetero[9]helicene multi-resonant thermally activated delayed fluorescent (MR-TADF) organic molecules DDCzBPh and DDCzBPy , consisting of two annulated MR-TADF units to a central naphthyl or quinoxanyl group, respectively, which exhibit simultaneously strong CPL, two-photon absorption, high photoluminescence quantum yields, and long-lived delayed fluorescence. title: First record and redescription of Gerista dimidiata Bolívar, 1905 (Orthoptera, Acrididae, Oxyinae) from Cameroon
abstract: Gerista dimidiata Bolívar, 1905 is the only species in its monotypical Afrotropical genus. It occurs at swampy-forest edges, where it is typically found on broad-leaved forest grasses. Prior to this study, G. dimidiata was only recorded from Nigeria and Bioko Island in Equatorial Guinea. Here, we report the first occurrence of G. dimidiata for Cameroon, specifically from the Littoral Region in Yansoki and Missole I, significantly expanding the known distribution range of the species. title: Multilocus DNA Barcoding Resolves Area-Based Genetic Variation in Freshwater Shrimps (Macrobrachium sp. and Caridina sp.) from Saline and Non-Saline Habitats in Northeastern Thailand
abstract: Freshwater prawns are important components of freshwater ecosystems, yet their diversity and genetic structure in northeastern Thailand remain insufficiently documented, particularly across habitats differing in soil salinity. This study assessed freshwater prawn diversity and phylogenetic relationships in saline and non-saline habitats using an integrative taxonomic approach combining morphological examination with mitochondrial and nuclear DNA barcoding. title: Fourier-Hermite Kinetic Network for Gas Transport Under High Knudsen Numbers
abstract: This work presents the Fourier-Hermite Kinetic Network (FHKN), a novel sequence-to-state temporal-spectral architecture designed to accelerate the prediction of rarefied gas transport in porous media. Traditional lattice Boltzmann method (LBM) simulations in complex geometries require massive computational overhead due to slow transient relaxation. title: Unlocking the Potential for Microplastic Degradation: In Silico Mutagenesis and Molecular Dynamics Simulations of PET-PETase and MHET-MHETase Interactions by Reverse Screening
abstract: Plastic pollution remains a growing global concern, requiring efficient and sustainable solutions. Enzymes such as PETase and MHETase from Ideonella sakaiensis offer natural mechanisms for plastic degradation but need further enhancement for large-scale applications. This study aimed to improve the structural stability and substrate-binding performance of PETase and MHETase by engineering their homologous variants through in silico methods. title: Correlación morfométrica y reproductiva en la machaca Brycon costaricensis (Characiformes: Bryconidae) en la Vertiente Norte de Costa Rica
abstract: Introducción: La machaca (Brycon costaricensis), es una de las principales especies objetivo en la pesca recreativa de agua dulce en Costa Rica, particularmente a lo largo de la vertiente Caribe. title: Microbial community coalescence restructures co-occurrence architecture and generates regime-specific patterns of network complexity and stability
abstract: Abstract Microbial community coalescence (MCC), the mixing of distinct microbiomes, is increasingly recognized as an important process in natural and managed microbial systems. However, how MCC reorganizes species association architecture and whether this restructuring alters community stability remain poorly understood. Here, we investigated how MCC modifies microbial co-occurrence networks and whether resulting architectures deviate from expectations based on stochastic reshuffling or direct compositional mixing of donor communities. title: Canadian wildfire impacts and global societal costs attributed to climate change over the 21st century
abstract: Abstract Wildfires in Canada are intensifying due to anthropogenic climate change, with far-reaching impacts on ecosystems, human well-being, and the global climate system. However, the long-term societal costs of future wildfires and the extent to which they will be shaped by climate change remain poorly quantified. Here, we project Canadian wildfire impacts over the 21st century and attribute projected changes in burned area, exposure, costs, and CO2 emissions to anthropogenic climate change under three Shared Socioeconomic Pathways (SSP1-2.6, SSP3-7.0, and SSP5-8.5). title: Evaluating Ustulina deusta as a proxy for the impact of Neolithic woodland management at the mid-Holocene Elm Decline in Britain
abstract: The mid-Holocene decline in elm ( Ulmus ) pollen frequencies is perhaps the most debated and researched pollen-analytical feature of vegetation history in northwest Europe, with various causes or combination of causes proposed to explain it. It has a significant radiocarbon age range in Britain, but its timing in the early stages of Neolithic settlement suggests that subsistence farming activities probably played a role as well as factors such as disease and climate change. abstract: ABSTRACT Efficient solar‐driven interfacial evaporation requires precise coordination of heat and mass transport, yet achieving such synergy within conventional molecular systems remains challenging. title: Applied antibacterial and surface decontamination potential of methyl salicylate-rich Gaultheria fragrantissima essential oil
abstract: AIMS: The persistence of biofilm-forming nosocomial pathogens on healthcare-associated surfaces represents a major challenge in infection control. This study aimed to evaluate the antibacterial, antibiofilm, membrane-disruptive, and surface decontamination potential of methyl salicylate-rich Gaultheria fragrantissima essential oil (GFEO) against clinically relevant pathogens. title: Modelling compressive loading in large‐bodied mammals reveals distinct biomechanical strategies in proboscidean humeri
abstract: Proboscideans exhibit limb morphologies specialised for supporting extreme body masses under predominantly compressive loading. These graviportal adaptations include repositioning of the limb bones closer to the trunk, resulting in a columnar stance. Among proboscideans, two humeral morphotypes have been proposed (slender and robust), yet their functional significance under compressive loading remains poorly understood. title: The distribution of fitness effects of nonsynonymous mutations varies phylogenetically across animals
abstract: The distribution of fitness effects (DFE) describes the selection coefficients of newly arising mutations and fundamentally influences population genetic processes. However, the extent and mechanisms of differences in the DFE for non-synonymous mutations have not been systematically investigated across species with divergent phylogenetic histories and ecologies. Here, we inferred the DFE in natural populations of 11 animal (sub)species, including humans, mice, fin whales, vaquitas, wolves, collared flycatchers, pied flycatchers, halictid bees, Drosophila, and mosquitoes. title: Structural Dynamics and Optical Spectra of the Phycobiliprotein PC612 Complex
abstract: Abstract Phycocyanin 612 (PC612) is a light-harvesting complex found in cryptophyte algae, characterized by its distinct open structure and flexible protein conformation, allowing the algae to survive in low-light aqueous environments. Although cryptophyte algae are known to show a diverse range of spectroscopic properties, the complex electronic structures and photophysical properties of their pigment molecules, known as bilins, are not yet fully understood, particularly in terms of how the surrounding protein environment influences them. title: Self-interference suppression in MIMO power line communication based on spatial linear projection filter
abstract: In modern communication technology applications, electromagnetic coupling inevitably occurs among multiple channels in multiple-input multiple-output (MIMO) power line communication (PLC) systems, which gives rise to signal crosstalk between channels and introduces additional detrimental effects on communication stability and effectiveness. This paper proposes a self-interference suppression method for MIMO-PLC. title: A low-cost surface ablation monitoring system using wind-induced motion of mass-balance stakes
abstract: Surface ablation measurements are critical for understanding glacier mass change over time. Mass-balance stakes are commonly used for localized measurements, with the exposed length typically measured manually at infrequent intervals. This paper presents the design and validation of new instrumentation that automates mass-balance stake readings, thus enabling continuous measurements with high temporal resolution. title: DeepLabCut-based automated system reveals diverse temperature tolerance among medaka strains and related Oryzias species
abstract: Temperature is a critical environmental factor influencing the physiology and behavior of ectothermic animals, yet conventional methods for evaluating thermal tolerance in fish rely on subjective manual observation of loss of equilibrium (LOE), limiting experimental throughput and introducing observer bias. Here, we developed an automated temperature tolerance evaluation system integrating DeepLabCut-based pose estimation with custom image processing algorithms to objectively quantify the timing of LOE during thermal stress tests. title: Effects of multi human disturbance on soil organic carbon: mediation by landscape patterns and forest community attributes in forest villages of the Henan section, Yellow River Basin
abstract: Introduction National Forest Villages (NFVs) represent a policy-relevant rural greening initiative with potential contributions to soil organic carbon (SOC) maintenance, yet how multi human disturbances are associated with forest SOC remains poorly understood. Methods We investigated all 99 NFVs in the Henan section of the Yellow River Basin by integrating field surveys, remote sensing data, and statistical approaches. title: Caffeine pollution changes anti-predator behaviour in Gammarus pulex similarly to manipulative parasites
abstract: Caffeine is an emerging environmental contaminant in freshwater ecosystems that is primarily introduced through wastewater. Even at low concentrations, caffeine can affect the physiology and behaviour of aquatic organisms. Still, its ecological significance remains little understood. We examined the impact of environmentally relevant caffeine concentrations on the anti-predator behaviour of the freshwater amphipod Gammarus pulex. title: A new subspecies of Fagus orientalis (Fagaceae) in Turkey: F. orientalis subsp. nurensis, a relict close to the ancestor of modern European and Oriental Beech
abstract: Genetic diversity assessment is a key component of understanding biodiversity and conservation action. In this study, we used High-Throughput Sequencing (HTS) of the nuclear ribosomal 5S RNA gene arrays (5S-HTS), to investigate the small isolates of Oriental beech ( Fagus orientalis Lipsky) thriving at the south-easternmost edge of the genus range in Western Eurasia (Nur Mountains, the southern spur of the Taurus range, South Anatolia). title: Belief and the beast: Religion and attitudes towards tigers in Central India
abstract: Abstract Human perceptions of wildlife are critical to shaping conservation outcomes, particularly in landscapes where people coexist with large carnivores. Religion, a deeply rooted sociocultural force, remains underexplored in the context of human–wildlife conflict. This study examines how faith‐based belief systems influence attitudes and tolerance towards tigers ( Panthera tigris ) in the surrounding area of the Tadoba‐Andhari Tiger Reserve, central India—where tigers are both culturally significant and frequently implicated in life‐threatening conflict. title: Robust optimal operation of AC/DC offshore energy hubs: Addressing wind uncertainty with mixed-integer second-order cone programming
abstract: Offshore energy hubs integrating wind power, battery energy storage systems (BESS), and hydrogen production are key to advancing sustainable energy systems. However, their operation faces distinct challenges due to the time-dependent dynamics of BESS and hydrogen systems and the complexity of the nonlinear models of their subsystems, requiring optimal scheduling over time and considering wind power variability, which introduces uncertainty in setting operational setpoints. title: Photophysical lock-in detection enables background-free upconversion emission imaging
abstract: Lanthanide-based upconversion nanoparticles (UCNPs) have attracted considerable attention in biomedical applications, due to their anti-Stokes shifted emission enabling autofluorescence-free signal detection. However, residual excitation light can still interfere with their relatively weak emission signals. abstract: Abstract C-type asteroid-derived samples, including Ryugu and carbonaceous chondrites, consist primarily of fine-grained matrices of magnesium-rich hydrous silicates formed by aqueous alteration. These matrices are commonly interpreted as mixtures of serpentine- and saponite-like phyllosilicates, although their mineralogical characteristics do not fully correspond to well-crystalline terrestrial layered silicates. abstract: Anti-quorum sensing (QS) therapy has been focused on to reduce the virulence of pathogenic bacteria. However, there is a risk that suppression of the staphylococcal QS Agr system might promote biofilm formation. In this study, we found that both Agr activity and the biofilm of Staphylococcus aureus can be reduced by a sappanwood extract (SWe). title: Height-aware and protection-informed flood assessment shifts global urban risk distribution
abstract: Abstract Floods pose a significant global threat, causing widespread human and economic losses. However, current flood risk assessments frequently rely on simplified assumptions, such as uniform flood depth-damage relationships and country-level protection standards, that neglect crucial factors like building height and the regional variation in flood protection capacity. title: Utahmycin C, a new glycosylated derivative of a rare azaanthraquinone produced by Streptomyces sp. YD248
abstract: Chemical investigation of Streptomyces sp. YD248 led to the isolation of utahmycin C ( 1 ), a new glycosylated member of the rare bacterial 1,3-dimethyl-2-azaanthraquinone family. title: Molecular identification and distribution of Dictyocaulus spp. in wild ungulates in Lithuania
abstract: Abstract This study aimed to investigate the diversity, prevalence and host specificity of Dictyocaulus lungworms in free-ranging wild ungulates in Lithuania using morphological and molecular approaches. A total of 129 individuals representing 4 host species (red deer, roe deer, moose and European bison) were examined. Four Dictyocaulus species were identified: D. cervi, D. skrjabini, D. capreolus and D. viviparus bisontis . Infection parameters varied markedly among host species. title: From active to activist ageing: conceptualising older adults’ activism in India and Finland
abstract: Climate and environmental crises are threatening older adults’ health globally. However, while older adults are vulnerable to the impacts of the climate crisis, they can also be resilient and may, among other things, exercise their influence through activism. In this conceptual article, we first argue that it is important to study older adults’ activism concerning the climate and environmental crisis, then identify possible theoretical perspectives to use in doing so, and lastly highlight some examples of activism in two very different countries, India and Finland. abstract: While highly successful, density functional theory is known to have limitations owing to its neglect of many-body electron-electron interactions. This neglect leads to errors in the single-particle energies, leading to underestimated bandgaps and bandwidths as well as errors in band alignment at interfaces. Many-body perturbation theory, in the form of the GW self-energy correction, has been widely used to improve upon these shortcomings. title: Dispersal costs affect taxonomic and functional beta diversity of riverine fish assemblages
abstract: Abstract The dispersal of fish along river segments is dependent on resistance factors such as channel slope, dam attributes, and the watercourse distance between locations. We examined how such dispersal costs shape the taxonomic and functional beta diversity of fishes in four basins in the Eastern United States of America. We clustered the fish species into functional groups defined using swimming and reproductive traits. title: Control design for floating wind turbines: a novel feedback control structure
abstract: The generator speed feedback control of onshore wind turbines, via the pitch controller to feather the blades, is well established, but employing the same controller gains with floating offshore wind turbines causes the turbines to become unstable. Such instability is attributed to the coupling between the nacelle fore-aft motion and the wind turbine controller, which makes the wind turbine negatively damped. title: Frontiers and Border Controls in Northern Syria after the Roman Conquest of Antioch, ad 969– c. 1070
abstract: Despite a millennium of maintaining boundaries with other polities, the borders erected by the Roman Empire after antiquity remain understudied. This article looks at new borders and frontier zones established in the late tenth century and maintained through most of the eleventh around Antioch (ad 969–1084). In the years after the Roman reconquest of the city boundaries were set in the east with Aleppo, and on the coast and in the Orontes valley with the other new power in the region, the Fāṭimid Caliphate. title: Resilience of ant communities (Hymenoptera: formicidae) to moderate urban disturbance in a mediterranean peri-urban landscape
abstract: Human activities alter the biotic and abiotic characteristics of the environment, affecting species richness, population abundances and community composition. Nevertheless, these activities intensify as we move from forested areas to the center of urban cities, with peri-urban areas presenting intermediate trends. In this study, we investigate the role of anthropogenic disturbance to ant community composition and diversity in the peri-urban forest of Agia Paraskevi (Attica), Greece. Sampling was conducted during a full year (June 2022 - May 2023) using pitfall traps, both in natural areas and
institutions: National and Kapodistrian University of Athens

title: Photo-guided azopolymer hydrogel actuators
abstract: Amorphous azopolymers are fascinating materials that can be deformed in arbitrary directions by light. However, they are so far used mostly for microfabrication, to anisotropically reshape dry polymer structures - essentially as a post-processing fabrication step. This is because the effect is known to be a plastic deformation, wherein the azopolymer is photo-softened and selectively reflows along the direction of the illumination polarization, owing to its polarization-dependent functional dyes. institutions: Norwegian University of Science and Technology

title: Results of Lunar PlanetVacTM, a pneumatic regolith sampling system deployed to the moon on Blue Ghost Mission 1
abstract: PlanetVac TM is a pneumatic sampling technology designed to acquire and transfer regolith from planetary surfaces to instruments for in-situ analysis or storage on sample return missions. PlanetVac TM employs a robust, dust-tolerant pneumatic approach to overcome the challenges associated with robotic sample acquisition and delivery. Its primary advantages include fast operation with no human-in-the-loop requirement, gravity-agnostic operation, and low Size, Weight, and Power. PlanetVac TM offers a low-cost approach to regolith sampling and eliminates the need for a complex robotic arm. Lunar

title: A socio-technical transition of the low-altitude economy: Evidence and governance implications from Chinese cities
abstract: The low-altitude economy (LAE) generally refers to economic activities conducted within airspace below 1,000 meters. Drawing on related theories on socio-technical transitions, LAE can be understood as a future regime challenging the dominant urban mobility paradigm. As an emerging field, it has yet to be systematically examined through empirical study, especially regarding local response. In this paper, we construct an Integrated Local Support Index (ILSI) based on the number of relevant local policies and the level of public interest measured by the Baidu Search Index. title: Hagbard’s Gallows in context: dating a Bronze Age monument in south-western Sweden
abstract: The Bronze Age monument known as Hagbard’s Gallows in Sweden is a combination of monumental standing stones, rock art and mounds. A new research project uses optically stimulated luminescence and radiocarbon dating techniques to investigate the monument’s chronology.

title: Fast convex model predictive trajectory planning for robot-assisted landings
abstract: Abstract Robot-assisted landings for aircrafts which are able to take off and land vertically offer the capability to speed up and automate landing and turnaround processes and are particularly advantageous for challenging landing conditions such as wind gusts or a moving landing platform. To perform an assisted landing, a precise and robust control approach is required, covering movement synchronization, catching and decelerating. In this paper a novel approach on model predictive trajectory planning for robot-assisted landings of unmanned aerial vehicles is designed, implemented and analyzed

title: (TD)DFT investigation of donor influence on the electronic and photovoltaic properties of D-π-A-π-A quinoxaline dyes
abstract: Abstract Context The design of efficient metal-free organic dyes is crucial for improving the performance of dye-sensitized solar cells (DSSCs). In this work, we investigated the influence of different donor groups on the electronic, photophysical, and photovoltaic properties of two D- π -A- π -A quinoxaline-based dyes, QX-DMA and QX-TPA. Density functional theory (DFT) and time-dependent DFT (TDDFT) calculations with solvation in tetrahydrofuran (THF) were employed to examine structure–property relationships. institutions: Universidade Federal Rural do Rio de Janeiro

title: Repair of Flexurally Cracked Concrete Beams under Sustained Loading via a MICP Diffusion Method
abstract: Most studies on microbially induced calcium carbonate precipitation (MICP) for concrete crack repair focus on unloaded members, while cracks in service are commonly subjected to sustained loading. This study proposes a diffusion-based MICP method for flexurally cracked concrete beams under sustained loading and compares it with a conventional injection method used for unloaded specimens. Five reinforced concrete beams were prepared and evaluated through chloride resistance tests and microstructural analysis.
